title: Odell Beckham Jr. was on the field for three plays on Monday night
summary: The first real sighting of Giants receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Monday night happened when ESPN cameras captured him giving his former head coach, Sean McVay, a post-game hug.
full_text: The first real sighting of Giants receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Monday night happened when ESPN cameras captured him giving his former head coach, Sean McVay, a post-game hug. During the game, OBJ made even less of a cameo appearance. Beckham was on the field for only three snaps. Out of 58 total offensive plays. By way of comparison, Malachi Fields had 47 snaps. Malik Nabers played 43. Darnell Mooney was on the field for 42. Even Braxton Berrios — primarily a special-teamer — had five offensive snaps. Making the lack of involvement from Beckham more surprising is the fact that starting quarterback Jaxson Dart made an early exit with a knee injury. Beckham and backup quarterback Jameis Winston have a strong rapport, and Winston struggled in relief of Dart, completing 11 of 27 throws. Why not give Beckham and Winston a chance to connect? The other question is whether Beckham has frustrations regarding his lack of involvement. Yes, he's apparently happy to simply be back in the NFL after a year out of football. But, with only three snaps in a prime-time game, is he really back? In Week 1, Beckham was on the field for 11 of 69 snaps. He has been targeted zero times, through two games. From the Giants' perspective, it's fair to wonder whether a game-day roster spot is being wasted on someone who isn't contributing to the cause. As MDS points out, the Giants have receiver Dalen Cambre on the practice squad. He was second in the NCAA in special-teams tackles as a senior, and he blocked two punts at the college level. Yes, the Giants bringing Beckham back to Big Blue is a good story. The fans love him. But the early-season trends aren't encouraging. At some point, they're going to need his roster spot. Especially if they don't put Dart on IR and add another quarterback (other than Berrios) to serve as the backup to Winston.
author: Mike Florio

title: Andy Reid: Kenneth Walker wants the ball every play, doesn't want to be relieved
summary: Through two weeks, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker looks like one of the true prizes of free agency.
full_text: Through two weeks, Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker looks like one of the true prizes of free agency. Walker currently leads the league in carries (47), rushing yards (290), touches (56), and yards from scrimmage (369). But that usage rate also comes with some concerns, particularly at that position. Rookie Emmett Johnson has spelled Walker a bit, and he’s been effective with 39 yards rushing and four receptions for 64 yards. His snaps are likely to increase as the year goes on. “Well, I think the way I look at it is … that’s part of the equation, but the other part is allowing Emmett to grow,” head coach Andy Reid said in his Monday video conference, via transcript from the team. “And so, I think Emmett will continue to get more snaps and then it'll take a little bit of load, off Kenny, but he wants that ball. He wants a ball every play, Ken does, and he's not asking to be relieved or anything else. “But I think as it goes on, you get a nice balance with those two in there and then it keeps them even more fresh as the season goes on.” After an overtime victory over the Colts on Sunday night, the Chiefs will face the Dolphins on the road in Week 3. Based on Miami’s results over the past two weeks, this upcoming game could be an opportunity to get Johnson more carries to spell Walker.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cowboys CB Cobie Durant, S P.J. Locke will miss a few weeks with injuries
summary: Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant and safety P.J.
full_text: Cowboys cornerback Cobie Durant and safety P.J. Locke were injured during Sunday's victory over the Commanders. Coach Brian Schottenheimer said both players will miss multiple weeks with their injuries. Durant has a hamstring strain and Locke a torn plantar fascia. It is to be determined whether they will land on injured reserve. Shavon Revel will see more playing time with Durant out. The 2025 third-round pick played 55 defensive snaps and 22 on special teams in the first two games. "Every rep he plays, he gets better," Schottenheimer said of Revel, via Todd Archer of ESPN. Markquese Bell will see more snaps in place of Locke. Bell has played 57 defensive snaps and 26 on special teams this season. The Cowboys played Sunday's game without safety Malik Hooker (forearm) and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring). Their availability for Week 3 remains in question.
author: Charean Williams

title: Todd Monken: Message to team after win is "So what, now what?"
summary: The Browns got their first win of the season in Tampa on Sunday and it was also Todd Monken's first win as an NFL head coach.
full_text: The Browns got their first win of the season in Tampa on Sunday and it was also Todd Monken's first win as an NFL head coach. It has been almost four decades since Monken took his first college coaching job and the path to getting the victory included a lengthy weather delay before the Browns could shut the door on the Buccaneers for good. On Monday, Monken was asked if he ever thought that his first win would play out that way and his answer transitioned from saying it isn't about him to offering a reminder that the goal isn't just to win once. "It’s a players’ game, and we got a lot to clean up, coaching and playing, and we took a giant step from Week 1 to Week 2," Monken said, via a transcript from the team. "So that’ll be the message we come back Wednesday is, ‘So what, now what?’ Are we willing to take that same jump? Or is it now, all of a sudden, we’ve arrived, because it’s week to week. You guys saw the scores, you guys know how this goes, every team’s a different matchup, and we didn’t turn the ball over, which helped us. In that first game we turned it over two of the first four drives, so basically, 'So what, now what?' What are we going to do this week to continue to improve? And we got the right guys to do it, that’s what I love about our group, because they’re going to be ready to go to work on Wednesday." Sustained success has been elusive in Cleveland since the Browns re-entered the league in 1999 and Monken's response underscores how much the team still has to do in order to get where he wants them to be.
author: Josh Alper

title: Aaron Donald: Game wasn't as fast as I thought
summary: Donald played his first game since 2023 on Monday night.
full_text: SoFi Stadium got a jolt of energy before Monday night's game when Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald was the final defensive starter announced to the home crowd. Donald said the response from that crowd "kind of amped me up a little bit" as he ran onto the field for the first time since deciding to end the retirement that started after the 2023 season. Donald did not travel to Australia for the opener and took more time to ramp himself up for his return to game action. The result was three tackles and a tackle for loss while playing 33 of the team's 58 defensive snaps in Monday night's 28-6 win over the Giants. Donald said he would like to win "a little faster" when he's blocked one-on-one and that he feels like everything will feel more natural with a little more playing time under his belt. "The game really wasn't as fast as I thought ," Donald said, via the team's website. "It was more of me calming myself down, overrunning stuff or just my feet not being in the ground how they supposed to be, not trusting my eyes, little stuff like that. But playing the game, when I held out in '17, '18 it was the same way when I came back, it took a couple games to get going. It's a little different. I ain't played in two years, so I gotta watch the film, see what I did good, see what I did wrong, and just clean it up." The plan was for the Rams to team Donald with Myles Garrett, but Garrett's knee injury leaves that on hold for the time being so all involved will hope that the weeks to come find Donald recovering even more of the game that made him a three-time defensive player of the year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Seahawks expect Sam Darnold to practice "in some capacity" Wednesday
summary: Word over the weekend was encouraging about quarterback Sam Darnold's recovery from the glute injury that kept him from playing in Week 2 and head coach Mike Macdonald brought more good news on Monday.
full_text: Word over the weekend was encouraging about quarterback Sam Darnold's recovery from the glute injury that kept him from playing in Week 2 and head coach Mike Macdonald brought more good news on Monday. Macdonald said that Darnold is expected to be on the field when the team returns to practice on Wednesday. "Right now the plan is for him to be out there in some capacity, and we'll go from there," Macdonald said, via the team's website. "How much? We'll see from here to Wednesday what that number is, but right now that's the goal." The answer to the question of how much work Darnold is able to do will be tied to his chances of being cleared to play against the Commanders in Week 3. Drew Lock handled things well in Sunday's rout of the Cardinals, so the 2-0 Seahawks will not have much reason to hurry Darnold back if the best course of action is a slower buildup to game action.
author: Josh Alper

title: Alec Pierce aggravated heel injury, will miss at least several weeks
summary: As the Colts try to turn around a season that has started with two straight losses (and now nine in a row), they'll be missing one of their highest-paid players, for multiple weeks.
full_text: '' As the Colts try to turn around a season that has started with two straight losses (and now nine in a row), they'll be missing one of their highest-paid players, for multiple weeks. Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Pierce aggravated his heel injury during Sunday night's loss to the Chiefs. Pierce had surgery on the heel in the offseason. Pierce will "attempt to rehab" the injury in lieu of surgery. He is expected to miss "several weeks." If all goes well, Rapoport says, Pierce "could return midseason." In the offseason, Pierce signed a four-year contract with a base value of $28.5 million per year — well below the market value of more than $42 million. He caught four passes for 61 yards in a 41-23 loss to the Ravens in Week 1, and one pass for 11 yards against the Chiefs in Week 2. The Colts, at 0-2, are in a three-way tie with the Texans and Titans in the AFC South.
author: Mike Florio

full_text: 1. Seahawks (last week No. 1; 2-0): No Darnold? No problem. 2. Bills (No. 2; 2-0): September wins are celebratory. January wins are mandatory. 3. author: Mike Florio

title: Kyle Shanahan: Mike Evans' hip injury will have to be managed this week
summary: The 49ers have a few injury concerns entering Week 3, including one to veteran receiver Mike Evans.
full_text: The 49ers have a few injury concerns entering Week 3, including one to veteran receiver Mike Evans. Via Nick Wagoner of ESPN, head coach Kyle Shanahan said on Monday that Evans will “ have to be managed this week ” as the wideout deals with a hip injury. Evans exited Sunday’s 35-13 victory over the Dolphins in the second half and did not return. Shanahan noted postgame that the injury didn’t appear to be serious, and if the game had been closer, Evans could have returned. Defensive lineman Romello Height has a broken hand and will need surgery. There’s an outside chance he could be available in Week 3. Receiver Demarcus Robinson and defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. both have suffered high-ankle sprains. Robinson is a candidate for injured reserve, with the idea he could return. But Shanahan also noted that the 49ers will have to be selective about who does and who doesn’t go to IR, because the team is running out of slots for players who can return from the list. Additionally, defensive lineman Mykel Williams will not start practicing this week as he is still on the physically unable to perform list. He is more likely to be back for practice entering Week 4.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Aaron Glenn: No regrets about how we handled end of regulation against Packers
summary: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's late-game decision-making came under fire in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers, but he doesn't feel any differently about his choices after a night to sleep on it.
full_text: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn's late-game decision-making came under fire in Sunday's overtime loss to the Packers, but he doesn't feel any differently about his choices after a night to sleep on it. After the 20-17 loss, Glenn said he never considered calling a timeout when the Packers faced a fourth down near midfield with about a minute left in regulation. The Packers wound up running the clock down and taking a delay of game penalty before trying a Hail Mary on the final snap of the game. On Sunday, Glenn said he didn't want the team's offense to be backed up after a punt and reiterated that on a Monday video conference while expressing no doubt about the course of action he chose for the team. "Between me and our game management guys, our analytical guys, we talk through those situations quite a bit," Glenn said. "That situation actually came up in a number of our conversations. When we have the punter at the logo, we don't want to put ourselves in a situation where we get our guys in a backed up situation. I know we talk about getting our offense going in that situation, but the thing is they had two timeouts also. If you put yourself in a backed up situation and things don't go as planned, I think you’re giving the other team an opportunity to go out there and make a play. I just felt like that was the right decision to do at that point and we actually wanted to play for overtime when it came to that.” Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said on Sunday that he was "really confused" by how Glenn handled the situation, which could be translated to being really thankful that Glenn allowed the Packers to control how the final minute of regulation played out.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jayden Daniels consulting specialists after dislocating left elbow Sunday
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow during Sunday's loss to the Cowboys and is now trying to sort out how long he will be out of action as a result of the injury.
full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow during Sunday's loss to the Cowboys and is now trying to sort out how long he will be out of action as a result of the injury. Daniels went for imaging on the elbow on Monday and head coach Dan Quinn said at a Monday press conference that he will now solicit opinions from specialists about the next courses of action. Daniels suffered the same injury during the 2025 season and missed four games before returning to the lineup. He aggravated the injury in his return and then missed the final four games of the season. It's not clear if the past injuries will play a role in how Daniels and doctors choose to treat Sunday's dislocation. Quinn said on Sunday that his team will "rally around" backup quarterback Marcus Mariota and confirmed on Monday that Mariota will start against the Seahawks in a Week 3 home game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kyler Murray clears concussion protocol, set to start Week 3 vs. Bucs
summary: Murray will be back in the starting lineup for next week's game after Carson Wentz started Week 2.
full_text: Kyler Murray is set to return to the starting lineup. Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell told reporters in his Monday press conference that Murray has cleared concussion protocol and is on schedule to play in the team’s matchup with the Buccaneers. “Kyler has cleared the final phase of the protocol,” O’Connell said. “He’s doing great, he’ll be cleared, and he will start this week against Tampa Bay.” Murray went down early in the Week 1 win over the Packers when he was hit while trying to slide on a scramble. He departed that contest having completed 3-of-5 passes for 18 yards with an interception. Carson Wentz replaced Murray for the last two weeks. He was 11-of-20 for 143 yards in Sunday’s victory over the Bears. O’Connell praised how steady Wentz has been as a backup. In five games last year for the Cardinals, Murray completed 68.3 percent of his throws for 962 yards with six touchdowns and three interceptions. Also on the injury front, O’Connell said Ty Ingram-Dawkins (hip) is day-to-day and Brett Thorson has a hamstring issue.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Sean McVay attributes Week 1 loss to "dumbass coach that makes travel plans"
summary: After the Rams beat the Giants on Monday night, McVay took the blame for the Week 1 debacle in Australia.
full_text: The Rams looked like Super Bowl contenders on Monday night against the Giants, a significant improvement from their Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Australia. Rams coach Sean McVay blamed the Rams' much-discussed travel plans, and himself, for that Week 1 loss. McVay was asked after the win over the Giants why the Rams looked so different than they did in Australia, and McVay said it was primarily about his own decision to arrive in Australia only a day before the game. "Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn and sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that puts you in bad spots," McVay said. The Rams' decision to arrive in Australia only about 24 hours before kickoff was an attempt not to acclimate to the time change at all. The 49ers arrived in Australia a week early and were well acclimated. The 49ers won 27-7, and the Rams' travel schedule has been heavily scrutinized. McVay took the blame for not having his team ready to play in Australia, but they were very ready to play in Los Angeles on Monday night, winning 28-6.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Dan Campbell on Kerby Joseph: We're trying to get him back, but he's not ready
summary: The Lions have struggled in the secondary through the first two weeks of the season and part of the reason why they're having a hard time is the absence of safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph.
full_text: ' The Lions have struggled in the secondary through the first two weeks of the season and part of the reason why they're having a hard time is the absence of safeties Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph. Head coach Dan Campbell said at a Monday press conference that Branch, who is coming off a torn Achilles, is probably closer to returning from the physically unable to perform list than Joseph. Joseph has been dealing with knee problems since early last season and Campbell was asked on 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday what he would say to someone who wonders if Joseph is going to play at all this season. "I wish I could make you feel good ," Campbell said. "I can’t make you feel good. It’s going to come as it comes, and he’s not ready. We’re trying to get him there as fast as we can, and we’re trying to be as smart about it as we can. If he’s ready, when he’s ready, of course we want to play him and get him on the field." The Lions lost another safety when Avonte Maddox went down in Week 2 and they added veteran Jalen Mills to their practice squad on Monday to help bolster their depth. Barring a major change for Joseph, they may remain on the search for help at the back end of the defense all year.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants receiver Malik Nabers suffers apparent arm injury
summary: Nabers exits in considerable pain.
full_text: It's been a bad night for the New York Giants. After losing quarterback Jaxson Dart to a knee injury (he's questionable to return), receiver Malik Nabers has been injured. Nabers left the game after apparently injuring his upper right arm. He tried to make a contested catch while being covered by Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie. Immediately after the play, Nabers put his left hand over the area between his bicep and shoulder. Nabers was in considerable pain. His status will be updated, presumably sooner than later. The Giants trail the Rams, 7-0. Nabers returned to action in Week 1 after suffering a torn ACL in his knee last September. It was uncertain whether he'd play in the opener until pregame warmups. He caught six passes for 69 yards against the Cowboys. He has one catch for one yard against the Rams. UPDATE 9:02 p.m. ET : It's being described as a shoulder injury for Nabers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Rams roll Giants 28-6 after Jaxson Dart's departure
summary: Matthew Stafford threw four touchdown passes, two to Davante Adams, who had 195 yards.
full_text: The Rams are back . . . and so is Aaron Donald. Eleven days after a lackluster performance against the 49ers in Australia, the Rams rebounded with a dominant 28-6 victory over the Giants in Donald's season debut. Both teams are 1-1. The Rams might have won big anyway, but the Giants had no chance after Jaxson Dart injured his left knee on the first drive. The Giants had only 182 yards, and Jameis Winston was 11-of-27 for 111 yards and an interception. The Giants crossed midfield six times, but punted six times, kicked two field goals, threw an interception and once turned it over on downs in their 10 possessions. It was as depressing as their season-opening win over the Cowboys was encouraging. Donald, playing his first game in 981 days after unretiring Aug. 30, made three tackles, including a tackle for loss. The Rams gained 481 yards despite playing without wide receiver Puka Nacua. Davante Adams more than made up for Nacua's absence, catching eight passes for 195 yards and two touchdowns. Matthew Stafford threw touchdown passes of 31 and 11 yards to Adams, 10 yards to running back Kyren Williams and 5 yards to tight end Terrance Ferguson. Stafford was 22-of-31 for 327 yards with an interception to go with the four touchdowns. Williams ran for 85 yards on 12 carries, but he did lose a fumble. Blake Corum had 12 carries for 79 yards. Giants safety Jevon Holland totaled eight tackles, an interception, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery in an elite performance.
author: Charean Williams

title: Michael Penix Jr. will start for Falcons on Thursday night
summary: 2024 first-rounder will return from November 2025 ACL tear.
full_text: The Falcons' quarterback carousel has finally landed on their first-round draft pick from 2024. The team has announced that Michael Penix Jr. will start in Thursday night's game against the Packers at Lambeau Field. Penix suffered a torn ACL in November 2025. He fully participated in practice before both regular-season games, but he was not ready to play. Some would say that, if he's going to be ready to play on Thursday, he could have played on Sunday against the Panthers. Instead, it was Cooper Rush. Rush was removed in the third quarter for undrafted rookie Jack Strand. In combination, they threw three interceptions and generated a passer rating of 28.8. And so it will be Penix time for the 0-2 Falcons, whose next three games are scheduled to be played in prime time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Monday Night Football: Puka Nacua is officially inactive with hip injury
summary: Aaron Donald may be back, but the Rams will not have one of their best offensive players for Monday night's matchup against the Giants.
full_text: Aaron Donald may be back, but the Rams will not have one of their best offensive players for Monday night's matchup against the Giants. Puka Nacua is officially inactive due to his hip injury. Reports had indicated this was the way things were trending for Nacua, who did not practice on Friday or Saturday. Nacua caught five passes for 74 yards in the Rams’ season-opening loss to the 49ers. For the Giants, cornerback Deonte Banks and linebacker Micah McFadden are both inactive after they were listed as questionable. New York’s remaining inactives are tight end Thomas Fidone, offensive lineman J.C. Davis, defensive lineman Bobby Jamison-Travis, defensive lineman Darius Alexander, and safety Jason Pinnock. For the Rams, Nacua, receiver Jordan Whittington, safety Kamren Kinchens, receiver C.J. Daniels, guard Bill Murray, and quarterback Ty Simpson are inactive. Simpson is Los Angeles’ emergency third QB.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Brian Burns says his low ankle sprain is "nothing serious"
summary: Burns limped off the field and to the locker room on Monday night but said after the game he would be OK.
full_text: Giants pass rusher Brian Burns limped off the field in obvious pain on Monday night, but in the locker room after the game, Burns said the medical diagnosis showed that the damage to his ankle wasn't as bad as it felt. Burns said as he sat at his locker that he could feel his ankle getting stiff but the Giants' medical staff had told him it's a low ankle sprain that shouldn't cause him to miss much time. “It eases my mind to know it’s not nothing serious," Burns said. Burns said he's had similar injuries and knows how to rehab them so he can get back on the field quickly. “I’ve dealt with this before,” Burns said. “It all depends on how fast you can get the swelling and inflammation down. I’m going to do everything possible to get as tamed as I can." Burns said he would begin his rehab while on the flight from Los Angeles back to New York. "The recovery process starts now, so it will be ice and compression until we get back to the facility and do more work on it, try to stay off it, keep it elevated," Burns said. "That's all you can do with sprains. I've dealt with it before." Burns is one of the Giants' best defensive players, and on a night when quarterback Jaxson Dart, wide receiver Malik Nabers and left tackle Andrew Thomas all got hurt, a serious injury to Burns was the last thing the Giants needed. Fortunately, he's going to be OK.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jaxson Dart is believed to have a sprained MCL
summary: MRI is coming on Monday.
full_text: The Giants have gotten some good news, for now, regarding quarterback Jaxson Dart's knee injury. Via NFL Network, it's believed that Dart suffered a sprained MCL. The assessment is based on a preliminary exam. X-rays were negative, and an MRI will be conducted on Tuesday. After the game, coach John Harbaugh was asked about the report. "We'll know more tomorrow," Harbaugh said. "That's in the neighborhood of it, I would say. We'll get an MRI tomorrow and have a really good feel for it, and give you more information then." The MCL can heal with rest and rehab, unless the tendon is completely torn. If Dart misses time, Jameis Winston will continue to play in his place. On Monday night, Winston completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception. The Giants host the Titans on Sunday, with the Cardinals next and a visit to the Commanders. So they could find a way to win some games, even if Dart is absent.
author: Mike Florio

title: Ben Johnson: Caleb Williams week-to-week, likely will miss time
summary: While Williams appears to have avoided a major hamstring injury, he is likely to be sidelined.
full_text: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams avoided a major injury, but his hamstring is likely going to need some time to heal. In a radio interview with ESPN 1000 Chicago on Monday, head coach Ben Johnson noted that Williams is likely to be sidelined for a bit. "It sounds like it's going to be a week-to-week deal for him ," Johnson said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. "I've got to still talk with our trainer. We'll do that here shortly and I'll have the lowdown from him. But it sounds like it's week-to-week, but will likely miss some time.” Johnson added that the Bears “potentially” dodged a bullet with Williams’ injury not being more severe. “You know, we’ll see,” Johnson said. “He’s tough and he comes back from these types of things, I think, better than the average human being. So, we’ll see.” Williams was 15-of-26 for 138 yards with an interception before departing Sunday’s loss to the Vikings. He also rushed 42 yards on five carries. Tyson Bagent is Chicago's backup quarterback. The Bears will play the Eagles on Monday night in Week 3.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Matthew Stafford: We leaned on Davante Adams Monday and he came through for us
summary: The Rams didn't have Puka Nacua for Monday night's game against the Giants, but the wide receiver's absence didn't wind up holding them back.
full_text: The Rams didn't have Puka Nacua for Monday night's game against the Giants, but the wide receiver's absence didn't wind up holding them back. Matthew Stafford found the groove that eluded the Rams in Week 1's loss to the 49ers and threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns in a 28-6 win. The first of those scores came late in the first quarter when he found a wide open Davante Adams for a 31-yard score and it would not be the last time Adams found holes in the Giants defense. Adams used a double move to shake off Giants defenders for a 64-yard catch on the next Rams possession and he added his second touchdown catch of the night in the third quarter. The night ended with eight catches for 195 yards that Stafford said the Rams really needed given who wasn't available for the game. "He's an elite player ," Stafford said, via the team's website. "He made all sorts of plays today. [He] made contested catches. He ran great routes and got open. He did it all for us, and he's a guy that can do that. We understand that. We know it. And like I said, leaned on him big time tonight, and he came through for us." The Rams will be hoping to have more hands on deck in Denver next weekend, but Monday was a reminder of how much they bring to the table even when they aren't playing with a full deck.
author: Josh Alper

title: Dan Campbell: Lions don't know what we are yet
summary: Lions coach Dan Campbell says two games into the season is way too soon to know what kind of football team he has.
full_text: Lions coach Dan Campbell says two games into the season is way too soon to know what kind of football team he has. "We don't even know what we are yet, entirely. We don't know what we are," Campbell said. "The 2026 Detroit Lions' offense, defense, special teams, what do we really hang our hat on? We've got an idea on some of our go-to guys, our heavy hitters, but what do we really do well with those guys? And we won't, and I hate saying it, we're not gonna know until probably around the bye [Week 6]. Until we get a good four or five games, and you really start to figure out, this is what we can do and where we can really grow." Campbell said the Lions' 41-31 loss to the Bills on Thursday night doesn't mean they're not a good team that will have a successful season. "As bad as it was, it's not as bad as it appears to be," Campbell said. "And you clean a couple things up, you get guys right, you put guys in the right positions, one guy does what he's supposed to do, that leads to trust the other guy, now we can start cutting it loose and we get our confidence back, and the offense starts playing better, we start converting more, now all of a sudden you begin to get a little bit better, the floor begins to rise on where you're at. I'm not discouraged." Now the Lions prepare for a home game against the Jets — where a loss would drop their record to 1-2 and raise even more questions about what kind of team the Lions are.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Brian Burns, Andrew Thomas injured in fourth quarter
summary: Monday night's game can't end soon enough for the Giants.
full_text: Monday night's game can't end soon enough for the Giants. Not only are they getting blown out by the Rams, but they have had injuries to some of their biggest players. Quarterback Jaxson Dart injured his left knee on the first possession and is standing on the sideline in street clothes. Wide receiver Malik Nabers left briefly with a shoulder injury. Now, pass rusher Brian Burns and left tackle Andrew Thomas are injured. Thomas limped off late in the fourth quarter and Burns followed soon after. Burns' injury looked serious as Rams center Coleman Shelton inadvertently rolled over Burns' left ankle, pinning it to the ground. He needed the assistance of two athletic trainers to get off the field. The Giants did not have an update on Burns or Thomas before the game ended.
author: Charean Williams

title: Report: Jaxson Dart wanted to return to the game despite knee injury
summary: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart left Monday night's game early with a knee injury, and he didn't return.
full_text: '' Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart left Monday night's game early with a knee injury, and he didn't return. It apparently wasn't his choice. Via Jordan Raanan of ESPN, Dart wanted to return to the game . Obviously, the Giants wouldn't allow it. Laura Rutledge of ESPN has added that the Giants eventually took Dart's uniform, preventing a return. She also said his limp is "very minor." The specific diagnosis remains to be seen. Lip readers have spotted an interaction between coach John Harbaugh and a staffer during which Harbaugh possibly is being told Dart will be out 4- 6 weeks. That timeframe could point to an MCL injury. Obviously, however, no one knows for now. And the official diagnosis presumably is coming on Tuesday, after Dart gets an MRI.
author: Mike Florio

title: Davante Adams has 195 yards, two TDs as Rams take 21-3 lead
summary: Davante Adams is having a career day.
full_text: Davante Adams is having a career day. The Rams receiver has eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns. His second touchdown came on an 11-yard pass from Matthew Stafford and increased the Rams' lead to 21-3 over the Giants. Adams' career-high for receiving yards is 206 on 11 catches while playing for the Packers against the Bengals in an overtime game in 2021. It was Adams’ 119th career touchdown, ranking him seventh in NFL history. He is only two touchdown receptions behind Larry Fitzgerald, who is sixth on the list. Stafford passed Philip Rivers for sixth on the all-time passing touchdowns list with his third of the night. He has 426 career passing touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Jaxson Dart ruled out but "going to be OK"
summary: The Giants quarterback hurt his left knee on the team's first possession of Monday Night Football.
full_text: The Giants officially ruled out Jaxson Dart for the second half, but ESPN sideline reporter Laura Rutledge delivered a positive update from General Manager Joe Schoen. The Giants are still evaluating the injury, with Dart getting an X-ray at SoFi Stadium, but Schoen told Rutledge that Dart is "going to be OK." That presumably means Dart did not tear a ligament in his left knee and will return this season. Coach John Harbaugh did not provide any information to Rutledge about Dart's injury in a halftime interview. Dart was hurt on the Giants' first possession on a third-down play when Rams defenders Josaiah Stewart and Byron Young pressured him. Young hit Dart high, pushing him into Stewart, and, with Dart airborne, his left knee jammed into Stewart’s quad. Dart remained on the turf with 11:20 left in the first quarter. He went 3-for-5 for 20 yards before leaving. Jameis Winston has replaced Dart and is 5-of-13 for 71 yards and an interception.
author: Charean Williams

title: Monday Night Football: Matthew Stafford, Davante Adams have Rams up 14-3 at halftime
summary: The Rams are playing without wide receiver Puka Nacua and pass rusher Myles Garrett.
full_text: '' The Rams are playing without wide receiver Puka Nacua and pass rusher Myles Garrett. They haven't missed them so far tonight, with the Giants having lost quarterback Jaxson Dart on the first possession. Stafford has thrown for 184 yards and two touchdowns, with Davante Adams catching five for 145 and a touchdown. The Rams lead 14-3. Rams defensive lineman Aaron Donald has three tackles, including one for loss, in his first game action in 981 days. Donald retired after the 2023 season but officially unretired Aug. 30. Adams, 31, has not had a better game since Dec. 15, 2024, against the Jaguars when he caught nine passes for 198 yards and two touchdowns. Stafford has completed 11 of 15 passes and has thrown a pick. His touchdowns covered 31 yards to Adams and 10 yards to running back Kyren Williams. The Rams should have had three more points to end the half, but kicker Harrison Mevis missed a 43-yard try wide left on the final play of the half. Giants safety Jevon Holland has done everything he can to keep his team in it. Holland, who had an interception of Dak Prescott last week, has an interception, a forced fumble and a recovered fumble. At the end of a 5-yard Kyren Williams run late in the first half, Holland punched the ball out and recovered it at the Los Angeles 11. It was Williams' eighth career fumble. The Giants had six possessions in the first half and four times crossed midfield with drives to the Los Angeles 43, 43, 18 and 3 without a touchdown. After Holland's fumble recovery, the Giants settled for Dominic Zvada's chip-shot, 24-yard field goal with 25 seconds left in the half. Dart went 3-of-5 for 20 yards before injuring his left knee. Jameis Winston replaced him and was 4-of-12 for 58 yards and an interception, a throw straight to Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie in the end zone. Cam Skattebo has only 18 yards on seven carries.
author: Charean Williams

title: Long-time Bills radio voice John Murphy believes he lost credential over criticism of Joe Brady
summary: In an age of sports media that features plenty of reporters and analysts who are on the payroll, directly or indirectly, of the teams and/or leagues they cover, some teams and leagues feel emboldened to take action against those who dare to cover them with scrutiny or criticism.
full_text: In an age of sports media that features plenty of reporters and analysts who are on the payroll, directly or indirectly, of the teams and/or leagues they cover, some teams and leagues feel emboldened to take action against those who dare to cover them with scrutiny or criticism. Long-time Bills radio voice John Murphy lost his press-box credential after writing a column regarding new coach Joe Brady for WIVB-TV, which is the official TV station of the team. Via Alan Pergament of the Buffalo News , Murphy received a text from WIVB sports director Josh Reed two days after the column was posted that Murphy wouldn’t have a seat in the press box at the team's new stadium. Said Murphy regarding whether he believed the denial was a result of his column, “I think so, but I don’t know.” The denial was attributed to a policy against part-time workers getting credentials. The Bills declined a request for comment from Pergament. Murphy claims that Bills V.P. of marketing Chris Jenkins told Murphy he'd receive a credential for the season, and that Murphy was shown the seat he'd be using. Murphy also said that his subsequent column predicting a 10-win season for the Bills wasn't posted by WIVB, after the station said it couldn't be published due to pressure from the Bills. Murphy spent 34 years as an analyst and a radio voice for the Bills. He retired in 2023 after suffering a stroke. “I feel pretty bad,” Murphy told Pergament. “[WIVB] didn’t fight for me. [The column] wasn’t that bad.” It's not currently clear, and never may be known with certainty, whether the Bills retaliated against Murphy. Typically, such motivation isn't worn on the sleeve of the entity doing the retaliation. If that's what's happening, it would be sad. And it possibly would be a manifestation of the extreme pressure the organization is feeling to justify the decision to fire coach Sean McDermott while promoting Brady and G.M. Brandon Beane.
author: Mike Florio

title: Matthew Stafford moves into tie for sixth on all-time TDs list as Rams take 14-0 lead
summary: Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford moved into a tie for sixth on the NFL's all-time passing touchdowns list on Monday night.
full_text: '' Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford moved into a tie for sixth on the NFL's all-time passing touchdowns list on Monday night. He tied Philip Rivers with his second touchdown of the night. Stafford's 10-yard scoring toss to running back Kyren Williams was the 425th of Stafford's career and gave the Rams a 14-0 lead with 11:07 left before halftime. Brett Favre is fifth on the all-time list with 508, and Tom Brady is the leader with 649. Stafford threw a 31-yard touchdown pass to Davante Adams in the first quarter. He nearly had a second touchdown to Adams, completing a 64-yard pass to Adams before safety Jevon Holland pulled down Adams at the Giants 14. Adams has four catches for 118 yards and a touchdown. Stafford is 10-of-12 for 157 yards and two touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Lessons learned from Week 2: Vikings, Packers have breakout stars; Bengals have NFL's most-improved unit
summary: Lukas Van Ness and Dallas Turner are wreaking havoc on opposing offenses
full_text:
In the NFL , we can become so focused on what's new -- new players, new coaches, new coordinators, new philosophies -- that we overlook what's already in place.
And we can forget that what's in place can change. Players who start slow aren't doomed to be busts. Sam Darnold won a Super Bowl after playing for five different teams in his first eight seasons. Coaches who start slow aren't doomed to get fired and never get another job. Bill Belichick went 36-44 in five years with the Browns and had to work his way back up the ladder before becoming one of the greatest coaches of all time. The NFL can be harsh, but there are, more often than not, opportunities for growth.
We're seeing it on display as two former first-round picks step up when their teams absolutely need it most, a reminder that patience is a virtue. That and more to start our six lessons from Week 2:
The dominant talking points surrounding the Vikings ' and Packers ' pass rushes entering this season were about who wasn't playing. The Vikings traded Jonathan Greenard to the Eagles , and Micah Parsons is still out as he recovers from a torn ACL.
Enter Dallas Turner and Lukas Van Ness , both of whom have been excellent this season and were especially terrific Sunday.
We'll start with Turner, who has 20(!!!) pressures already. That is not just the most in the NFL this season, but the most through two games in the Pro Football Focus database (since 2006). He also has 11 quarterback hits and three sacks, including, fittingly, this one to seal Sunday's win over the Bears . (Note to offensive coordinators: Don't have a tight end block this man.)
DALLAS TURNER WALKOFF SACK FOR THE VIKINGS pic.twitter.com/8wGRHUIMKW
His Week 1 tape was a ton of fun, with the size, speed and power all on display.
Dallas Turner Week 1 tape vs Green Bay pic.twitter.com/gA7mjLoaBQ
Is Brian Flores doing a great job scheming advantageous situations for Turner? Yes. Is Flores a defensive mastermind overall? Yes. But someone has to actually make the plays on the field, and Turner is absolutely doing that.
After a quiet rookie year and slow start to his second year, Turner had 6.5 sacks and a 16.2% pressure rate from Week 10 onward last year. It went under the radar because the Vikings had such dire quarterback issues, but the signs were there. He's only 23 years old. What a fun player.
Van Ness, meanwhile, had flashed before, too. He dealt with a foot injury for much of 2025, but had a 16.3% pressure rate on the season overall. There's been another clear step so far in 2026: 2.5 sacks and a 19.6% pressure rate. Sunday was his finest outing yet: 1.5 sacks, nine tackles, four quarterback hits, three tackles for loss. He was everywhere, including a fourth-down stop that may have saved the game for Green Bay.
Blink and you'll miss Lukas Van Ness with the huge fourth-down stop (and also Jonathan Ford creating carnage). pic.twitter.com/iF3xBTKI2x
If Van Ness has finally unlocked all the potential his athleticism holds, that is a crucial boost. And once Parsons returns, the Packers could have a really dangerous duo.
Want to see why the Bengals sent the 10th pick to the Giants for Dexter Lawrence , paid Boye Mafe a lot of money and signed Jonathan Allen despite a tough year in Minnesota? Turn on the film from Cincinnati's 20-6 Week 2 win over the Texans . Cincinnati sacked C.J. Stroud four times and pressured him 28 times on his 60 dropbacks. That's not just an absurd rate (47%) but their most pressures in any game since 2019 -- before Joe Burrow was even on the team!
The Bengals made these big moves with Burrow in mind. Isn't it nice that the offense doesn't have to put up 30+ points every week -- and put Burrow in harm's way by having him drop back over and over again -- to win? Scoring 20 and winning going away is an encouraging sign.
Oh, did I mention the Bengals allowed just 3.3 yards per carry? In fact, it might have been even more impressive than the pass rush. Watch Lawrence singlehandedly destroy this fourth-and-inches.
Wake up babe a new angle of the Dexter Lawrence 4th down run stop just dropped pic.twitter.com/jeLg0IXhwB
Here's a good example of what this new-look defensive line can do against the pass: On this third and 11, the Texans have four blockers to deal with just two: Mafe and Lawrence. But Mafe splits the right tackle and right guard, forcing Stroud off his spot, and Lawrence is right there, having run by the center and left guard. Stroud commits intentional grounding.
Texans use four guys to block just two ... and still lose immediately. pic.twitter.com/FbInNR1TwR
Mafe has an 18.8% pressure rate through two games. Cedric Johnson , a 2024 sixth-rounder, has already tied his career high with two sacks. The impact of the top-end talent additions spreads throughout the entire unit. On one play, three offensive linemen (RT, RG, C) focused on Lawrence, the LG took on Allen, and the LT took on Mafe, giving linebacker Demetrius Knight Jr . a free shot on Stroud.
Yes, it was the Texans sans Nico Collins . But this defensive front is really disruptive; it was also excellent in Week 1 against a good Buccaneers line. It completely changes how Cincinnati can play, and it's allowing Al Golden -- who felt a lot of heat last year -- to dial up all sorts of pressure looks.
Jaylen Waddle's Broncos debut was stunningly underwhelming: one catch for 2 yards on three targets as the Broncos got crushed by the Chiefs .
Week 2 was much, much better: eight catches (on 10 targets) for 138 yards. It's not just the numbers, but the way they occurred. Waddle had two big catches on routes over the middle, where his speed got him behind the linebackers just in time for Bo Nix to deliver. He had a 49-yarder on a deep ball. On a third-and-2, he turned a short out route into a big gain by breaking a tackle, and on a crucial third and 3 late, he roasted Jourdan Lewis on a double move.
Jaylen Waddle showed out in his first home game with Denver 8 REC, 138 YDS, 17.3 AVG on 10 TGT vs. Jacksonville After a quiet Broncos debut, Waddle helped Denver erase a 10 point deficit and grab its first win. https://t.co/qmZR0HioXM pic.twitter.com/DxVPCl9Mi1
Waddle had five catches as the left outside wide receiver, two catches as the left slot and one catch as the right slot. He lined up all over the field, including twice in the backfield (Denver had 21 rushing yards on those two plays). Sean Payton's words afterward showed the Broncos learned their lesson after the opener.
"It was significant," Payton said. "I just gave him a game ball. You can see the explosiveness, the run after the catch, all of those things. I'm glad he's ours."
There were two overtime games on Sunday, with the Packers beating the Jets 20-17 and the Chiefs beating the Colts 33-30. Not only were both really fun finishes, but they were examples of why the new overtime rules are so much better than the old ones.
The Jets opted to take the ball first against the Packers, a decision that goes against the norm, but Aaron Glenn had his reasons.
"Usually, if you can get yourself in a situation like that and you can really control the clock, you can control exactly how they're going to play offense once you go and score. So, we control the clock, we go run it down; say we run it seven minutes, which we've done before, we've run a number of times off the clock, it only gives them so much time to try to rebut."
Unfortunately, Geno Smith took sacks on first and second down, the Jets punted, and Trey Smack made a short field goal. Game over.
On "SNF," the Colts opted to defer. The Chiefs scored a field goal. The Colts drove down the field and faced the issue that can make being second in the field-goal sequence difficult: fourth-and-8 in field-goal territory. If they went for it and failed, the game would be over. But if they kicked, they'd give the ball back to Patrick Mahomes and a Chiefs offense that had been playing well. The Colts kicked a field goal (that's a different discussion, and I…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: 2026 NFL Week 3 injury panic meter: Jaxson Dart, Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels go down in losses
summary: Projecting the outlook for some of the league's biggest Week 2 injuries
full_text:
Another week of NFL football means another laundry list of injuries. Week 2 saw some of the league's most intriguing young quarterbacks -- Jaxson Dart , Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels -- all go down with injuries that knocked them out of their respective games.
A litany of other high-impact, non-quarterback also suffered key setbacks and will be sidelined for multiple weeks after being injured on Sunday and Monday. Which players will aim to return in Week 3? Which ones will be out for a minimum of a month after going on injured reserve? Who could miss just a week or two?
Here, we've rounded up the top early-season injuries from around the NFL, and we'll be assessing each situation with a panic meter as spelled out below:
The New York Giants entered "Monday Night Football" in Week 2 with all the hope in the world after their 28-20 Week 1 upset of the Dallas Cowboys on "Sunday Night Football." All that optimism came to a screeching halt on the game's opening drive when quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury that caused him to limp off the field. New York ruled him out of the game at halftime.
Postgame, ESPN reported that it's believed that Dart has a sprained MCL going off of initial testing.
Jaxson Dart went down in pain and was clutching at his left knee after this play. He was able to walk off the field on his own. pic.twitter.com/gDH8gCrkPA
However, Giants general manager Joe Schoen told ESPN sideline reporter Laura Rutledge that Dart is "going to be OK." That's certainly an interesting shift from the internet's attempt to read the lips of the Giants' trainer telling head coach John Harbaugh Dart will be out "four to six weeks." The 23-year-old quarterback was healthy enough to walk around on the sidelines in street clothes in the second half.
He's out 4-6 weeks .. read his lips pic.twitter.com/t54zRrvOrp
Dart missing potentially a month, could be disatrous for the Giants. Backup Jameis Winston is a fun personality, but he's more known for that these days than his ability to be a winning starting quarterback in the NFL. His 111 yards and an interception on 11 of 27 passing wasn't exactly the definition of an inspired performance. Fortunately for New York, its schedule remains soft the next three weeks with games at home against the Tennessee Titans (0-2) and Arizona Cardinals (1-1) before playing at the Washington Commanders (0-2) in Week 5.
The schedule stiffens up starting in Week 6 with games against the New Orleans Saints (1-1), at the Houston Texans (0-2) in Week 7 and then the Philadelphia Eagles on the road in Week 9 after the Giants' Week 8 bye.
It appeared as though the Chicago Bears ' 2026 season (1-1) was over after quarterback Caleb Williams was carted off in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings with a lower leg injury. It turns out the hamstring injury isn't significant. Chicago coach Ben Johnson told ESPN Chicago that Williams  "will likely miss some time" and called him "week-to-week." That's a major relief for the Bears.
If Williams can suit up against the 2-0 Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football" in Week 3, that's obviously the best-case scenario. However, him just missing a week before returning in the Bears' home game against the New York Jets in Week 4 could allow for him to have enough time to get back to full strength before suiting up again.
Another year, another injury for 2024 NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year quarterback Jayden Daniels. The Washington Commanders' signal-caller dislocated his left elbow on the final play of the first half of the team's 37-20 Week 2 defeat at the Dallas Cowboys. It's the same injury he suffered last year that caused him to miss seven games. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said there isn't a timetable for Daniels' return and that Marcus Mariota will start in Week 3 against the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks (2-0).
At 0-2 and it being unknown when Daniels could return, it's time to panic in Washington. The Commanders likely fall to 0-3 and then have games against the Indianapolis Colts (0-2), New York Giants (1-1) and at the San Francisco 49ers (2-0) before a Week 7 bye. It could get dark in a hurry in the nation's capital.
Los Angeles two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Puka Nacua popped up on the injury report with a hip and groin injury, and he ended up being inactive in the Giants' 28-6 victory on "Monday Night Football." Coach Sean McVay told reporters it's a "separate issue" from another lower body injury he dealt with in the preseason, so there's some hope this could just be a week-to-week injury. Plus, three-time, first team All-Pro wide receiver Davante Adams has enough gas left in the tank to carry the passing game for a little while without Nacua. He soared for 195 yards receiving and two receiving touchdowns while catching eight of his 10 targets.
Coach John Harbaugh told reporters postgame that three-time Pro Bowl edge rusher Brian Burns suffered a low ankle sprain in the team's loss at the Rams Monday night. ESPN observed Burns wearing a boot on his left ankle and riding a golf cart back to the team's bus.
Burns himself doesn't seem concerned that this injury will be a long-term issue. The Giants are also as equipped as any team to lose the player who racked up 16.5 sacks in 2025, the second-most in the league. They have two ex-top-five-pick edge rushers in Kayvon Thibodeaux and Abdul Carter in addition to a softer schedule across the next three weeks. However, it's unclear how long this injury will linger with one of the Giants' top players.
"It's just getting stiff," Burns said postgame, via SNY , when asked if the ankle feels better with him sitting back in the locker room. "It eased my mind to know it isn't anything serious. That's all. ... Yeah, I've dealt with this. It just depends how fast you can get the swelling and inflammation out. I'm going to do everything possible to get it as tamed as I can. .. The recovery process starts now."
Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce , who led the NFL in yards per reception in both 2024 (22.3) and 2025 (21.3), won't be seen on the football field anytime soon. He aggravated the heel injury he had surgically repaired this offseason, and ESPN reports his goal is to fix the issue through physical therapy instead of having surgery during the season. He'll be sidelined for a number of weeks with the goal being a return midseason in roughly six to seven weeks.
That's a massive blow to the Colts' offense with Josh Downs really being the only true field-stretching wide receiver Indianapolis has with Pierce unavailable. On Monday evening, the Colts signed longtime Daniel Jones target Darius Slayton , per The Ringer . It's getting desperate early for the 0-2 Colts.
Seahawks' leading rusher Jadarian Price , the team's 2026 first-round pick, departed their 31-7 road win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 2 with what was announced as a chest injury but later revealed to be a shoulder injury. Per ESPN , coach Mike Macdonald made it clear he's not concerned about it saying, "It's intact and nothing serious, seems like."
Green Bay may have lost their best offensive lineman for the rest of the 2026 NFL season. Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele was carted off on the fourth play from scrimmage in the Packers ' 20-17 overtime win at the New York Jets. Coach Matt LaFleur didn't sound encouraged about the chances of seeing him again this season.
"That doesn't look good," LaFleur said, via The Packers Wire . "That could be a season-ender potentially."
This is a massive blow because they simply aren't the same team without Bako-Bewele. Many people pin the Packers' five-game losing streak to end the 2025 season on losing All-Pro edge rusher Micah Parsons in Week 15 at the Denver Broncos , but that was also the last game of the year that Bako-Bewele played as well that season. LaFleur will be tasked with shuffling the deck chairs up front along the offensive line with the team likely relying on 2025 second-round pick offensive lineman…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Rams' Aaron Donald makes impact in his first game in almost three years
summary: Donald's presence made the Rams a more formidable defense on Monday night
full_text:
The gold standard for an athlete's first game following an extended retirement is Mario Lemieux's one-goal, two-assist performance 3.5 years after he last played professional hockey. Michael Jordan authored another notable comeback debut when he scored 19 points following his first retirement.
Aaron Donald's performance on Monday night falls somewhere between Lemieux and Jordan. It wasn't as memorable as Lemieux's but was better than Jordan's as Donald contributed to a Rams win (Jordan's Bulls fell to the Pacers).
Donald, playing in his first game in almost three years, showed flashes of the form that made him a three-time Defensive Player of the Year.
Donald played 32 snaps: 18 pass-rush snaps and 14 run snaps. He had a 0.75-second get-off on his pass-rush snaps, the third-fastest game this season for a defensive tackle ( via ESPN ). Donald was credited with one pressure, which is significant as he has never gone a game without having at least one.
On his run snaps, Donald had three tackles that included a tackle for loss. He was able to get those tackles despite being double-teamed on several instances.
Donald's biggest play occurred late in the first half, when he knifed through the line and brought Najee Harris down for a 3-yard loss on third-and-2 from the Rams' 3-yard line.
Aaron Donald with the stop on 3rd & 2 💪 @NYGvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/pcR865miwx
Donald's impact on the game goes beyond stats, although he was impressive from that standpoint as well.
As expected, the Rams used the 35-year-old Donald in stints, a byproduct of his layoff. Donald was used less, but -- based on the metrics -- he was able to give the Rams quality snaps whenever he was on the field. He was able to fire off the ball with his trademark quickness.
Donald, like all the great athletes do, made life easier for his teammates. He took on and attracted extra attention from the Giants , which led to more opportunities for his teammates to make plays.
More so, Donald's sheer presence created issues for the Giants, who had to account for him every time he stepped onto the field. Donald compounded that issue by lining up on opposite side of the line of scrimmage.
While it is reasonable to expect that Donald's usage and production will increase as the season progresses, his output and impact during Monday night's game is why the Rams wanted him to come out of retirement. Sure, Sean McVay would obviously love if Donald had a vintage two- or three-sack performance at some point. But if nothing else, Donald can routinely do what he did on Monday night, which is making an impact in multiple ways while creating more issues for the opposing offense.
"Today, the defense played how we were supposed to play," Donald said afterward . "Always got room for improvement, right? So it was a good start, good win. Enjoyed the day, and we're going back to work tomorrow."
Donald received a high grade for his first game back after a three-year hiatus. A sack/a few more splash plays would have given him an "A," but his stuff of Harris near the goal line -- in addition to his overall impact on the Rams' defense -- sealed his "A-" grade.

title: Sean McVay rips himself for Rams' Week 1 Australia travel plans: 'Sometimes you have a dumbass coach'
summary: McVay's team bounced back in a big way on Monday night
full_text:
Rams coach Sean McVay has emphatically -- and humorously -- taken accountability for his team's lackluster performance during its season-opening loss in Australia.
McVay's travel plans for that game -- arriving in Australia just 28 hours prior to kickoff -- backfired as Los Angeles was thoroughly outplayed by the 49ers , who rolled to a 27-7 win. McVay called himself out for that decision following Monday night's win over the Giants .
"Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn and sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that puts you in bad spot," he said.
"Sometimes you win, sometimes you learn and sometimes you have a dumbass coach that makes travel plans that puts you in bad spot." Sean McVay on the difference with the Rams between Week 1 and Week 2. pic.twitter.com/RjfnnGLuJn
During Monday night's game, ESPN broadcasters shared that McVay told them that he and his team simply had no energy during the loss to the 49ers, which was likely the byproduct of the travel schedule. In the immediate aftermath of the loss, however, McVay was hesitant to put too much blame on the travel while crediting the 49ers for their performance.
"I don't believe that's why we didn't play well enough," he said . "I really don't. I'm more than comfortable with that. I'll always make decisions that I think are best for the football team. It's easy in hindsight to be able to say it was a miss. But those are responsibilities that I'll take and then you try to be able to look at it. I'll always look at myself inside out and figure out where I can improve."
Regardless of why, McVay has obviously had a change of heart as it relates to the reasons behind his team's struggles in Week 1. On Monday night, however, the Rams looked much more like the team that was a popular preseason pick to win the Super Bowl .
The 28-6 win was highlighted by Matthew Stafford's four-touchdown performance, Davante Adams torching the Giants' defense to the tune of 195 yards and two touchdowns on eight receptions, and a defense that welcomed back the return of Aaron Donald , who made three tackles (including a tackle for loss) in his first game in nearly three years.
"Obviously we're happy about it," Adams said afterward . "We're thrilled to win, and any win in this league is one to celebrate. But when you look back, it's you're trying to be great and be a be a Super Bowl caliber team. You got to hold yourself to a high standard, and I think we can do a little bit better than we did."

title: NFL Week 3 picks and score predictions: Two undefeated teams go down, Broncos edge Rams in thriller
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
I don't usually want to write any team off after watching it play just two games, but guys, I'll be honest, I don't think the Dolphins are going to make the playoffs this year, and now that I'm looking at their schedule, I'm not sure they're even going to win a game.
I know we're only two weeks through the season, but I'm starting the 0-17 watch now.
If you're wondering how bad the Dolphins have been this year, just consider this: They're the only team that has yet to hold a lead in a game. Forget winning, they haven't even HELD A LEAD. We are heading into Week 3 and they have not been in the lead for even a single second this season. If you can't hold a lead, you can't win. That's how you end up 0-17.
That's a rough stat for Dolphins fan, but if you're a Falcons fan or a Chargers fan, you can't laugh, because your team might be worse.
The Falcons haven't run a single play in the red zone this year. I don't know if they're doing red zone work in practice, but if they are, they can just skip over that this week and work on something else. It's almost impossible to go the first two weeks of the season without getting into the red zone a single time. As a matter of fact, the Falcons are the first team in 18 years to make it through the first two weeks without running a red zone play.
And then there's the Chargers.
The Chargers are the second team in NFL history to lose back-to-back games by double digits with both coming at home against teams that had a sub-.200 win pct the previous season. The other was the 1926 Racine Tornadoes (Oct. 10-17), who played just one more game before folding.
The Chargers have literally set football back 100 years. My takeaway from that stat is that the Chargers are essentially one game away from folding their franchise, and to be honest, that might be for the best.
So did I pick against the Chargers, Falcons and Dolphins this week? Let's get to the Week 3 picks and find out.
Actually, before we get to the picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here . I get 1.7 cents every time someone clicks through on that link, so make sure to click early and often. But I also get docked 1.7 cents every time I get a pick wrong, so it all evens out.
Let's see how much I'm going to lose this week.
Somehow, a game between two WINLESS teams might be my favorite game on the schedule this week. Actually, now that I'm looking at the entire Week 3 schedule, this is probably closer to my fourth favorite game, but that's still pretty high for a matchup involving two 0-2 teams.
There's a good chance that the Colts and Texans are both actually good, but we just don't know it yet, because the NFL scheduling department threw them under a bus to start the season.
Out of these two teams, I'm probably more worried about the Colts. This team hasn't won a game since Nov. 9. They lost Alec Pierce to an injury in Week 2 and he won't be able to play this week, so that means the Colts' passing game will be taking a hit. This feels like a week where Jonathan Taylor is going to be getting a lot of work, but I'm not sure that's a good thing with the Colts about to face one of the best defenses in the NFL.
Not only does Houston have what should end up being a top defense, but this year, the Texans have the offense to go with it. I know, that seems like a crazy thing to say with the Texans coming off a game where they scored just SIX POINTS, but they shot themselves in the foot against the Bengals . They had a missed field goal, a separate botched field goal snap and a failed fourth-and-inches in Bengals territory. If one or all of those things go their way, it's a different game.
Although they struggled to score, they did just fine in Week 1 by putting up 31 points against the Bills . I'm starting to think the C.J. Stroud found a time machine and went back and kidnapped the 2023 version of himself, because that's what he's looked like this year. He's thrown for 627 yards through two weeks, which is the second-highest number in the NFL, and a big reason that's happened is because he's been playing smart football. The Texans likely won't have Nico Collins this week, but Stroud didn't have him in Week 2 and he still managed to throw for 353 yards.
This is the third time in the past four seasons that the Texans have started 0-2 and on the previous two occasions (2023, 2025), they made the playoffs. I'm starting to think they're going 0-2 on purpose.
PICK: Texans 27-24 over Colts
My favorite game to play every week is to try and guess who the Vikings ' starting quarterback is going to be.
The NFL is a quarterback-driven league, except in Minnesota. If the Vikings have proven one thing over the past 12 months, it's that they can win games no matter who's under center. As a matter of fact, with their win over the Bears in Week 2, they became the first team in NFL HISTORY to win four straight games with four different starting quarterbacks.
2025 -- Week 17 starting QB: Max Brosmer 2025 -- Week 18: J.J. McCarthy 2026 -- Week 1: Kyler Murray 2026 -- Week 2: Carson Wentz
At this point, they should just start someone new every week. I think Jimmy Garoppolo is available in free agency. Call him.
Actually, the Vikings don't need to call anyone and that's because Kyler Murray will be returning to the field on Sunday after playing just three possessions in Week 1.
Whether it's Murray, Wentz or anyone else, it almost doesn't matter who the Vikings have at QB because their defense is so dominant. This is a team that will happily win games 9-3, just like it did on Sunday.
The Vikings' defense is one of the best in the NFL: The unit is fun to watch and I'm not just saying that because one of their players celebrated a turnover in Week 2 by doing the "Hot Dog" dance.
I thought I recognized this dance 😂😂 @rodgers_isaiah | @Vikings pic.twitter.com/VOlNzijGV1
If you have a kid under five, the Vikings are now their favorite team just because of that celebration.
I trust the Vikings' defense more than almost any other defense in the NFL right now, but I think their offense is going to struggle in Tampa Bay. At 0-2, the Buccaneers ' season is essentially on the line: Over the past 30 years, no NFC team has started 0-3 and rebounded to make the playoffs. It's put up or shut up time in Tampa and if the Bucs don't win this game, they might start looking to see if there's any fine print in Baker Mayfield's contract to see if they can get a refund on his extension. I don't think NFL contracts work like that, but it doesn't hurt to check.
I think the desperate Bucs somehow find a way to pull off the upset here.
PICK: Buccaneers 19-16 over Vikings
For the first time ever, the NFL is playing a game in Rio De Janeiro and the best part about that is the fact that I now get to remind you about the time I played an extra in a movie that took place in Rio De Janeiro. I was a train passenger in "Fast Five" and my train in the movie was headed to Rio, but I'm not actually sure if it made it, because the train got blown up by Paul Walker and Vin Diesel.
I've seen every Fast and the Furious movie and as someone who played a key role in Fast Five, I can personally attest to the fact that it's the best one in the series https://t.co/4lQNomUGjL pic.twitter.com/BBopsqGeO1
After my performance, most people thought I was going to be the next George Clooney, but I decided to pursue the much more glamorous life of being an NFL writer. And this game is where that decision is finally going to pay off big time, because I'm definitely the only NFL Media member who has ridden a fictional train to Rio, which basically makes me the only expert you can trust on an NFL game being played there. And let's not forget, this game is on CBS. It's like my entire professional life has come full circle.
