title: Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels injured in Week 2: What's the outlook for Bears, Commanders signal callers?
summary: Williams hurt his hamstring on a run; Daniels dislocated his elbow after an awkward fall
full_text:
Caleb Williams and Jayden Daniels will forever be intertwined as the No. 1 and No. 2 picks, respectively, in the quarterback-loaded 2024 NFL Draft . But right now they're unfortunately tied together by a different bond: Both young stars suffered injuries in Week 2, with Williams hurting his hamstring on a non-contact play and Daniels dislocating his left elbow while trying to brace his fall after getting stepped on by an offensive lineman.
For Williams, it's his first significant NFL injury; he has started all 38 games (including playoffs) since being drafted by Chicago. For Daniels, it's the fourth significant injury he has suffered since the start of last season and his second left elbow dislocation in the last 11 months.
Both players will be out for at least some time, though further testing -- beginning Monday -- and their responses will provide a clearer timeline. Johnson described Williams as "week to week" on ESPN Chicago mid-day Monday; Quinn will provide his update later in the day.
Playing on a rain-soaked field, Williams took a bootleg dropback and outraced Andrew Van Ginkel to the edge. But in doing so, he pulled his right hamstring and quickly went down in pain. He needed help getting to the sideline and was then carted off the field.
Caleb Williams - Took a long stride to avoid the tackle and went down non-contact. Not seeing too much at the knee. This one could just be a hamstring injury but I’ll keep analyzing it. pic.twitter.com/rGwh2a1xmD
Caleb Williams had to be helped off the field after that last play. 📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/ecsgk7fwdi
The non-contact aspect was initially the most worrying part, but he and the Bears appear to have very much avoided the worst-case scenario.
You could kind of see in real time," coach Ben Johnson said. "I'm actually happy it's nothing with the knee; that was my first inclination. But yeah, the hamstring could be pretty damaging as well. So, we'll see how bad it is tomorrow and we'll go from there."
Daniels, meanwhile, suffered a dislocation of his left elbow in a very similar manner to the way he suffered his first one last year. This time, he got stepped on by left guard Chris Paul and, trying to brace is unnatural fall, put his left arm on the ground. Viewer discretion is advised below.
#JaydenDaniels @Commanders By video, clear left elbow dislocation Similar to last season Joint comes out easier 2nd time Original ligament tear heals "looser" Will be ruled OUT 2nd half #WASvsDAL pic.twitter.com/777bekF7pC
Daniels stayed down for several minutes before being carted off with a towel draped over his head and face. Coach Dan Quinn said X-rays showed no fracture and that Daniels would fly home with the team and undergo further testing on Monday.
Several reporters noted Williams (who did not meet with the media postgame) walked through the locker room without crutches and perhaps a slight limp . That's obviously better than "on crutches" or "with a significant limp," but hamstrings can be tricky.
Based on the prognosis Johnson shared Monday -- "week to week" -- it seems like Williams' injury falls in line with a Grade 1 strain. Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix Sports reported the team hasn't yet ruled him out for Week 3 on "Monday Night Football" against the Eagles, but that seems to be an aggressive timeline given Johnson's words.
Per the Princeton Sports & Family Medicine website , for a Grade 1 strain ...
Williams very much fits the high-speed athlete description, though. He is a mobile quarterback whose movement skills are paramount to everything he does. Johnson uses a variety of dropbacks, including from under center and rollouts like the one Williams got hurt on. If it is indeed a Grade 1 strain, Williams would likely miss at least one game, but perhaps more if the Bears opt for caution. And there's reason to opt for caution, as hamstring injuries can linger or be re-aggravated.
Williams did hurt the same hamstring in 2022. There's been so much time between the two injuries that no connection can be drawn, but it's at least a nugget worth noting.
Last year, coincidentally, Daniels missed one game with a hamstring strain. If it is indeed a Grade 1 strain, Williams is likely looking at a game or two missed, but again, there are several factors at play.
A Grade 2 strain would cause more time to be missed. In 2016, wide receiver A.J. Green suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain in Week 11 and did not play the rest of the season (though he had initially planned to return after a few weeks). In 2011, Patrick Willis suffered a Grade 2 hamstring strain and missed three games, which would represent the earlier side of the return timeline.
Daniels was out for three weeks last year after suffering his first left elbow dislocation , though three things are to be considered here:
Daniels could again go the route of wearing a brace, though as the second bullet point shows, landing on the elbow again would be extremely painful. Football is an unpredictable sport, as Daniels' getting stepped on shows. Quarterbacks get hit at odd angles, and Daniels, as a player who runs a lot, can be prone to even more hits. The fact that this injury happened on a fluke play and Daniels had been so good about avoiding contact as a runner (he had 69 rushing yards in the first half alone) makes the injury all the more devastating. You simply can't control or predict how and why players get hurt in the manners they do.
Chao has a good explainer for why Daniels could miss less time -- perhaps a similar timetable to last year -- and play with a brace if he opts to avoid surgery again (or push surgery off until the offseason).
Jayden Daniels could return sooner than expected with an elbow brace, but he’ll likely need it for the rest of the season. Why surgery could still be considered, and why not operating after the first dislocation wasn’t a mistake. pic.twitter.com/4lhBk2dmuk
Again, like Williams, Daniels' testing will provide more detail. Unlike Williams, though, Daniels could be facing a larger decision regarding the long-term health of his injured shoulder.
Tyson Bagent will start for the Bears for as long as Williams is out. Marcus Mariota will start for the Commanders until Daniels returns.
author: Zachary Pereles

title: Caleb Williams injury update: Bears QB reportedly avoids major hamstring injury, has shot to play in Week 3
summary: Williams reportedly is not expected to miss much time and could play against the Eagles
full_text:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has reportedly avoided a major injury to his hamstring, per Tom Pelissero . Tests conducted on Monday brought forth good news, and Williams even has a shot to suit up for Chicago's Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football."
Bears coach Ben Johnson told ESPN Chicago that Williams "will likely miss some time" and labeled him "week-to-week." Still, this is very good news for Chicago.
With about eight minutes remaining in the fourth quarter of the Bears' eventual 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings , Williams went down with a non-contact injury, prompting fears of the worst. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft remained on the wet grass for some time, and rolled around -- struggling to get up.
The Bears' training staff then helped Williams off the field and loaded him into a cart. However, he did give the fans in attendance an emphatic thumbs up as he entered the tunnel.
Caleb Williams is down after a non-contact injury. He immediately grabbed at his leg and this does not look good. pic.twitter.com/ZCpeksJMhJ
Tyson Bagent replaced Williams under center and completed 5 of 9 passes for 54 yards. The Bears were in position to at least tie the game with just seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, but Bagent was sacked by Dallas Turner on the final play at the Vikings' 12-yard line.
Williams completed 15 of 26 passes for 138 yards and one interception before exiting the game, and rushed five times for 42 yards. Johnson told reporters afterward that he was glad Williams didn't suffer a knee injury, but admitted that a hamstring injury "could be pretty damaging, as well." The Bears do have an extra day for Williams to rest, with Chicago scheduled to close out Week 3 in prime time, but even if he doesn't suit up next week, the good news is that the Bears' quarterback is not expected to miss much time with this hamstring issue.
While the weather certainly affected Chicago's offensive output in Week 2, the Bears were the top NFL offense in Week 1. In the 59-37 victory against the Carolina Panthers , Williams became the first Bear to ever throw for 250 yards and two passing touchdowns while also rushing for 50 yards and scoring two rushing touchdowns in a single game. Both D'Andre Swift and Kyle Monangai crossed 100 yards rushing and found the end zone as well. Chicago actually scored six rushing touchdowns, which tied for the most in a season opener in NFL history.
If Williams cannot go in Week 3, Bagent will get his fifth career start for Chicago with the Eagles coming to town. Philly moved to 2-0 on Sunday with its 24-20 victory over the Tennessee Titans . Jalen Hurts threw a touchdown pass to Darius Cooper with nine seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, making him the first Eagles player since Carson Wentz to begin a season with two passing touchdowns in each of the first two games of the year. The Eagles went on to win the Super Bowl , the last time it happened.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Ranking 5 worst losses in Week 2: Falcons, Buccaneers and Commanders all in the running
summary: Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers sputtered in New England, while Jayden Daniels suffered another major injury setback as ugly Sunday performances piled up across the league
full_text:
The second NFL Sunday of the year was much different than the first. Last Sunday featured the most combined points per game (53.3) in Week 1 of NFL history, while Week 2 didn't quite deliver.
The Minnesota Vikings and Chicago Bears had to play in a torrential downpour and mustered just 12 total points. The Houston Texans couldn't score a single touchdown against the new-look Cincinnati Bengals defense, and Aaron Rodgers couldn't get the Pittsburgh Steelers into the end zone against the New England Patriots either. The Atlanta Falcons were again atrocious, and the Los Angeles Chargers were again upset by a team they probably should have defeated.
There were several bad losses on Sunday and a lot of disappointing results. They say Week 1 is a liar, but many teams should hope that Week 2 is the actual liar. Let's power-rank the five worst losses from around the NFL this past Sunday.
Historical data courtesy of CBS Sports Research
The Steelers fell to the Patriots in New England, 20-3. It matched the fewest points in any game started and finished in Aaron Rodgers' career, going back to Week 1 of 2021.
Rodgers completed 23 of 39 passes for 187 yards and one interception, while fumbling twice. The Steelers went 2-of-12 on third downs, while recording just 235 yards of total offense. Pittsburgh has just 499 total yards through two weeks, which are the fewest through two games in Rodgers' Hall of Fame career.
It's not like the Patriots were fantastic either. They converted just four of 12 third downs, while Drake Maye threw for 208 yards and an interception. Fans want to know where the MVP finalist they had last year went.
So, what's the ceiling for the Steelers? They have a new head coach, but it's tough not to judge this team like we have the Steelers squads of recent years. This is a team that can potentially steal a playoff spot, but it isn't a legitimate contender. Rodgers is looking his age, the offensive line is struggling to protect and DK Metcalf can't catch.
Patriots defense pushed the Steelers back from 3rd & 7 to 4th & 43 😳 PITvsNE on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cuwaepRRDX
If you want me to overreact to Week 2, I can definitely do that with the Washington Commanders . You may say that a 37-20 loss to the Dallas Cowboys shouldn't qualify for one of the worst losses of the week, but with what we saw on Sunday afternoon, the Commanders are cooked.
Washington is 0-2 for the first time since 2019, and 2-12 over its past 14 games. Dak Prescott may have proved that this is still one of the worst defenses in the NFL, as he threw for 279 yards, four touchdowns and just five incompletions.
The real reason the Commanders make this list is because star quarterback Jayden Daniels dislocated his left elbow again. Initial X-rays showed no fracture, but could he miss more time than he did in 2025? Daniels didn't have surgery on his elbow last year. Should he have? If he does now, how long will that keep him off the field?
Commanders fans can't be feeling optimistic about how the season is going, and Sunday was a disaster. They are already without star left tackle Laremy Tunsil , while his replacement, Brandon Coleman , left yesterday with a finger injury. Meanwhile, star guard Sam Cosmi is in concussion protocol.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers fell to the Bengals in Week 1 after losing the turnover battle 4-1, and the Cleveland Browns in Week 2 provided a great bounce-back opportunity. Not only is Cleveland perceived to be one of the worst teams in the NFL, but this was also a revenge game for quarterback Baker Mayfield , who was drafted No. 1 overall by the Browns and then ditched by the organization for Deshaun Watson . There was no way Baker and the Bucs were going to lose as 8.5-point favorites. Right? Right?!
The Bucs fell to the Browns on Sunday, 23-19, while Mayfield threw for 182 yards, one touchdown and one interception. The Bucs are 0-2 for the first time since 2014, and 3-10 in their past 13 games after starting the 2025 campaign 5-1. Mayfield has committed 17 turnovers in his past 13 contests and is now 0-2 vs. his former team!
Everything about this game was gross, with a two-hour, 12-minute lightning delay late in the fourth quarter. It set the stage for Mayfield to lead a game-winning drive on a rain-soaked field, but that possession ended on downs at the Browns' 20-yard line.
What's going on with Todd Bowles' defense? Watson completed 24 of 30 passes for 238 yards and two touchdowns in what was his first win since Week 2 of 2024. It was actually reported before the game that Cleveland could be looking to make a change at quarterback depending on how Sunday went!
You don't want to overreact to Week 2 too much, but Bowles may be on the hottest seat in the NFL, Mayfield isn't playing up to the contract he just signed, and the Buccaneers don't look like the top dog in the NFC South. That honor may belong to the New Orleans Saints , who just upset the Baltimore Ravens . Or maybe it's the Carolina Panthers , who won the division last year. Right now, it's definitely not the Bucs. You can't lose to the BROWNS in your home opener.
If we were making a list of most disappointing teams through two weeks, the Chargers are likely headlining. They lost to the Arizona Cardinals in their season opener and then to the Las Vegas Raiders this past Sunday, 26-14. That makes the Chargers the first team in NFL history to start 0-2 with losses to 14-loss teams from the previous season.
It's clear that Justin Herbert hasn't been good. He threw for 192 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions on Sunday, but he's far from the lone issue. Not only is his offensive line and wide receiving corps struggling, but this Chargers defense has been a disappointment. Not many people saw Tre Tucker exploding for 119 yards receiving and a touchdown on five catches yesterday!
What's even more disappointing is that the Chargers' schedule gets much tougher immediately. At 0-2, are they done?
This eight-week stretch features three of last year's four conference championship teams, along with the last four NFL MVPs in Matthew Stafford , Josh Allen , Patrick Mahomes and Lamar Jackson . Best of luck to Jim Harbaugh and the Chargers in turning this thing around.
The Falcons are the worst team in the NFL right now, and they fell to the Panthers in their home opener on Sunday, 34-3.
With Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr . still out, it's been mostly Cooper Rush under center. With him, Atlanta has registered the worst passer rating (38.2) by any team through two games since the 2019 Miami Dolphins . The Falcons are apparently the fourth team since play-by-play was first tracked in 1978 to not have a red zone drive through the first two games of a season!
When the Falcons finally yanked Rush and inserted undrafted rookie Jack Strand at quarterback on Sunday, the fans in Mercedes-Benz Stadium responded with a standing ovation. Strand then threw a pick-six on his first NFL passing attempt.
Falcons fans…The moment you’ve all been waiting for…here’s Jack Strand pic.twitter.com/wk0px7dYWH
Rush and Strand combined to complete 18 of 32 passes for 129 yards and three interceptions in Week 2. It's hard to watch Drake London and Bijan Robinson shake their heads in frustration on the sideline. Sure, the Falcons offense should be "better" with Penix or Tagovailoa in, but how much better? I still think the Falcons are one of the worst teams in the NFL, and Sunday proved it.
You can be happy your favorite team is not the Falcons, but they are about to become a league-wide problem. Atlanta is scheduled to play its next THREE games all in prime time! The NFL needs to step in and do something.

title: Arizona Cardinals need offensive stars to breakout
summary: Through two games the high flying, wheeling and dealing offense has been. Not great. Yes they scored 26 points against the Los Angeles Chargers, but they settled for five field goals, making four and really never looking in sync for the entirety of the game. Then game two happened and it was one of the […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Mike LaFleur of the Arizona Cardinals looks on during the fourth quarter of the game against the Seattle Seahawks at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through two games the high flying, wheeling and dealing offense has been. Not great. Yes they scored 26 points against the Los Angeles Chargers, but they settled for five field goals, making four and really never looking in sync for the entirety of the game. Then game two happened and it was one of the most listless performances on offense I can remember. If you take out Bam Knight’s 24 rushing yards at the end of the game, the team had 127 yards of offense. Even with Knight’s 24 yards, the 151 total yards is the low water mark for the franchise since 2023 when rookie Clayton Tune was a sacrificial lamb to the best defense in the league, the Cleveland Browns. On that day, no one expected much and the 58 yards was embarrassing, but not exactly out of left field. Outside of that one, you’d have to go back to 2018 to be sub 151 yards of total offense. Maybe more than the lack of offensive output is the fact that outside of the second highest paid tight end in the NFL, this group looks devoid of talent. And it’s not because they lack talent, they just don’t seem to be interested in utilizing the talent. Look at these numbers through two games: Jeremiyah Love – 20 carries 70 yards one touchdown, five receptions 25 yards 25 touches for 95 yards for the third overall pick. Michael Wilson – 7 receptions 74 yards on 14 targets Marvin Harrison Jr – 1 reception 33 yards on four targets Eight receptions for 107 yards on 18 targets for the former fourth overall pick and the newly paid receiver. Even Trey McBride’s numbers today looked more like a running back than a tight end with eight receptions for 41 yards and one touchdown. Look, no one is expecting the greatest show on turf by week two, but with the talent we believe this team has, you can’t put up a game that takes you back to Steve Wilks, Mike McCoy and Sam Bradford era. Of course that team had David Johnson, Larry Fitzgerald and Christian Kirk… ok, maybe the names were nice, but DJ was coming off his career altering injury, Fitz was 35 and Kirk was a rookie in game two of his career, so saying that is equal is disingenuous, but this wasn’t fun to watch in the least.

title: NFC South Week 2 Review: Two impressive wins, two embarrassing losses
summary: The Panthers and Saints grab their first wins of the season, while the Falcons and Buccaneers quest for a W continues. The division’s young quarterbacks are making a case that their time is now. Are the Buccaneers already feeling buyer’s remorse, and will the Falcons ever reach the red zone? Here’s the Week 2 NFC […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 20: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers is sacked by Mason Graham #94 of the Cleveland Browns during the second quarter of the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Panthers and Saints grab their first wins of the season, while the Falcons and Buccaneers quest for a W continues. The division’s young quarterbacks are making a case that their time is now. Are the Buccaneers already feeling buyer’s remorse, and will the Falcons ever reach the red zone? Here’s the Week 2 NFC South Review. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-2) Week 2 Result: Buccaneers 19 – Browns 23 Week 3 Opponent: Minnesota Vikings The Buccaneers are a volatile product, as they’ve always been during the Bowles-Mayfield era, but things feel different this year. Mayfield has only thrown for one touchdown across two games, and Tampa Bay is 0-2 for the first time since 2024. Bowles’ defense couldn’t hold off a second-half surge from the Browns, and unlike most seasons, Tampa Bay isn’t dealing with a laundry list of injuries. If this team can’t get a win soon, Todd Bowles could find himself unemployed before the season ends. The Buccaneers will host the 2-0 Vikings, who will have Kyler Murray under center after he cleared concussion protocol Monday. New Orleans Saints (1-1) Week 2 Result: Saints 24 – Ravens 17 Week 3 Opponent: Las Vegas Raiders "And the @Saints turn out the lights on the Ravens here in Baltimore!" – Spero Dedes on the Lamar Jackson INT pic.twitter.com/x6R3QjITJG — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 20, 2026 The Saints scored 15 unanswered points in the 4th quarter, delivering an upset on the road in Baltimore. Tyler Shough is looking like the quarterback he was hyped up to be all offseason. The offense has shown its potential in the first two weeks, but the defense deserves credit for keeping the Ravens offense in check in the second half. Chase Young has been off to an impressive start, and if this defense can keep playing complementary football, this team will be a force in the division. The Saints return home to host the red-hot Raiders, who are 2-0. Carolina Panthers (1-1) Week 2 Result: Panthers 34 – Falcons 3 Week 3 Opponent: Detroit Lions Bryce Young continues to torment the Dirty Birds. He delivered another cerebral performance, escaping pressure with ease and consistently finding the open man. After building a quick lead, the Panthers defense stuffed the Falcons in a locker. Devin Lloyd was all over the field, racking up a sack, two TFLs, two interceptions, and a touchdown. There is a Cooper Rush/Jack Strand tax applied here, but credit to the Panthers for taking care of a weaker opponent the way a good team should. They’ll host the Lions in Charlotte, who are desperate to turn their 0-2 start around. Just a few plays from Devin Lloyd on Sunday. Genuinely, this was one of the best linebacker performances I've seen. The way he mirrors and funnels to the RB in the first clip is great. Good patience to read and attack the angle route from Bijan as the hook-curl defender, and he… pic.twitter.com/bHs6Jlogpw — Jared Feinberg (@Jared_NFLDraft) September 21, 2026 Atlanta Falcons (0-2) Week 2 Result: Falcons 3 – Panthers 34 Week 3 Opponent: Green Bay Packers The Falcons lost by 30 and were shut out in their first 2025 matchup against the Panthers. This Sunday they lost by 31, but hey, they got on the board this time. This offense is a disaster, and this defense already looks stretched thin after two games. Tommy Rees is struggling, and his offense has more than personnel problems; it’s schematically inept. Special teams hasn’t looked sharp, and fans have a right to worry that their 41 year old kicker has lost his touch. It’s a short week for the Falcons, who travel to Green Bay Thursday for their first of three consecutive primetime games. Pray for America. Two weeks isn’t enough time to make concrete proclamations, which is good news for the Falcons and Buccaneers. There’s still plenty of time to recover, but if things don’t get back on track for the 0-2 teams, the Saints and Panthers could make this a two-team race by mid-season.

title: Michael Penix Jr. will start at QB on Thursday Night Football against the Packers
summary: After two weeks of starting their third-string quarterback, the Atlanta Falcons will get their preferred starting quarterback back out there for Week 3. Michael Penix Jr. will start for Atlanta against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football, the team announced. Between reporting from insiders yesterday and Kevin Stefanski saying earlier that there could […]
full_text: FLOWERY BRANCH, GEORGIA - JULY 29: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons runs through drills during training camp at IBM Performance Field on July 29, 2026 in Flowery Branch, Georgia. (Photo by Todd Kirkland/Getty Images) | Getty Images After two weeks of starting their third-string quarterback, the Atlanta Falcons will get their preferred starting quarterback back out there for Week 3. Michael Penix Jr. will start for Atlanta against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football, the team announced. Between reporting from insiders yesterday and Kevin Stefanski saying earlier that there could be an announcement today, it seemed likely we’d hear Penix’s name called. Blessedly, we now have. Michael Penix Jr. has been named starting quarterback for Thursday's game https://t.co/EyBzaBvKii pic.twitter.com/320iqTJ4hN — Atlanta Falcons (@AtlantaFalcons) September 21, 2026 Penix is the only quarterback on this roster that could credibly be Atlanta’s long-term starter, and his audition for that role under the new Stefanski/Ian Cunningham/Matt Ryan regime begins on Thursday night. Drafted eighth overall out of Washington by Raheem Morris and Terry Fontenot, Penix was intended to sit for a couple of seasons and then take over for Kirk Cousins, but wound up in the starting role earlier than intended when Cousins struggled in 2024. The lefty has appeared in 14 games for Atlanta, starting 12, and has completed 59.1% of his passes for 2,757 yards, 12 touchdowns, and six interceptions. We’ve seen glimpses of his ability to attack any area of the field during that time, but not enough to make us think he’s a franchise quarterback. Now fully recovered and cleared from the ACL injury he suffered last fall, and with a couple of extra weeks to work on the remaining but undefined physical hurdles Penix mentioned as the final portion of his recovery, he’ll make his debut in primetime. We’re not yet sure if Tua Tagovailoa will be cleared to return to action, but he’ll do so as the backup with Penix ready, if indeed he does. Cooper Rush will be the team’s third quarterback and Jack Strand will be mothballed the rest of the way if everyone stays healthy, and all of Atlanta’s weapons get a significant upgrade in terms of outlook, as does the entire offense. If Penix hasn’t been as consistent and accurate as we’d like to this point, the fact that he can credibly throw the ball deep and is a much more poised and polished passer than Rush should open things up for an offense that had only scored 16 points in two games thus far. Penix, for his part, will need to show he’s healthy, improved, and a good fit for this offense going forward to make the Falcons commit to him beyond the 2026 season. It’s a tall task, but Penix is talented and will hopefully start both his career renaissance and get the Falcons a badly-needed win on Thursday Night Football.

title: Falcons vs. Panthers recap: A famine for the eyes
summary: Every NFL season begins with a glimmer of hope, a flickering candle in the darkness that seems to show an open door. If you’re a good team, that light burns brighter and longer, and your confident steps forward carry you toward a destination you desire. If you’re a bad team, that light is quickly snuffed […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Chuba Hubbard #30 of the Carolina Panthers runs the ball against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Butch Dill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Every NFL season begins with a glimmer of hope, a flickering candle in the darkness that seems to show an open door. If you’re a good team, that light burns brighter and longer, and your confident steps forward carry you toward a destination you desire. If you’re a bad team, that light is quickly snuffed and you are plunged into umbra, and months are spent fumbling in the darkness looking for a latch that may not even exist. The Atlanta Falcons saw their light snuffed on Sunday. I know that it’s a long season, and the struggling Green Bay Packers are up next on a short week with Michael Penix Jr. potentially returning, and that the state of the NFC South means Atlanta is not out of it two weeks into the year. But I also know that 0-2 is a tough hole to climb out of, and that this Falcons team has to look like a completely different squad with a change at quarterback to see a reasonable way to climb to a winning season. They are already at the fumbling in the darkness stage, because things are bleak and I have not seen enough from this coaching staff or roster to assume they’re going to be able to clean up this mess quickly. And it is a mess. The defense is game and clearly the best unit on the field, but they also allowed Xavier Legette to get behind them for a 55 yard gain, got eviscerated by Bryce Young to the tune of 287 yards and three touchdowns, and let Chuba Hubbard have a solid day on the ground. Special teams looks mediocre in terms of returns and coverage and alarming in terms of the kicking game, now that Nick Folk has missed three field goals in two weeks. And the offense is abysmal, with playmakers looking forlorn on the sideline as Cooper Rush and Jack Strand combined for five turnovers and three points, with Bijan and Brian Robinson doing as much as they could (123 yards on 27 carries, five catches for 25 yards) and London trying his damndest as the only real bright lights on a tough day. An improvement in quarterbacking play will lift this offense to competence, but the pass protection, the miscues, and the penalties suggest it’s going to take a lot of growth to make them better than that. Bad luck and unimaginative planning got the Falcons to their current state at quarterback—you never sign a third quarterback expecting he’ll have to start the first two games of the season, but Penix and Tua were your top two options—but the rest can be hung on game plan and execution. The Falcons can’t (and won’t even try) to attack defenses deep, do not have a good plan for getting the ball to playmakers with those limitations, and are not getting the blocking to just run teams over. I would say the plan to keep Bryce Young in check was a good one—he was pressured at a very high rate, for example—but he repeatedly found open options because the secondary slipped up. And so on. This does not look like a team that has easy answers to adversity, to say the least. What can the Falcons do? Keep going, obviously, because there’s no choice but to do so. But they also need to figure out quickly how to put together a coherent offense that can get them more than 16 points in two games, no matter who ends up being under center in a given week, and how to clamp down on the miscues that have led to defensive and special teams woes that cost them further. The team that just lost by 30-plus points to the Panthers for the second time in two seasons does not look any better under a new regime than it looked under the old one, and while I’ll grant you it takes time and the team’s true goal for contention seems very likely to be 2027, they did want to be fun and competent this year lest they completely lose a fanbase early on that has endured way too many losing seasons. I don’t know what it will look like if the Falcons figure things out starting on Thursday Night Football against the Packers, but I do know that it won’t look anything like this. What I do know is that 0-3 with Atlanta’s schedule and Carolina and New Orleans actually looking like competent football teams probably will mean the lights are out on the 2026 season. On to the full recap. The Good Bijan Robinson looked awfully glum on the sidelines at the end of the game, and it’s difficult to blame him. He’s the player Atlanta counts on to make this thing go, and right now that job is too big for any one man to do. Still, Bijan averaged 4.5 yards on 16 carries and rushed for over 70 yards, doing his part despite being stymied regularly early for minimal gains thanks to subpar blocking. Brian Robinson Jr. is proving to be a nice second fiddle for Bijan, too. He looked decisive and powerful as a runner in this one, putting up 51 yards on 11 carries and doing his best work late when the game was out of hand. Atlanta’s likely to try to keep Bijan fresh when things go awry like this, but I’d trust Brian Robinson in short yardage and goal line situations…if the Falcons ever get into them. Drake London is relentless. Rush missed him badly at least once in the first half, but every catch he got was either a first down or a first down and a major gain. He easily finished as the team’s leading receiver with 51 yards on four grabs, but looked incredibly frustrated on the sideline at the end of the game (again, with justification) and simply isn’t getting enough from his quarterbacks to put up the monster lines he did last year. He needs Penix back in action. Za’Darius Smith is a playmaker. He split a sack in this one with Cameron Thomas—who also had a nice game, I should note—and also hit Bryce Young’s arm on a key third down to force an incompletion. Through two games, he’s been an impactful signing, something I expect to continue. Samson Ebukam and Gervon Dexter came up with a terrific second quarter sack of Bryce Young to decisively end a drive. On second and long, Young went backwards in an attempt to escape but Ebukam got his arm around him and he and Dexter drilled the quarterback to the ground to make it 3rd and 21. Carolina would try a short run and then punt. On a shakier day for the secondary, I thought Xavier Watts mostly played quite well. He forced a fumble, led the team in tackles, and more than once basically crossed the entire field to make a stop. It’s been a quiet start for Watts and Jessie Bates, who are expected to turn up some turnovers for Atlanta, but Watts is still having an impact. I wouldn’t say Jack Strand was good , but after the Falcons pulled some starters alongside Cooper Rush and he threw an unfortunate pick six that was tipped into the air, he looked more competent than I would’ve expected given that he was being thrust into game action in an impossible situation. He threw multiple balls too hard but did deliver some nice quick passes along the way, and as a runner he was very effective, picking up multiple first downs. I don’t want to see him again this season because it would imply we are firmly in football hell and because he’s not remotely ready to play extended action against good football teams, but there’s very obviously a backup quarterback worth developing here. The game did end! At varying points I was afraid it would not. The Ugly Cooper Rush went for it on the very first offensive play of the game, scrambling away on play action for nine yards…but then put the ball on the ground at the end of the play and gave it right to Carolina. Rush had no need to dive for the first down, especially since he was short of the marker, and it was just another ill-advised decision from a quarterback who is very clearly over his head. He followed that up by hesitating for way too long on third down on the next drive, throwing it late and seeing the ball tipped and then picked off. The icing on the cake was an…

title: Ravens vs. Cowboys odds: Opening lines for Week 3 matchup
summary: High expectations for the Baltimore Ravens’ home opener gave way to a disappointing 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints. Next up, the team is heading to Brazil to take on the Dallas Cowboys, who are fresh of a dominant 34-17 victory over the Washington Commanders. The Ravens open Week 3 as three-point favorites over […]
full_text: High expectations for the Baltimore Ravens’ home opener gave way to a disappointing 24-17 loss to the New Orleans Saints. Next up, the team is heading to Brazil to take on the Dallas Cowboys, who are fresh of a dominant 34-17 victory over the Washington Commanders. The Ravens open Week 3 as three-point favorites over the Cowboys ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ). Dallas is technically the home team in this matchup, and their internationally-recognized brand could give them more supporters in the stands of Maracaña Stadium in Rio de Janeiro. But will that be enough to constitute a home-field advantage when both teams are traveling to another continent and playing in an entirely foreign stadium? The matchup is further complicated by reports of poor field conditions from Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio and A to Z Sports’ Mauricio Rodriguez . The NFL has downplayed those concerns, but both teams could wait until they assess the field in person before making decisions on players dealing with injuries, especially those affecting lower body parts. The Ravens did not have wide receiver Zay Flowers (hamstring) on the field on Sunday, and left tackle Ronnie Stanley (toe) left the game and did not return. Returning to the field after months away on an international trip with a questionable playing surface could also be a tough ask for defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike (neck) and Teddye Buchanan (knee). The Cowboys entered the season relatively healthy outside of a thumb injury to left guard Tyler Smith that landed him on injured reserve. But in their first two games, they have already lost three defensive backs: cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and safeties Malik Hooker (arm) and P.J. Locke (foot). Those absences could quickly place Dallas’ secondary under the microscope against a Baltimore passing game that ranks third with 8.3 yards per play and ninth with +0.16 EPA/dropback.
