title: 3 Reasons Why the Chicago Bears Lost to the Minnesota Vikings
summary: Welcome back to the second installment of my new series for the 2026 season, where I recap what I believe were the three reasons the Chicago Bears won or lost the previous game. In week 2, the Bears hosted the division rival Minnesota Vikings in their home opener at soggy and sloppy Soldier Field, where […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears looks on against the Minnesota Vikings during the first quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome back to the second installment of my new series for the 2026 season, where I recap what I believe were the three reasons the Chicago Bears won or lost the previous game. In week 2, the Bears hosted the division rival Minnesota Vikings in their home opener at soggy and sloppy Soldier Field, where the play on the field was just as abysmal as the surface itself. In a game that featured 543 combined yards, it comes as no surprise that the team with the fewest penalties and turnovers won the game. With all that said, Chicago still had multiple chances to win but failed to do so. And here are my three reasons why. 1. Ben Johnson Much like to the quarterback position in how it garners praise in wins and ire in losses, the head coach of the Bears finds himself in the spotlight for the wrong reasons this week. Did Ben Johnson fumble the ball at the goalline to give the ball back? Of course not, but he did sub Swift in for Monangai after the latter carried the offense on his back and into scoring position with 31 yards on three consecutive carries – energizing the crowd and his teammates in so doing. Was it Ben Johnson’s fault that rookie Sam Roush dropped a would-be TD or failed to block the edge rusher on the blocked field goal? Again, no, but as offensive coordinator Ben decides who goes into the game and when. While it may sound harsh, I feel the head coach is ultimately responsible for the penalties that a team commits, especially when he is in charge of the offense and it was his offense that committed 7 of the 8 accepted penalties in the game. Did he commit the false starts by the center? No! But who’s job is it to make sure the center knows what to do? Ultimately, that is the HC. And that’s before we get into the failed chess match against Viking’s DC Brian Flores where the offense looked out of sync and simply ineffective. Oh and the last play where you had a TE blocking their best Edge 1 on 1? Not a good look with the game on the line. You gotta be better, Ben. Sunday was clearly not your best, nor was it even good. 2. Sam Roush Before I highlight the rough play of the rookie TE, I must first point out that I was and remain a fan of Chicago drafting him as their TE3 in the third round of the 2026 NFL draft. He is an elite athlete at the position and arguably best blocking TE in his class. When he finally caught a pass, I loved seeing him shoot forward like a heat seeking missile looking to punish a few feisty Vikings. That said, he had his roughest day as a pro – hopefully ever. He was one of many Bears offensive players to commit a drive-killing penalty but he also dropped a potentially game winning TD and missed his block on both field goal attempts which ultimately led to a block and 3 points off the board. Roush will be a critical part of our offense as we look to run 13 (1 RB, 3 TE) personnel more this season. Games like these can be the turning point in a season for young players, motivating them to put forth just a bit more effort and attention to detail throughout the week of practice that can come up in the clutch in a game of inches. And considering he’s in a room with veteran Cole Kmet and selfless stuff Colston Loveland, I expect that is exactly what we will see. 3. Run Defense Much has been said in the aftermath of this one about the improved effort and performance of Chicago’s defense. And while holding a team to 9 points, especially with our offense, will lead to a win 99% of the time, I just can’t let the team off the hook for how they performed when it comes to stopping the run. With RB1A out this week in Jordan Mason, Aaron Jones carried the load and despite being in his age 32 season, ran like the Aaron Jones of old to the tune of 105 yards and a 4.6 yard average. His highest total in almost two years. The way he was getting 5 yards down the field before getting touched and routinely making the first defender miss was simply unacceptable. Sure, we all anticipate our offense doing a better job of putting points on the board and winning games like these. But in the Black and Blue division and in black and blue weather, the run game is what travels and what makes the difference and it proved as much this week. What about you? Who or what caught your attention in the worst of ways? What needs to improve most for us to win against Philly next week?

title: NFL Week 3 Power Rankings: Contender or Pretender?
summary: Somehow, someway, the 2026 NFL regular season has turned the page on Week 2, and we’re onto Week 3. After an unpredictable opening weekend of football, things started to level out a bit in Week 2. Even so, there’s still plenty to learn over the next few weeks about which teams are for real and […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 20: Joe Burrow #9 of the Cincinnati Bengals huddles with teammates against the Houston Texans during the second half of the game at NRG Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images Somehow, someway, the 2026 NFL regular season has turned the page on Week 2, and we’re onto Week 3. After an unpredictable opening weekend of football, things started to level out a bit in Week 2. Even so, there’s still plenty to learn over the next few weeks about which teams are for real and who are just off to unsustainable starts. With that in mind, let’s dive into our WCG Week 3 Power Rankings! 1. Buffalo Bills (2-0) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender The offense is legit, and even if there are questions about the defense (they’ve given up 31 points in consecutive weeks), it should be enough to keep them as strong Super Bowl contenders all season. Josh Allen looks primed for another MVP run, so assuming the defense can get their sea legs under them at some point soon, they might be the most complete team in the AFC. 2. Seattle Seahawks (2-0) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender No Sam Darnold, no problem. Following a close first half, the Seahawks pulled away in the second half, and Jaxson Smith-Njigba showed why he’s one of the best receivers in the game. With Darnold expected back within the next week or two, Seattle appears to be in great shape to defend their title in the coming months. 3. San Francisco 49ers (2-0) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender We knew the 49ers offense would be a problem (in a good way) this season, but their defense rounding into form is a great sign. After all, that’s basically what they were missing for most of last season. San Francisco is on a roll right now and doesn’t appear to be slowing down any time soon. It appears the NFC West is once again going to be the best division in football. 4. Cincinnati Bengals (2-0) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender The defense is legit, and that’s something Bengals fans have been hoping for since their trip to the Super Bowl a few years ago. Keeping quarterback Joe Burrow healthy will be the key to their season, but assuming all goes well on that front, there’s no reason to believe that they can’t contend in the AFC and push for a deep playoff run. 5. Los Angeles Rams (1-1) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender Week 1 overreactions are always abundant, but last week felt like a time when way too many people “gave up” on the Rams far too soon. Granted, the injury to Jaxson Dart drastically altered Monday night’s game, but I’m not sure the Giants would have been able to stop that offense, regardless of who they had at quarterback. The wait for Myles Garrett’s return will be painful, but it was good to see Aaron Donald back on the field. The Rams are just fine. 6. Philadelphia Eagles (2-0) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender The Eagles are a vastly talented team, and even if neither win has been convincing (+6 points), they are well-rounded on both sides of the ball. They’ll have a nice test on Monday night against the Bears in Chicago, but with Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury, their path to a win should be much easier facing backup quarterback Tyson Bagent. A 3-0 start would be about as best-case scenario as possible, even if none of their wins have looked overly dominant. 7. Minnesota Vikings (2-0) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender Any time a team starts 2-0 within their division over the first two weeks of the season, it’s a great sign for things to come. The offense has some questions, especially at quarterback. Still, assuming Kyler Murray can hit the ground running, they’ve given themselves more than enough of a head start to push for a playoff spot, especially with an elite defense that has blitzed both opponents at close to an 80% rate. 8. Kansas City Chiefs (2-0) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender Sunday night was a fun one, and it appears that the Chiefs are all the way back. Despite being just nine months removed from a torn ACL, quarterback Patrick Mahomes is moving well, and it’s clear that he still has one of the best arms in the league. Kansas City’s defense looks considerably better than they did last year, even if they gave up a higher point total than ideal in Week 2. The AFC West is there for the taking, and right now, it feels like the Chiefs are ready to take the crown back. 9. Baltimore Ravens (1-1) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender Week 1’s offensive output was about as impressive a debut as offensive coordinator Declan Doyle could have asked for. Week 2 didn’t go as planned, but they kept it close until the final minutes. There’s no reason to think that the Ravens won’t get back on track in Week 3, and overall, they’ve looked like a much more complete team so far in 2026 under first-year head coach Jesse Minter. 10. Jacksonville Jaguars (1-1) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender On the road or not, Sunday’s loss came as somewhat of a surprise to most around the league. The Jaguars had been on such a heater that it started to feel like a win was guaranteed each week. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence wasn’t able to follow up on an impressive Week 1, but Denver has one of the best defenses in the league. The good news is that they are in a very winnable division. The bad news is that they have a tough schedule over the next two months. I’m buying what Liam Coen is selling, no matter what the schedule looks like on paper. 11. Denver Broncos (1-1) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender Things didn’t look good against the Chiefs in Week 1, and the offense hasn’t looked the same with offensive coordinator Davis Webb calling plays. That said, this is still a very good defense, and their past success gives them enough track record to believe that they can grab a Wild Card spot at minimum. They’ll face a tough schedule in the immediate future, but their win against the Jaguars proves that they can beat anyone. 12. New England Patriots (1-1) Contender, pretender, or TBD: Contender I won’t discount the Patriots’ remaining strength of schedule, including games against the Jaguars, Bills, and Raiders over their next three. That said, this is a well-rounded team with plenty of offensive firepower and a defense that should keep improving. I won’t believe they are “dead” until I see it, and we are far from that point. 13. Chicago Bears (1-1) Contender, pretender, or TBD: TBA (Pending Caleb Williams’ health) Early reports are that Williams avoided a serious injury, and although he might miss a few weeks, the team hasn’t ruled him out for Week 3’s Monday night matchup against the Eagles. Assuming backup quarterback Tyson Bagent can keep them above water, this should be a Wild Card contender at worst. Staying “alive” over the next two games will be key, and it starts with the Eagles on Monday night at Soldier Field. 14. Detroit Lions (1-1) Contender, pretender, or TBD: TBD The talent is there, but over two weeks, it’s been a mixed bag. Sure, they’ve put up 31 points in back-to-back games, but the majority of that has been put up through two halves in two games. The offense has plenty of talent, but even when healthy, the offensive line has questions. More importantly, the defense is an issue. They’ve given up back-to-back 30-plus-point games (71 overall), over 900 total yards, and have allowed two big quarterback performances—plenty to be learned in the coming weeks, even with an easy schedule. 15. Green Bay Packers (1-1) Contender, pretender, or TBD: TBD The Packers’ six-game losing streak is over, but it took overtime and two serious injuries to offensive starters to get it done. All-World edge rusher Micah Parsons *can* return in two games, although he might be pacing for shortly after that. That said, their next two games are very winnable, which would land them at 3-1 heading into a big Week 5 matchup against the Bears. We’ll see how they fare on Thursday against a…

title: Reviewing the Bears’ PFN grades from Week 2 vs. Vikings
summary: Sunday didn’t go according to plan for the Bears. Not only did Caleb Williams suffer a hamstring injury, but Chicago ended up losing 9-3 to the Vikings in a low-scoring affair that was the complete opposite from the high-scoring shootout against the Panthers last week. The rainy conditions made it difficult for either team to […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears scrambles with the ball against the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sunday didn’t go according to plan for the Bears. Not only did Caleb Williams suffer a hamstring injury, but Chicago ended up losing 9-3 to the Vikings in a low-scoring affair that was the complete opposite from the high-scoring shootout against the Panthers last week. The rainy conditions made it difficult for either team to stretch the field vertically, meaning that trench play was at a maximum. In the end, the Bears just didn’t have an answer for the Vikings’ blitz-heavy approach, and a few major blunders in key moments saw them lose for the first time this season. Each week, I’ll be reviewing how each of Chicago’s eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network’s Impact Scoring model. Here’s what Week 2 looked like. Offense Caleb Williams: 69.9 (25th of 30 QBs) Kyle Monangai: 73.7 (19th of 41 RBs) D’Andre Swift: 71.0 (29th of 41 RBs) Kalif Raymond: 74.2 (23rd of 61 WRs) Rome Odunze: 69.0 (45th of 61 WRs) Luther Burden III: 65.7 (60th of 61 WRs) Colston Loveland: 66.9 (24th of 24 TEs) Braxton Jones: 79.5 (16th of 65 OTs) Joe Thuney: 72.9 (36th of 55 OGs) Garrett Bradbury: 71.1 (24th of 31 Cs) Jonah Jackson: 84.5 (4th of 55 OGs) Darnell Wright: 87.3 (1st of 65 OTs) It’s a clear downgrade from the Bears’ Week 1 performance in terms of the analytics, which matches up with the box score and the actual score. The passing attack was particularly rough, and though poor separation from the team’s weapons didn’t make life easy for Caleb Williams, the quarterback’s own play certainly could’ve been better, too. In all, the Bears ranked No. 27 in the NFL in PFN Offense Impact Scoring in Week 2 after leading the league in the metric in Week 1. There’s obvious inconsistency from week to week here, but a few trends are worth noting. Darnell Wright and Jonah Jackson have graded as elite in each of the last two games, and Braxton Jones has been an average-to-above-average starting tackle in both games. Joe Thuney, Garrett Bradbury, and Luther Burden III remain underwhelming analytically. Defense Montez Sweat: 52.9 (95th of 105 EDGEs) James Lynch: 63.3 (56th of 105 EDGEs) Kentavius Street: 58.0 (66th of 79 DTs) Neville Gallimore: 58.0 (67th of 79 DTs) Grady Jarrett: 60.4 (58th of 79 DTs) Jordan van den Berg: 56.3 (74th of 79 DTs) Austin Booker: 71.4 (44th of 105 EDGEs) Dayo Odeyingbo: 77.7 (23rd of 105 EDGEs) Devin Bush: 84.0 (6th of 67 LBs) D’Marco Jackson: 68.5 (57th of 67 LBs) T.J. Edwards: 59.9 (67th of 67 LBs) Malik Muhammad: 75.7 (26th of 86 CBs) Jaylon Johnson: 64.5 (81st of 86 CBs) Tyrique Stevenson: 60.4 (86th of 86 CBs) Dillon Thieneman: 75.1 (21st of 71 SAFs) Cam Lewis: 70.5 (48th of 71 SAFs) As one could anticipate given the fact that the Bears only allowed 9 points on Sunday, they had a handful of top performers in Impact Scoring in Week 2. In particular, Dillon Thieneman and Malik Muhammad stood out the most to me when I watched them on the All-22. Both rookies have shown a high level of urgency and quick processing at their respective defensive back positions. Though Devin Bush struggled with taking on blocks in the run game, he did look good as a blitzer and in coverage, save for his dropped interception. But the Bears struggled significantly in the defensive trenches, and that showed on tape. They generated very little pressure up the middle, which made things tougher for a defensive end room that’s built much more for clean-up duties alongside interior pressure rather than quick pass-rushing wins. Dayo Odeyingbo had what was, in my mind, his best performance as a Bear, but the defensive line was generally lackluster. We’re getting close to panic status after two disappointing performances from both Jaylon Johnson and Tyrique Stevenson on the back end. Special teams (for the sickos) Cairo Santos: 79.9 (10th of 25 Ks) Tory Taylor: 84.3 (6th of 28 Ps) Despite having one of his two field goal attempts blocked, Cairo Santos isn’t penalized for Sam Roush’s blown blocking assignment. He made a field goal from 50 yards out, which gave the Bears the only points they scored all afternoon. Tory Taylor finished seventh in net average with 46.0 yards per punt, and his +29 net yards over expected ranked fourth among NFL punters in Week 2.

summary: Every team has a game where seemingly everything goes wrong. For the Chicago Bears, that game happened on Sunday afternoon at rainy Soldier Field. full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Aaron Jones Sr. #33 of the Minnesota Vikings runs with the ball during the fourth quarter of the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. For the Chicago Bears , that game happened on Sunday afternoon at rainy Soldier Field. And to make matters worse, the Bears lost starting QB Caleb Williams for the foreseeable future. Luckily, his injury prognosis looks a lot better now (“week to week”) than it did in the immediate moments after Williams went down while running for what would have been the go-ahead touchdown. Just one week after scoring a team record opening week 59 points, the Bears couldn’t even muster a touchdown against their rivals from the north country. The much-talked about Brian Flores Minnesota Vikings defense lived up to its reputation and then some, and the horrible weather conditions certainly didn’t hamper Minnesota’s efforts. The conditions certainly took away some of the Bears air attack, and the team struggled to do much else. Especially when it came to executing in the red zone. Needless to say, after fumbling a would-be touchdown on the one yard line, last week’s game ball recipient D’Andre Swift isn’t going to repeat this week. Let’s get to the game balls. Offense Game Ball: RB Kyle Monangai Considering the 3 point offensive output, there’s very little to celebrate here. Caleb Williams was a magician throughout most of the game, causing Vikings defenders to miss him left and right in the backfield. Nothing to see, just Caleb Williams making a bunch of NFL players look like JUCO transfers. pic.twitter.com/YuLFIBCH7b — Ryan Droste (@ryandroste) September 20, 2026 But he was routinely under pressure against the Vikings defense and had very little success throwing the ball through the steady rain that lasted for the entire game. And unfortunately, he also threw his first interception of the season during the first quarter. Swift actually led the team in receiving and was just two yards behind leading rusher Kyle Monangai, though Swift had a putrid 2.8 YPC for his efforts. And that fumble on the one yard line was a backbreaker. Monangai should have been running the ball on the goal line. 2. One thing that can be frustrating about Ben Johnson is he tends to treat the players as chess pieces. He doesn’t always ride the hot hand. Kyle Monangai was clearly giving MIN problems at 4.7 yards per carry. Yet Johnson stuck with D’Andre Swift, who averaged 2.8. #Bears pic.twitter.com/Oy7idD1tIY — Erik Lambert (@ErikLambert1) September 21, 2026 And with that, we’re going with Monangai as our game ball recipient. He rushed the ball 10 times for 47 yards (4.7 YPC) and caught two passes for 11 yards. He ran hard throughout, and it would have been nice to see him get more opportunities when the Bears were close to the end zone. Defense Game Ball: LB T.J. Edwards The Bears defense, fresh off of giving up 37 points to the Carolina Panthers, looked much better this week against the Vikings. Of course, the weather certainly didn’t hurt matters. WR Justin Jefferson was mostly a non-factor, catching the ball just three times for 55 yards, and 30 of those yards came on a completion during the Vikings’ first possession. All of Jefferson’s catches came in the first half. I thought linebacker T.J. Edwards showed up the most in crucial situations on Sunday, twice making diving, shoe-string tackles on plays that could have been much bigger gains for Minnesota. While his stat line doesn’t pop off the box score (4 tackles, 2 solo), it’ more about the situations where he made those stops. He had no missed tackles and was great in coverage. The two tackles below were the aforementioned crucial stops. The first, early in the second quarter, had Edwards catching Vikings WR Demond Claiborne on a 3rd and long with a lot of green in front of the runner had Edwards missed. The second features Edwards stopping RB DeeJay Dallas on a 3rd and long early in the fourth quarter that almost resulted in a conversion. pic.twitter.com/rPbFkgCfm8 — ✶ ✶ ✶ ✶ (@Someone20241575) September 20, 2026 Bryan Orenchuk and myself will have plenty to say about this game this week on a new episode of Bears Over Beers on Wednesday evening. It will be available on the 2nd City Gridiron YouTube channel or via your favorite podcasting platform. Our 2nd City Gridiron Podcast Channel is available on Apple , Spotify , iHeart , Audacy , and other popular podcast platforms. Who would have received your game balls? Let us know in the comments section below.
author: Ryan Droste

title: Updated: Caleb Williams avoided serious injury; is likely ‘week-to-week’
summary: That massive *sigh* you just heard is from the entire Chicago Bears fanbase welcoming the good news just published about their young franchise quarterback. An update that is MUCH better than the initial speculation. Per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the prognosis for Caleb Williams is positive, as he avoided a serious hamstring injury. Ultimately, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears scrambles with the ball against the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images That massive *sigh* you just heard is from the entire Chicago Bears fanbase welcoming the good news just published about their young franchise quarterback. An update that is MUCH better than the initial speculation. Per Tom Pelissero of The Ringer, the prognosis for Caleb Williams is positive, as he avoided a serious hamstring injury. Bears QB Caleb Williams avoided any major injury to his hamstring Sunday, tests confirmed today — and the team isn’t even ruling him out for next Monday’s game against the Eagles, sources tell @ringer @netflixsports . A massive sigh of relief in Chicago. pic.twitter.com/mfCT5x0JWR — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) September 21, 2026 Ultimately, there still should be precaution exercised here, as hamstring injuries can be tricky to both diagnose and treat without risking setbacks. That being said, there is a chance Caleb Williams does not miss any time due to what is being considered as a mild hamstring pull. It’s certainly better than what Dak Prescott of the Dallas Cowboys recently underwent, as he missed an entire season due to the required surgery. It’s also not the first time in Caleb Williams’ football career that he’s pulled a hamstring. In December of 2022, he suffered a similar injury in his left leg and would not be back to full speed for a month. As teammates have described, Caleb is a very resilient baller who will push to return as soon as possible. Ben Johnson will be speaking to the media in the near future. And, chances are, we should expect Tyson Bagent at quarterback against the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football unless the Bears are 100% convinced Caleb Williams is good to go in one calendar week. Still… I can speak for many of us when I say, “Thank God.” UPDATE: Ben Johnson did a morning spot with Jeff Joniak on ESPN1000 and said , “It sounds like it’s going to be a week-to-week deal for him. … But he will likely miss some time.” UPDATE: Johnson said Williams probably won’t practice this week, but he won’t rule him out for Monday night against the Eagles, adding , “We’re saying week to week with him right now. We’ll see where he’s at as the week progresses and how long that means… It was somewhat encouraging, the report we got.” “He’s right now working through every avenue that he’s got available to get back on track here,” Johnson said about Williams. “We’ll see what that looks like. Here’s what I know. This guy’s a little bit different than the average human being. I said that last night, I’ll double down on that. He gets back – he has in the past – a lot faster than what people can anticipate and so I’m not putting a timeline on this. We’re going to say week to week. He’s going to attack this with everything that he knows.”
author: Erik Duerrwaechter

title: Dear talking heads: Shut up about Caleb Williams’ injury reaction
summary: When you’re at the top of the world, making the spectacular look ordinary, they love you. The moment you slip, they’re ready to pounce. Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears just learned that this week.  A week after putting up an insane 59 points on the Carolina Panthers, the offense looked disjointed and undisciplined against […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears reacts after an injury against the Minnesota Vikings during the third quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images When you’re at the top of the world, making the spectacular look ordinary, they love you. The moment you slip, they’re ready to pounce. Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears just learned that this week. A week after putting up an insane 59 points on the Carolina Panthers, the offense looked disjointed and undisciplined against Brian Flores’ Minnesota Vikings defense in a 9-3 loss. Now, people are talking about Ben Johnson’s jig being up after one game—one poor outing after a track record of excellence so far in his Chicago tenure. But Williams’ injury, and the reaction to it, is the most egregious part. The quarterback going down with a hamstring injury in the fourth quarter while scrambling deep in Minnesota territory added injury to the insult of the day’s offensive performance. All of us held our breath watching him struggle to get off the field and get carted to the locker room, towel over his head at one point, only to then let out a collective sigh of relief when we heard it was a hamstring injury, not an Achilles or knee blowout. That news, however, has only brought the insult back into the injury. Now, Williams’ frustrated, emotional reaction has brought the mouth-breathers out, chastising him for making a scene over what might only be a Grade 1 hamstring strain. All those tears, head-hanging, and letting the fans know you’re okay from the cart are only for real, serious injuries. Now we’re talking about Williams being a crybaby, being too emotional to be a franchise quarterback, being a diva, and all the other things that go hard when you’re stupid. Never mind the fact that Williams, despite being far from perfect on the day, was battling his ass off to get a hard-fought win and trying to make a play for his team on a frustrating afternoon, only to know he had to leave the game at the worst possible moment. Never mind that he, in the moment, had no idea how bad the injury actually was. For all he knew, his muscle might’ve avulsed off the bone, which would have almost certainly meant the end of his season. Never mind the fact that even a Grade I strain still hurts a lot . (I would know. I’ve had almost that exact injury in almost that exact same circumstance, and it does not feel good when the back of your leg trembles as if someone plucked it like a guitar string.) It still means your hamstring has a tear in it, even if it’s a minor one, and that Williams could still miss several games. (Even though he hasn’t been ruled out for next week’s tilt against the Eagles, he almost certainly should not play). And never mind that all of this is going through Williams’ mind in the span of just a few minutes, unsure of what the future holds. Nope. All the former NFL players-turned-podcasters and media hot-take artists who would flail around like they got shot if they had the same injury just couldn’t wait to question his toughness and make fun of him rather than simply be glad the injury wasn’t worse. Because that’s what we reward these days: stupidity, ignorance, and a lack of empathy for anything we don’t personally go through. (Honestly, that makes the former-player takes that much worse: you’ve been through these situations, and you still felt the need to pop off?) It’s all because of who he is—the unapologetic fingernail-painter whose pose and superstar ability fly in the face of what football culture says you should be. It’s about what the Chicago Bears are and what they’re becoming—no longer the laughingstock of the league but an up-and-coming contender with real expectations and a coach who doesn’t care about playing nice. I warned you it was coming . That they were just waiting for the chance to talk crazy about Williams the moment he looked vulnerable. Well, here it is. And it’s even more idiotic than I expected. And the worst? Some of y’all should know better, and you proved you don’t. Silence is always an option. If you feel the need to pile on Williams for how he reacted to getting hurt, I’m inviting you to employ it now.
author: Khari Thompson

title: Bears vs. Vikings: Inside the Snap Counts, Stats, and so many mistakes
summary: Luckily, the Chicago Bears have a 24-hour rule that gives them a day to either celebrate a win or get over a loss, because this is a game the Bears would like to forget. But before they move on to the Philadelphia Eagles, they’ll need to dissect some of the worst tape this regime has […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 2026: Minnesota Vikings safety Joshua Metellus (44) and safety Theo Jackson (26) jared the ball from Chicago Bears tight end Sam Roush (87) in the fourth quarter at Solider Field in Chicago, Illinois, on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) Luckily, the Chicago Bears have a 24-hour rule that gives them a day to either celebrate a win or get over a loss, because this is a game the Bears would like to forget. But before they move on to the Philadelphia Eagles, they’ll need to dissect some of the worst tape this regime has ever had with their 9- 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings. Chicago’s 3 points were their lowest output since December 26, 2024, and if you were wondering when a Ben Johnson-led offense had this few points, you’d need to go back to October 9, 2022, his first year as the full-time play caller in Detroit, when the Patriots shut out the Lions. The Bears gained more yards (297 to 246) and had more first downs (17 to 11), but they deserved to lose this game. They were penalized 8 times for 58 yards, while the Vikings were penalized just 3 times for 25 yards. The Bears got into the red zone three times and got to a goal-to-go situation twice, but a fumble on the one-yard line and a blocked field goal doomed their chances of winning. The defense, which looked bad a week ago, bounced back against a lesser opposition in the rain, but everything else that could have gone wrong did. Minnesota defensive coordinator Brian Flores threw a lot of looks and pressure at the Bears, and he dictated the game to Ben Johnson, who didn’t have an answer. Let’s look at the Bears’ playing time breakdowns and a few individual stats from the game. OFFENSE Caleb Williams had a game he’d like to forget, with his lowest passer rating since the aforementioned 12/26/24 game against the Seattle Seahawks. Kalif Raymond was the Bears’ most productive wide receiver for the second consecutive week. Which, you know, is good for Raymond, but with Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III on this team, it’s not a good look for them. Tight end Colston Loveland has 1 catch and 3 yards in two weeks and was pass blocking on the final play of the game instead of running to the end zone with his 6’6″, 241-pound frame. Chicago’s offensive line, which was so good a week ago, wasn’t moving people yesterday, and center Garrett Bradbury was called for 4 penalties (3 accepted, 1 offsetting). Bears TE Colston Loveland said postgame that Caleb Williams broke down the team and didn't mention his injury. Per Loveland, Williams told them: "Let it hurt, let it sting, watch the tape, clean it up, get back and be 1-0 next week." — Kalyn Kahler (@kalynkahler) September 21, 2026 DEFENSE Chicago held the Vikings to just 3 for 13 (23.1%) on third downs. Rookie safety Dillon Thieneman toed for the team lead with 7 tackles. He also had a pass defended. Defensive lineman James Lynch, who got the start, also had 7 tackles Tyrique Stevenson had 5 tackles, a tackle for loss, and a PD. Cam Lewis had 5 tackles. Rookie Malik Muhammad II recorded the first sack of his career to go along with 3 tackles and a TFL. Dayo Odeyingbo had a TFL, a sack, and 2 QB hits. Austin Booker had a TFL and a sack. SPECIAL TEAMS* *The above image has players who only played in the third phase. Cairo Santos made a 50-yard field goal but had a 23-yarder blocked. Rookie tight end Sam Roush missed his block on the play. Tory Taylor had 4 punts for a 48.8 average (46.0 net), with 3 punts inside the 20. Jack Sanborn had 2 tackles. Raymond had 30 punt return yards on 3 returns. Zavion Thomas had 3 kickoff returns for 68 yards. To check out the complete Bears vs. Vikings box score, I find ESPN’s site is easy to navigate. title: 5 Bears Takes: Waiting on a Williams update, red zone failures, and good defense?
summary: Week 2 of the NFL delivered another outstanding weekend of football, but the offense was much harder to find for most teams. Unfortunately, the Chicago Bears were one of those teams, putting up just three points over 60 minutes of football. Despite a final score of 9-3 not going their way, all eyes are on […]
full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 2026: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) was hurt and was replaced by Chicago Bears quarterback Tyson Bagent (17) in the fourth quarter of an NFL game against the Minnesota Vikings at Solider Field in Chicago, Illinois, on Sunday Sept. 20, 2026. (Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) Week 2 of the NFL delivered another outstanding weekend of football, but the offense was much harder to find for most teams. Unfortunately, the Chicago Bears were one of those teams, putting up just three points over 60 minutes of football. Despite a final score of 9-3 not going their way, all eyes are on the health of quarterback Caleb Williams, who left in the fourth quarter what appeared to be a serious hamstring injury. At (1-1) and (0-1) within the division, how they fare over the next few weeks (or maybe more) will determine how competitive they can be in November and December. For more on a disastrous Sunday and how to move forward, let’s dive into our weekly postgame Bears Takes. 1. Although head coach Ben Johnson was noncommittal during his postgame presser, Monday’s MRI results for Caleb Williams might dictate how serious of a contender the Bears can be moving forward this season. The early reports are promising, though. Even with a strong performance from the defense on Sunday, it was fair to say that the Bears’ ceiling was going to be dictated by how well they were able to settle in after a rough Week 1 against the Carolina Panthers. With Williams out for the foreseeable future, the road back to the playoffs became that much harder. According to NBC Sports’ Mike Florio, there’s optimism that Williams suffered a Grade 1 sprain, which would keep him out only a few weeks. Outside of Florio, both Johnson and the top insiders have echoed the same information: Williams will have an MRI on Monday to determine the severity of his hamstring injury. Given how bad it looked in real time, anything short of season-ending would feel like a big “win” for the long term. That said, anything that avoids injured reserve should keep the Bears in the playoff race. For what it’s worth, the Seahawks are in a very similar position with Sam Darnold leaving Week 1 with a glute injury. They are also trying to keep their heads above water, but the initial thought is that Darnold will return before Williams. Sunday’s loss (which we’ll touch on more later) was tough enough, but it’s worth keeping in mind that navigating this at 2-0 with a divisional win is a lot easier than what they are currently facing. To muddy the waters even more, this will be the first time that Johnson will be calling plays relying on a backup quarterback. The offense will need to change moving forward, but relying on their run game will be key to finding offensive success. For now, we’ll wait for a more concrete timeline and hope it’s on the shorter end of everyone’s feared timeline. 2. Even before Williams’ injury, the offense was getting their brains beat out by Vikings’ defensive coordinator Brian Flores. Like we pounded home last week, overreacting to Week 1 rarely works out well. Plenty of other teams struggled around the league to follow up their season-opening performances. All week, we heard about the battle between Johnson and Flores. For outside observers, I’m sure it’s a great chess match to watch twice a year, but for Bears fans, it hasn’t been overly fun since Johnson came over from Detroit. Despite their 59-point performance last week, the offense struggled all day to move the ball. Even when they were in position to score, it backfired every time except for their first-quarter field goal. Williams had one of his worst games in quite some time, but he was far from the only disappointment on Sunday. The run game struggled to get going consistently. For all the explosive plays they had last week, many more runs went for less than two yards in their home opener. More concerning, their receivers weren’t getting open, and the offensive line wasn’t holding up in pass protection against the blitz. To be fair, Flores blitzed over 70% of the time, but even so, this offense has proven it can succeed against that approach in the past. The offensive line is down two starters from last season, but even so, they looked disjointed for most of the game. Despite all their issues, they still had multiple chances to put points on the board and simply couldn’t. The goal-line fumble from D’Andre Swift felt like a back-breaker in the moment, but the blocked field goal felt like a week-long issue in the making. Rookie long snapper Beau Gardner has shown a tendency to snap the ball high, but the blocking off the edges was shaky last weekend against the Panthers, too. While these are the types of games that feel like they are simply impossible, Johnson and this offense will now be tasked with getting back on track against another tough defense on a national stage next Monday night. Figuring out the penalties will be key, but their execution in “scoring position” must also vastly improve. Now they’ll be doing that with a backup quarterback under center. 3. The defense was far from perfect, but if you had told anyone earlier in the week that they gave up just nine points and no touchdowns, everyone would have assumed the Bears won in a blowout. There aren’t going to be many “pretty” performances from this defensive group, but this was about as good a day as anyone should realistically ask for in 2026. Allowing an aging Aaron Jones to go for 105 yards on 23 carries isn’t ideal, but allowing just 127 total passing yards, three sacks, and no touchdowns should be enough for almost any team to win a game. That said, maybe we shouldn’t be as surprised. After all, Carson Wentz has been responsible for handing some ugly losses to the Bears. Before Sunday, the last time he started a game and beat the Bears was when the Bears couldn’t overcome a 12-point defensive effort, in which they had multiple cracks inside the five on Thursday night football. Regardless of the Brock Osweiler-type black magic, the defense played more than well enough to come out with a victory on Sunday. Still, it didn’t happen thanks to some very uncharacteristic struggles from the offense. On the plus side, their performance should give fans hope that they won’t set bad records and that being closer to league-average isn’t out of the question. If we are being honest, their best shot at staying afloat might be playing as close to league-average as possible, with Williams expected to be on the shelf for a while. 4. For years, we’ve heard how good of a backup Tyson Bagent is. With Williams out for the foreseeable future, we’ll see if he can keep the Bears in the mix. It’s also worth noting that this will be Johnson’s first time navigating these waters, too. Simply put, the Bears’ immediate playoff hopes (even heading into Week 3) will ride on how much Johnson can get out of his backup quarterback. The team has loved him since he came in as an undrafted free agent from Shepherd. He’s survived through two head coaches and is just a little over a year removed from signing a two-year extension. Regardless of what anyone wants to believe, the difference between Williams and Bagent is very different. While Bagent has some mobility in his game, the stark difference in arm strength will be extremely noticeable. That doesn’t mean Bagent can’t succeed. In fact, Johnson’s vote of confidence in him should give Bears fans plenty of hope that with some modifications to the offense, they can still do more than enough to win games. I expect the offense will become more of a “quick strike” unit that relies on quick, decisive reads and, of course, a strong run game. That might help the offensive line get into a better rhythm, but the big-play aspects of this unit might be less consistent. Think more of what Johnson did in Detroit with Goff as a better example. How long Williams is out will also matter. Initial…
author: Aaron Leming

title: Boye Mafe has been a major free agent hit for the Bengals so far
summary: In 2021, the Cincinnati Bengals had one of the best offseasons in team history, highlighted by the addition of Trey Hendrickson in free agency. At the time, Hendrickson was viewed as a solid player who still had room to grow after four years with the New Orleans Saints. But what happened next was what truly […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Boye Mafe (53) reacts after a play during the first quarter against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect In 2021, the Cincinnati Bengals had one of the best offseasons in team history, highlighted by the addition of Trey Hendrickson in free agency. At the time, Hendrickson was viewed as a solid player who still had room to grow after four years with the New Orleans Saints. But what happened next was what truly made this one of the best moves in team history. Hendrickson would blossom into a legitimate Defensive Player of the Year candidate. His addition was a big reason why the Bengals made back-to-back AFC Championship Games and earned an appearance in Super Bowl LVI. This offseason, the Bengals attempted to recreate that magic with Boye Mafe, another rising edge rusher who hadn’t quite had his breakout yet but still flashed a wealth of potential for a Seattle Seahawks defense that carried the team to a Super Bowl LX championship. Neither Hendrickson nor Mafe was viewed as a true game-changer when the Bengals signed them, but the former became a hit, and the latter is off to a good start toward becoming one. Pass rush win rate leaders through week 2 for edge rushers (via PFF and SumerSports) pic.twitter.com/1SJInJjblu — Shaun Newkirk (@Shauncore) September 21, 2026 In Sunday’s 20-6 win over the Houston Texans, Mafe terrorized CJ Stroud throughout the game and never let the Pro Bowl quarterback find any rhythm. The 27-year-old edge rusher finished with eight QB pressures, the third-most of any player in Week 2 (pending Monday Night Football). After two games, Mafe has racked up 12 total pressures, the fourth-most of any NFL defender. His 85.3 defensive grade from Pro Football Focus is the 10th-highest among NFL edge rushers. But don’t sleep on Mafe’s ability to hold his gap and defend the run. His 86.8 run defense grade ranks fourth among all edge rushers and is tied for 11th among all NFL defenders. That’s an area the Bengals desperately needed an upgrade this offseason. Boye Mafe (53) getting 3 straight pass rush wins vs Texans rookie Keylan Rutledge pic.twitter.com/O4HoVdF8UB — Goodberry (@JoeGoodberry) September 21, 2026 For all the good Hendrickson did rushing the passer, his run defense could leave a lot to be desired. It’s part of why the defense faltered so much in recent years, despite Hendrickson being arguably the best pass rusher in football. At times, it was just too easy for opponents to run the ball when Hendrickson was on the field, but so far, Mafe is showing he can hold up well against the run and pass. The Bengals will still need these pressures to turn into more sacks as the season wears on. Mafe has one sack so far after notching two last season, though he is getting pressure at a higher rate. After getting pressure on 11.5% of his pass-rushing snaps last season, he’s up to 17.4% through two games this year. And his 85.3 PFF grade would be the highest of his five-year career, with the previous high at 75.1 in 2024. Take away Tampa Bay’s pick-six in Week 1, and the Bengals defense has allowed just 26 points this season. Mafe has been a big part of that, and it’s starting to make people believe this team can make a run back to the Super Bowl. Boye Mafe with the strong debut for the Bengals. He led the team with 4 pressures, was in on the forced fumble with Cook and had the recovery in the first half, and later had a sack fumble forced in the second half. pic.twitter.com/yIZb7EPSDX — Bengals & Brews (@BengalsBrews) September 14, 2026

title: 5 things we learned from the Bengals’ dominant win over the Texans
summary: The Bengals went into Houston to face a Texans defense that was known for its physicality, but Cincinnati came out looking like the bully. You might call the Week 2 win “the Dexter Lawrence game,” but that name could apply to Cincinnati’s Week 1 win and potentially subsequent wins as well. Here are five things […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 20: Quarterback C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans is sacked by linebacker K.C. Ossai #52 of the Houston Texans on fourth down in the final seconds of the NFL football game between the Houston Texans and Cincinnati Bengals on September 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Bengals went into Houston to face a Texans defense that was known for its physicality, but Cincinnati came out looking like the bully. “It’s on us.” #CINatHOU September 20 at 1:00 PM on CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/jHA5xOFTMW — Cincinnati Bengals (@Bengals) September 20, 2026 You might call the Week 2 win “the Dexter Lawrence game,” but that name could apply to Cincinnati’s Week 1 win and potentially subsequent wins as well. Here are five things we learned from Sunday’s victory: This defense is as physical as any defense In Week 1, the Bengals caused fumble after fumble by Baker Mayfield and company. But against the Texans, they just hounded them for the entire game in every aspect. Keep in mind, Houston went toe-to-toe with Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills in Week 1. And the Bengals held them to zero touchdowns. The Texans did outgain the Bengals, 374 yards to 266 yards. But, like in Week 1, they didn’t break when it mattered, making C.J. Stroud look inaccurate thanks to 41 pressures. How about this from the raw @PFF data: The #Bengals racked up 41 pressures against Houston on Sunday. FORTY-ONE. Their average pressures per game over the last six years: 12.6 Previous high over that span: 33. — Paul Dehner Jr. (@pauldehnerjr) September 21, 2026 Cincinnati’s average pressures per game over the last six years is 12.6, and the previous high in that span was 33. So this is a whole other level of defensive play. The Bengals’ defense also held David Montgomery and Woody Marks to just 18 yards on 14 carries. As a result, Stroud threw 55 times, but it was to little avail. Perhaps most impressively, through two games, the Bengals are third in passing EPA per play and 6th in run defense EPA per play. The current Cincinnati Bengals DEFENSIVE rankings 4th in EPA per play 10th in Success Rate 3rd in Passing EPA/play 16th in Passing Success Rate 6th in Run Defense EPA/play 4th in Run Success Rate pic.twitter.com/IdQYTt20Xw — Goodberry (@JoeGoodberry) September 21, 2026 Dexter Lawrence, it should go without saying at this point, is instant chaos on every single play, blowing up the middle of the line to the point that the rest of the defense feels empowered to make something happen. It really is an unbelievable turnaround led by an unbelievably talented nosetackle. Ja’Marr Chase is just fine This probably wasn’t much of a concern for most, but after a knee scare late in the offseason and a 12 yard performance in Week 1, Chase reminded the world of just how good he is. His seven catches for 75 yards and two touchdowns don’t even begin to tell the story. A better way to get how amazing he looked is to watch this twisting catch against Derek Stingley Jr. one more time for yourself. That toe drag tho 😮‍💨 CINvsHOU on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xgHtW39CJO — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Amarius Mims is already elite That’s two straight games where the third-year right tackle has pitched a shutout, keeping the Bucs and Texans to zero pressures on over 70 pass-block snaps. Somehow, Mims kept Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter to zero pressures on 34 pass-block snaps. He flashed elite potential last year, but he’s completely arrived now. We can’t get carried away with the 0-line The line is better, yes, but a good amount of credit needs to go to Mims. He’s an absolute anchor, and we would see Joe Burrow leverage that to improvise on the right side behind his giant bodyguard. But the rest of the line had some issues, especially Orlando Brown Jr., who may need an intervention. Burrow was sacked five times and hit ten more. That is far from ideal, and it’s an easy recipe for another injury-shortened season. Evan McPherson is all the way back to being Money Mac When your kicker is so consistent from behind 50 yards that you don’t hesitate to go for three points when you’re across midfield, that’s a major asset. He’s now four for four from 50+ yards in two games. It’s clear that McPherson has his confidence back, which is allowing his tremendous talent to shine through just as it did in 2021.

title: Bengals News: 2-0 and it feels so good
summary: Wow what a difference a year makes. The Cincinnati Bengals are once again 2-0, and this time there is actual optimism to go along with that. It also hasn’t been Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins carrying the team on their back to the wins. In fact, quite the contrary. The defense has been […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Cincinnati Bengals defensive tackle Dexter Lawrence II (97) celebrates after defeating the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Wow what a difference a year makes. The Cincinnati Bengals are once again 2-0, and this time there is actual optimism to go along with that. It also hasn’t been Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins carrying the team on their back to the wins. In fact, quite the contrary. The defense has been holding up the offense, and that has not gone without notice from the quarterback. “It feels like early on in 2021,” Burrow told Geoff Hobson from Bengals.com . “We’ve got a really good defense, and try to stay in front of the sticks, not turn the ball over, kick field goals, put points on the board, we’re going to win with our defense.” Back in 2021 you had players like linebackers Germaine Pratt and Logan Wilson as well as several secondary guys like Jessie Bates, Chidobe Awuzie and Mike Hilton who could make the defensive plays at the end of the games to seal things out. That is something this team hasn’t really had these past few seasons. It takes so much pressure off an offense when you don’t have to assume the other team is going to score nearly every time. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Bengals News Postgame Quick Hits | Bengals Deliver Statement In Bruising Complete Game Win Over Texans It certainly shows how far this defense has come the this team can win only scoring 20 points. It used to be iffy if they scored 30. It shows this team doesn’t have to treat every offensive possession as a do-or-die situation needing to score points. Especially when they are playing such a great defense like that of the Houston Texans. Dexter Lawrence is changing the game plan for the Bengals and their opponents Box score watchers will always be disappointed in Lawrence. But you simply have to understand that this guy absolutely is having a massive impact when he is out there. The Texans had to abandon the run because they simply couldn’t get away from Lawrence or anyone freed up by trying to block him. Not to mention the amount of pressure the defensive line is getting with just four rushers is no mistake. Joe Burrow played ‘incredibly average.’ That could be scary for AFC Some fans may get riled up by this, but truly this offense has not bloomed yet. It mostly looked to not make the big mistake against Houston. That means there should be another level to this team where Burrow and this offense is able to get going and score those big points while also having this defense behind them. NFL News Todd Monken fires back after win over Buccaneers: ‘Browns are the Browns, (expletive) that’ The Cleveland Browns certainly got their first win pretty early this season. They also looked generally good on the day, but we will have to see how long that continues. To have this kind of rant after their recent history with Deshaun Watson at quarterback is kind of comical. Jim Harbaugh ‘not deterred’ by Chargers’ 0-2 start following double-digit loss to Raiders Things are not great for the Los Angeles Chargers. A vast majority of people would have expected them to start 2-0, but instead they sit at 0-2 with a huge hole to dig out of. So much for that Justin Herbert finally having that year their fans have dreamed about. 2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games The Bengals did not allow a single touchdown in Week 2 at the Texans, their first game allowing no touchdowns since Week 3, 2022, at the Jets. Cincinnati broke a franchise-long and NFL-long streak of 65 consecutive games allowing at least one touchdown. The Bills now own the longest active streak in the NFL, having allowed at least one touchdown in 47 consecutive games. Just a crazy, crazy stat. It isn’t exactly surprising given the fall off this team had defensively over that time. However, it feels good to have that monkey off their back I’m sure.

title: Lessons from Week 2: Deshaun Watson, Baker Mayfield, Week 1 Browns, defense in our 4 Downs
summary: Raise your hand if you had the Cleveland Browns going on the road upsetting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. No one? Okay, well, not no one, but very few. Raise your hand if you had quarterback Deshaun Watson outplaying Baker Mayfield. Okay, no more questions. Despite a lengthy rain delay late in the 4th quarter, the […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (6) greets Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson (4) after a game at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Raise your hand if you had the Cleveland Browns going on the road upsetting the Tampa Bay Buccaneers . No one? Okay, well, not no one, but very few . Raise your hand if you had quarterback Deshaun Watson outplaying Baker Mayfield. Okay, no more questions. Despite a lengthy rain delay late in the 4th quarter, the Browns found a way to finish their Florida road trip on a high note by beating the Bucs. Almost everyone picked Tampa Bay to win ; however, it was Cleveland leaving Raymond James Stadium with a victory. 1st Down: Never overreact to Week 1 Week 1 overreactions are the best. It’s what makes the NFL (or any sport, for that matter) unique. Yes, the Browns had a bad outing last week against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The most important thing for Cleveland was to see how they would respond. Both offensively and defensively, the team had a much better showing. This team is unlikely to make the postseason, but they have the opportunity to play spoiler in certain weeks. If the NFL has taught us anything, never overreact to the 1st week of the season. Unless it is justified. 2nd Down: Give Deshaun Watson his flowers Give credit where credit is due. Everyone knows how poorly Watson has played since he’s been in Cleveland, but Week 2 was one of his best outings as a Brown. The last time I saw Watson play this well was back in 2023 during the 2nd half of their game against the Baltimore Ravens. Granted, the bar is low, but he looked like the guy that the Browns traded for. Watson made the necessary plays that he needed to make and used his legs to his advantage. Considering how he looked last week and how he was talked about locally and nation the entire week, a performance like this was something he needed. It’s unlikely that he finishes the season as the starter, but overall not a bad at-the-office for Watson. 3rd down: Baker Mayfield shows why the Browns moved off him I don’t like bringing up stuff from the past, but this third down will be the exception. When it comes to Mayfield, he’s not a bad quarterback, but he’s not someone who’s going to elevate your team and get you to a Super Bowl. You can question Cleveland for replacing Mayfield with Watson, but you can’t question the Browns moving off of Mayfield. Deshaun Watson outplayed Baker Mayfield on Sunday. It’s not an exaggeration; it’s a fact. Tampa Bay signing Mayfield to an extension was a premature decision, and it’s a decision the team felt they were forced to make. I understand not wanting to lose Mayfield in free agency, but giving him all that money when he hasn’t earned it just wasn’t smart by them. It was the decision the Browns refused to make. Mayfield hasn’t played well going back to the second half of last season, and it has continued. Constant overthrows and not seeing open receivers; it was a bad day for Mayfield. Sunday showed why Cleveland was right to move on. 4th down: Defense responds It is no exaggeration to say that the Browns defense had one of their worst outings in some time in Week 1, by their standards. This week? Much better. Cleveland’s defense could use Myles Garrett right now more than Jim Schwartz. Losing a player like Garrett hurts because you don’t have that presence when it matters the most. Having someone like that can elevate an entire defense, but as of now they don’t have that. Overall, outside of a few explosive plays given up, the performance was better. The tackling will get better as the year goes on, and the moving parts will eventually settle in. Defensive tackle Mason Graham is the best player on the defensive line as of right now. Jared Verse will receive some grace with the win, but the concerns about him were valid in terms of his pass rushing. Tampa’s offense didn’t do themselves any favors, but the Browns defense had a good day after an abysmal outing last week. Extra Points I don’t fault Todd Monken for being aggressive, but if you are going to be aggressive, at least be smart. Going for it deep in your own territory wasn’t the best idea and the play call was terrible. Thankfully, Monken avoided being a talking point this week by redeeming himself later in the game I don’t know if Tampa Bay is bad or not, but they aren’t as good as people suggested they would be. It’s early, but the early returns aren’t good. The Browns came out of the weather delay with high energy, which didn’t surprise me, as the effort for this team hasn’t been an issue. The run blocking is a work in progress; I cannot emphasize that enough. It will be a while before the offensive line will be able to run effectively Denzel Boston is pretty good. So is Harold Fannin Jr. And KC Concepcion. Oh, and Quinshon Judkins. 24 hours removed, what are some of your takeaways from the Browns vs Bucs in Week 2? Join the conversation! title: Did Cleveland play more man coverage this week? Browns defensive snap counts
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ defense played much better this week. It still was far from perfect, but I saw what I believed to be more man coverage, more blitzes, and obviously more times getting home to the quarterback. Now, I’d also say that Tampa Bay executed far less efficiently than Jacksonville did, but that happens in […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 20: Emeka Egbuka #2 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers misses a catch in the end zone against the Cleveland Browns during the fourth quarter of the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns’ defense played much better this week. It still was far from perfect, but I saw what I believed to be more man coverage, more blitzes, and obviously more times getting home to the quarterback. Now, I’d also say that Tampa Bay executed far less efficiently than Jacksonville did, but that happens in the NFL sometimes. There’s still work to be done, but for at least one week, it’s refreshing to see a coaching staff that doesn’t say, “I don’t care, I’m not changing my philosophy.” Lack of adapting is something that has frustrated me with Browns coaches over the years, even with Jim Schwartz to a degree. Let’s see if it continues. As blitzes increased, man coverage naturally rose in Week 2. The Browns were in man coverage on 55% of Baker Mayfield's dropbacks, per @NextGenStats . Cleveland ran Cover 1 on half of Mayfield's dropbacks. https://t.co/hfbe68T93u — Daniel Oyefusi (@DanielOyefusi) September 21, 2026 Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on defense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Defensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats DL Jared Verse 42 65% 1 tackle (1 combined). 1 TFL, 1 QH. DL Maliek Collins 41 63% 1 tackle, 1 assist (2 combined). DL Mason Graham 41 63% 1 tackle, 2 assists (3 combined). 1 sack, 1 TFL, 2 QH. DL Isaiah McGuire 40 62% 3 tackles, 1 assist (4 combined). 1 TFL. DL Mike Hall 26 40% No stats registered. DL Sam Williams 26 40% 1 tackle, 1 assist (2 combined). DL Adin Huntington 22 34% 1 assist (1 combined). DL Derek Barnett 22 34% 2 tackles (2 combined). 1 TFL. Jared Verse logged his first quarterback hit for Cleveland, and it was a better performance than Week 1, but through two games, he hasn’t flashed the same potential he did with the Rams. Mason Graham turned in his second straight solid effort, showing to be a consistent force up front. He received a PFF grade of 70.7, and logged his second sack of the season. Maliek Collins was back to his starter-level reps, while Adin Huntington’s reps took a hit. That’s something I called for last week, and it came to fruition. Grade-wise, both players still really struggled, so it’ll be interesting to monitor whether Collins can get back to being the dominant force he was a year ago. Kudos to Isaiah McGuire , who had a solid all-around game and graded out to a 71.0 by PFF. I even saw him in coverage once. Derek Barnett has also been a good veteran presence thus far for depth. Linebacker Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats LB Carson Schwesinger 65 100% 5 tackles, 5 assists (10 combined). 1 TFL. LB Quincy Williams 59 91% 4 tackles, 2 assists (6 combined). 1 TFL. We still haven’t seen the lights-out play from Carson Schwesinger , but this was also better than a week ago, and I also made mental note of his one tackle for loss, and then being the guy to close in on Baker Mayfield after that long lightning delay to prevent him from escaping. Per PFF, Quincy Williams graded out to a 78.9, third-highest on the team despite a lower tackling grade. Cornerback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats CB Denzel Ward 65 100% 4 tackles, 1 assist (5 combined). 1 FF. CB Myles Harden 56 86% 2 tackles, 3 assists (5 combined). 1 INT, 2 passes defended. CB Tyson Campbell 49 75% 4 tackles, 1 assist (5 combined). 1 TFL. CB Mekhi Blackmon 16 25% 2 tackles (2 combined). 1 pass defended. CB Noah Igbinoghene 8 12% 2 tackles (2 combined). This was a great day for the Browns’ cornerbacks. Tyson Campbell played hurt and had to leave a couple of times, but Denzel Ward and even Myles Harden stepped up huge. Harden, in arguably his best game, logged his first career interception and received a team-high 90.6 grade from PFF. Ward was a close second with a grade of 90.4. After that group, though, it’ll be interesting to see if Cleveland continues to look at their depth. Will we see Michael Coats called up at some point? Safety Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats S Grant Delpit 65 100% 5 tackles (5 combined). 1 sack, 1 QH. S Ronnie Hickman 62 95% 1 tackle, 2 assists (3 combined). 1 sack, 1 QH. S Emmanuel McNeil-Warren 10 15% No stats registered. Besides Jared Verse , the most disappointing defender through two games has to be Ronnie Hickman . He had several bad looks in the open field, which I get is much easier said than done to make those plays, but the angles, pursuit, and execution weren’t there. He did register his first career sack, but also let Mayfield get away a couple other times. Emmanuel McNeil-Warren also remains a small part of the defense. He played 15% of the snaps again, but I didn’t even know he was out there. These stats don’t reflect special teams, but it is worth calling out that he had 3 tackles on special teams.

title: Jerry Jeudy, Denzel Boston’s reps signal a chance: Browns offensive snap counts
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ offense struggled in the first half, but not due to quarterback play. They shot themselves in the foot with procedural errors or penalties. Late in the second half, they were only 1-of-9 on third downs, consistently being in long third down situations. But on the final drive, with a bunch of manageable […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 20: Baker Mayfield #6 of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers congratulates Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns after the game at Raymond James Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns’ offense struggled in the first half, but not due to quarterback play. They shot themselves in the foot with procedural errors or penalties. Late in the second half, they were only 1-of-9 on third downs, consistently being in long third down situations. But on the final drive, with a bunch of manageable situations, they went 4-of-4 to finish a respectable 5-of-13 on third down. This is stuff to build on, giving a glimpse of maybe, just maybe, Deshaun Watson being serviceable to this offense after all. Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on offense for the Cleveland Browns ’ Week 2 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Quarterback Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats QB Deshaun Watson 58 100% 24-of-30 (80%) for 238 yards, 2 TD. 7 carries, 22 yards (3.1 YPC). In what I’ll deem to be his best game as a member of the Browns, QB Deshaun Watson seemed to do everything right. He completed 80% of his passes, didn’t turn the ball over, was accurate, and succeeded with pressure in his face. According to Pro Football Focus, he was the team’s highest-graded offensive player with an 88.8. What we said about Watson before still holds true. He is in the unique position where, yes, it makes sense to give leeway to a guy who is coming off of two Achilles’ injuries as needing to get back into a rhythm. However, he also gets less leeway because we saw a bad product from him consistently prior to that. If this is the start of a turnaround, it’s up to him to continue making that happen. Running Back Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats RB Quinshon Judkins 39 67% 12 carries, 21 yards (1.8 YPC). 5 catches, 27 yards (5 targets). RB Raheim Sanders 11 19 2 carries, 4 yards (2.0 YPC). 1 catch, 7 yards (1 target). FB Michael Burton 10 17 No stats registered. RB Jaleel McLaughlin 8 14 1 carry, 3 yards (3.0 YPC). The Browns’ running game needs to get going. Todd Monken was asked about it on Monday, and said it hasn’t been good enough. Nonetheless, Quinshon Judkins still got a solid grade from PFF, in part due to his receptions and decent pass blocking grade. Browns HC Todd Monken on lethargic run game: 'We are what the statistics bear out. Gotta scheme it better, coach it better, block it better. It's not good enough.' — Tony Grossi (@TonyGrossi) September 21, 2026 With Dylan Sampson out, instead of giving Raheim Sanders an increased load, those backup reps were split between he and Jaleel McLaughlin . Wide Receiver Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats WR Denzel Boston 54 93% 5 catches, 95 yards (7 targets), 1 TD. WR KC Concepcion 38 66% 6 catches, 28 yards (6 targets). 1 carry, -6 yards (-6.0 YPC). WR Jerry Jeudy 34 59% 0 catches (1 target). WR Tylan Wallace 14 24% No stats registered. WR Isaiah Bond 4 7% 1 catch, 10 yards (1 target). Here we were talking up KC Concepcion all of training camp and the preseason, and its Denzel Boston who has taken over the team. He led the team in receiving reps and had the breakaway touchdown for Cleveland. You can see how Watson likes throwing to a big target like him, giving him that degree of trust with his radius. Boston was the third-highest graded player on offense by PFF, with a grade of 69.8. You can see how Jerry Jeudy’s role has diminished, as he only played 59% of the snaps, third highest on the team. Jeudy slipped coming out of his break on his one target. To his credit, he helped with a block on the touchdown to Blake Whiteheart . Tylan Wallace received 25% of the receiving snaps for the second straight week. Isaiah Bond only played four snaps, but caught one pass for a first down. Tight End Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats TE Harold Fannin 50 86% 5 catches, 54 yards (6 targets). TE Blake Whiteheart 27 47% 1 catch, 17 yards (2 targets), 1 TD. TE Carsen Ryan 1 2% No stats registered. We got some more involvement from Harold Fannin this week, and he continues to be a load to try to bring down. The Browns were going to have him take a snap on a quarterback tush push, but the Browns false started. For blocking, Fannin’s grades continue to be no good. Blake Whiteheart had a solid day in the blocking department, though, so they balance each other out a little. Offensive Line Pos Player Plays % Snaps Stats OL Spencer Fano 58 100% OL Elgton Jenkins 58 100% OL Austin Barber 58 100% OL Zion Johnson 58 100% OL Tytus Howard 56 97% OL Dawand Jones 2 3% This was not the best day for Tytus Howard , who had some penalties and also appeared to yield at least one sack. He was the team’s lowest-graded pass blocker this week, and was even worse in the run blocking department. Spencer Fano had a nice second game, grading out to a 72.9 by PFF (second-highest on offense). He received high marks in both pass and run blocking. Overall, the guards ( Zion Johnson , 48.4 and Austin Barber , 47.0) received poor grades from PFF too. However, Barber did extremely well in pass blocking, but was lackluster in run blocking. The same goes for Johnson overall.

title: AFC North Week 2: Is anyone actually really good? Bengals undefeated, but with holes
summary: Playing QB Baker Mayfield has paid off twice for teams in the AFC North, with the Cleveland Browns taking the victory in Week 2 as their former quarterback threw an interception and overthrew a number of receivers throughout the game. The Cincinnati Bengals knocked off Mayfield in Week 1, forcing four turnovers, including three fumbles […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) speaks with New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough (6) after the game at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Playing QB Baker Mayfield has paid off twice for teams in the AFC North, with the Cleveland Browns taking the victory in Week 2 as their former quarterback threw an interception and overthrew a number of receivers throughout the game. The Cincinnati Bengals knocked off Mayfield in Week 1, forcing four turnovers, including three fumbles from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback . Cleveland has a lot to build on going into Week 3, despite being a home underdog , but the official AFC playoff standings have the Browns at the bottom of the AFC North due to tiebreakers. That doesn’t mean the division looks good overall. Bengals winning despite… … an offense that just can’t get on track in general. Mayfield handed Cincinnati the game in Week 1, and the Bengals offense continued to struggle, outside of a few chunk plays, in Week 2: 2nd-lowest dropback success rate in a game in Burrow's career (per NGS)! but Burrow did a great job of extending plays and pushing the ball. So the the explosives (7 of them!) offset that lack of efficiency. Exactly how you should try to go at that Texans defense. https://t.co/DplQ53LVOj — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 21, 2026 Given their starts to the season, beating the Houston Texans and Bucs back-to-back is not as impressive as it might have seemed before the season started. The Bengals sit at the top of the division, led by their defense. Who would have thought that would happen? Can it sustain? Will the offense come together? The Pittsburgh Steelers have been horrible on offense Another team carried by their defense and a weak schedule, the Steelers saw QB Aaron Rodgers throw his coaches under the bus in Week 2. That might be a record, even for Rodgers. The Mike McCarthy-led Pittsburgh offense is just horrendous: 2026 has given us the two lowest Total EPA offenses to start a season since 2022, per @SumerSports The Falcons (-54.58) and Steelers (-51.59) now rank last and second to last respectively — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) September 20, 2026 That tweet is notable because the only reason the Steelers have a victory is that they played the somehow worse Atlanta Falcons (in a close game, mind you) in Week 1. Who are the Baltimore Ravens? In Week 1, the Ravens controlled the Indianapolis Colts on the road, a team that gave the Kansas City Chiefs a tough game on Monday Night Football, only to lose to the New Orleans Saints at home. A review of the game doesn’t show a huge flaw, big picture, but just not enough explosive plays on offense with WR Zay Flowers out of the contest. RB Derrick Henry had just 68 yards on 16 carries (a fine 4.3 average), while QB Lamar Jackson completed just 21 of 31 for 235 yards, with one touchdown and one interception. Jackson only ran for 34 yards on just four carries in Week 2. The Saints won the contest despite barely being able to run the ball, with QB Tyler Shough carrying the load as a passer, completing 27 of 34 passes for 252 yards and one touchdown. Shough also ran for a score. The Bengals are undefeated, but no one is crowning them as a great team at this point. The Steelers look putrid on offense and could fall apart quickly with an aging roster. The Ravens lost their main explosive player to an injury, and WR Jakobi Lane as well. summary: The Dallas Cowboys got their first win of the season against the Washington Commanders, with Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb leading the offense.
