There is still work to do defensively, particularly with tackling and finishing opportunities in […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys linebackers Jaishawn Barham (55) and Donovan Ezeiruaku (6) celebrate with defensive tackle Kenny Clark (97) and cornerback DaRon Bland (26) after a defensive play against the Washington Commanders during the first half at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys got their first win of the season against the Washington Commanders, with Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb leading the offense. Among the rookies, Jaishawn Barham provided the biggest moment, while Caleb Downs contributed on defense and special teams. There is still work to do defensively, particularly with tackling and finishing opportunities in the backfield. But here is how each rookie who played fared this week, listed in draft order, and any undrafted players worth noting after that. Caleb Downs (Tackles: 9 | TFL: 0 | Sacks: 0 | INT: 0 | PD: 1 | Special teams: 2 tackles, 1 forced fumble) Downs contributed in two phases, including a breakup on a pass intended for Terry McLaurin. His special-teams production added value beyond his defensive duties. The forced fumble did not produce a Dallas recovery, but it was another opportunity created by the rookie showing his playmaking skills on defense. Malachi Lawrence (Tackles: 1 | TFL: 0 | Sacks: 0 | INT: 0 | PD: 0 | QB hits: 1) Lawrence reached Marcus Mariota for a quarterback hit, although Washington completed the pass for 18 yards. That captures the distinction between affecting the quarterback and ending the play. The contact was encouraging, but Dallas still surrendered a substantial gain, and in Lawrence’s defense, there was a lot of “almost” moments by the entire Cowboys pass rush unit and not a single sack by any of them. Jaishawn Barham (Tackles: 7 | TFL: 1 | Sacks: 0 | INT: 0 | PD: 0 | Pressures: 1 | Forced fumbles: 1) Barham was the standout rookie this week. He started at middle linebacker and wore the green dot, taking responsibility for communicating the defensive calls and getting teammates aligned, and looked comfortable doing it. His biggest contribution came with Dallas protecting a seven-point third-quarter lead by creating a forced fumble recovered by Dee Winters, which gave the offense a short field and helped set up another Jake Ferguson touchdown. There is still plenty to work on with Barham, his day included a crucial missed tackle, but Barham handled a considerable assignment in only his second NFL appearance. His communication earned praise from veteran teammates, and he supplied the kind of turnover that can change a close game. Drew Shelton Shelton participated and reported as an eligible extra blocker. There’s nothing else more to report on his performance. LT Overton (Tackles: 1 | TFL: 0 | Sacks: 0 | INT: 0 | PD: 0 | QB hits: 0) Overton’s tackle limited a second-quarter run to one yard. That was a useful contribution against the run, although his recorded production offered little evidence of a disruptive afternoon overall.

title: Cowboys offense provides fireworks while the defense is still a little leaky
summary: Divisional games are always a battle, so watching the Dallas Cowboys come away with a 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders should feel good, even if it was a little ugly at times. The Cowboys needed a good rebound game after a shaky performance last week, and they got it. Bravo? Even with the win, […]
full_text: Divisional games are always a battle, so watching the Dallas Cowboys come away with a 37-20 win over the Washington Commanders should feel good, even if it was a little ugly at times. The Cowboys needed a good rebound game after a shaky performance last week, and they got it. Bravo? Even with the win, it’s hard to know how we should feel about this game, so today we’re going to look closer at things to get a better sense of how this group played. Let’s run through some things that stood out on Sunday. Prescott was dealing The passing game was great thanks to Dak Prescott. He finished 26 of 31 for 279 yards with four touchdowns and no picks. He finished with a passer rating of 143.7, his highest mark since the regular-season finale trouncing of the Eagles back in 2022. The great thing about Prescott’s play is he had some easy stuff drawn up for him with some nifty play designs to get receivers open, but he also made some difficult, spot-on throws to receivers in tighter coverage. He also made good decisions with his feet, running at the right moments, although it still made fans hold their breath considering how many quarterbacks were getting hurt across the league on Sunday. Prescott was dialed in, spreading the ball around and making all the right decisions. It was great to see, and it was only fitting that this performance allowed him to pass Tony Romo for the all-time record in passing touchdowns in franchise history. Well done, QB1. Running game troubles The only blemish in an otherwise great performance from the offense was their inability to run the ball. Javonte Williams never got anything started as he was met in the backfield on what felt like every other play. The interior offensive line could not get any push, and you cannot help but wonder how much they are missing Tyler Smith, who continues to miss games while recovering from thumb surgery. Adding to the issue is that they routinely forgot to block the edge defender. Washington repeatedly snuck in extra run attackers along the edge, and the Cowboys left those guys unattended, allowing them to crash in and blow up the run behind the line of scrimmage. Give the Commanders credit. They were strong in the trenches, particularly Javon Kinlaw. The veteran defensive tackle consistently won at the point of attack, moving blockers and shutting down running lanes. And safety Nick Cross was an effective run-blitzer. There just wasn’t much room for runners to run. The only good thing about the lack of a rushing attack is that Brian Schottenheimer opted to move away from it rather than continuing to run negative plays. That doesn’t make the problem go away, but it is a nice mitigation tactic, so give him credit for adjusting. The bootlegs and play-action were plenty effective with the Commanders always so focused on attacking the run. The offense kept throwing the ball despite the game script practically screaming at them to run it. Quietly doing his job The run-blocking needs serious work, but the pass-blocking is holding up well. Specifically, Tyler Guyton is quietly putting together a great start to the season. He was the subject of endless scrutiny this summer to the point where he was supposedly in a roster battle for his job, but he has since silenced any doubters. He did a great job in his pass protection assignments, allowing Prescott a clean, comfortable pocket to operate from. Not every first-round lineman the team drafts turns into an immediate All-Pro, but Guyton’s progress is super encouraging. He could still be on that path, even if his route is turning out to be a little more scenic. Thank goodness for DB depth It was just a few weeks ago when we couldn’t determine which safeties were going to make final roster cuts because the team was so deep with talent. Fortunately, the front office hung on to that depth, because it did not take long for them to need every single bit of it. They were already playing without starting free safety Malik Hooker, who suffered a fractured forearm in the opener last week. His replacement, P.J. Locke, only lasted three plays before suffering a non-contact foot injury. Fortunately, the defense still had rookie Caleb Downs, free agent Jalen Thompson, and special teams sub Markquese Bell to hold things down. Downs had a few moments where he made rookie mistakes, but he gets splashier and splashier with each new game. Additionally, starting cornerback Cobie Durant suffered a hamstring injury, forcing the team to call upon second-year player Shavon Revel Jr. to fill the void. While the young cornerback still has some moments to clean up, he also did a great job riding receivers toward the sideline. Three times in this game he used the boundary perfectly, and all three instances resulted in incompletions. Linebacker play The team was also without starter DeMarvion Overshown, who injured his hamstring last week. This put more of the workload on rookie Jaishawn Barham and new acquisition Dee Winters. There were moments where Barham looked a bit overaggressive and overran the play, or Winters was stiff-armed out of the play, but there were also times where both stepped up and shut things down. Ultimately, they combined on the biggest defensive play of the afternoon when Barham forced a fumble, and Winters pounced on it. Weakness or tightening? You can easily paint a narrative that the defense was still allowing opposing offenses to march down the field at will. In seven of the Commanders’ nine possessions, they moved the ball to the Dallas 36-yard line or better. That is a lot of chances to give up points, and Washington racked up almost 400 yards of offense. But you can also make a strong case that the defense tightened up when it mattered. Washington only managed to score two touchdowns. There were two clear scoring opportunities where the Commanders walked away with absolutely zero points. Granted they had some self-inflicted mishaps that hurt their chances, but the Cowboys didn’t let them off the hook. People will point to that unfortunate incident on the last play of the first half, but don’t forget the two plays before that. Washington had chances to punch the ball in from the one-yard line, but the defense forced two straight incompletions from Jayden Daniels. The defense also forced a three-and-out to open the game and a quick turnover midway through the third quarter that completely changed the momentum. These are good things that the defense deserves credit for. QB containment is still a thing The defense struggled mightily to bring the quarterback down. The pressure was inconsistent, sometimes getting close, other times allowing the quarterback to have all day. In every instance, they could never quite finish the play with a sack. Even knowing it is a strength of Washington’s offense, the front seven failed to keep the quarterback in the pocket. The QB kept eluding defenders and churning out big gains on the ground. Watching the game closely, there were some instances where Daniels was very decisive and very fast, and sometimes you have to just recognize the other team has great players too, so it wasn’t as egregious as it initially appeared. It’s still something to be mindful of. While last week the defense was burned by designed runs, on Sunday it came from pure improvisation because the defense was not equipped to make stops in space. The good news is the team will be moving to a stretch of games against quarterbacks with far less mobility soon. The bad news is they have Lamar Jackson coming up next, so it might get a little worse before it gets better. Special teams shout-out We always talk about the special teams when they do poorly, so it is only fair that we give them props when they show out. Brandon Aubrey was fantastic. Yes, he did have that one squib kick that fell short of the landing zone, which gave Washington great field position, but he also had a few others that the returner struggled to handle cleanly. Honestly, it is impressive what…

But yet, I think it put such insurmountable belief in my head that I can accomplish whatever I want to accomplish,” Prescott said after the game . “And any thought that I said or anything that I wanted to do, and I mentioned it and I said it out loud, I had a mom and I had brothers who poured gas on those thoughts, who told me I could.” Download the SB Nation app today! CeeDee Lamb was offended by the Commanders before putting up a monstrous performance for the Dallas Cowboys in Week 2 – Mauricio Rodriguez, A to Z Sports The Cowboys aren’t backing down from the expectations on offense, wanting to set the tone with this veteran, experienced group. There’s plenty to unpack from Sunday’s game, but it starts with what Lamb said after the final whistle. The star wide receiver had a monster day with 153 receiving yards and two touchdowns from quarterback Dak Prescott. The Commanders simply could not stop him. His message? The Commanders offended the Cowboys right from the get go by their decision to defer after winning the coin toss. “Honestly, personally, I just kind of take it offensive that they want to put our offense out first, like we’re not who we are,” Lamb told reporters. Jerry Jones: I was worried what it would be like if Cowboys started 0-2 – Michael David Smith, Pro Football Talk The Cowboys avoided 0-2, but can they avoid being 1-2 for the third year in a row in Brazil? “It would’ve been hard to walk down here and talk to y’all tonight 0-2,” Jones said. “ I really was worried about what it was going to be like if we did end up 0-2. I can’t say that I was a color of strength in my mentality coming into the game because I’ve got a lot of respect for the coaching over on the Washington Commanders side. Having said all of that, this was a very important win for us, important to these guys who put the work in, the coaching staff, for Brian, and I’m really proud of them.” Report Card: Cowboys grades improve across board in Week 2 win – Terence Watson, The Cowboys Wire The Cowboys need to get their run game going still, where they miss Tyler Smith at left guard a lot. Taking everything into account, the offense is starting to resemble the group Dallas fielded in 2025. However, struggles at center limited the unit’s effectiveness throughout the game. This offensive line misses Tyler Smith, and his absence appears to be affecting Cooper Beebe both as a run blocker and in pass protection. It was one of Beebe’s roughest performances since joining the team, earning an initial 37.8 pass-blocking grade and a 55.6 run-blocking grade from PFF .

title: Dak Prescott was at his best on Sunday
summary: After a demoralizing loss in Week 1, the Dallas Cowboys needed a bounce-back performance on Sunday against the Washington Commanders. Despite this matchup only being the second of the year for the teams, it truly felt like a must-win for both sides.  Thankfully for the Cowboys, they came out and looked like the better team […]
full_text: After a demoralizing loss in Week 1, the Dallas Cowboys needed a bounce-back performance on Sunday against the Washington Commanders. Despite this matchup only being the second of the year for the teams, it truly felt like a must-win for both sides. Thankfully for the Cowboys, they came out and looked like the better team from the jump, leading to a 37-20 victory. While Dallas’ defense did show some marginal improvements, their offense was the star of the show. A few players on the offense put together performances that stood out, but none were more impressive than quarterback Dak Prescott. Dallas’ signal-caller played one of the most productive games of his career, earning him the Week 2game ball award. On the day, Prescott completed 26 of 31 passes for 279 passing yards and four touchdowns. The 33-year-old was in complete control from the opening snap, recording a remarkable 143.8 Passer Rating to go with a 91.1 Pro Football Focus offensive grade. His fourth-quarter touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb helped Prescott make some history, giving him more touchdown passes than any other quarterback in Cowboys franchise history. Dak Prescott has more touchdown passes than any other QB in Cowboys franchise history (Via @dallascowboys ) pic.twitter.com/4px29CreXX — 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) September 20, 2026 Prescott was arguably the most productive quarterback in the NFL in Week 2. He led the league in CPOE (18.0) and Success Rate (65.8%) and was second in EPA/Play (0.459) and Adj EPA/Play (0.459). Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott generated +17.9 EPA across his dropbacks against Washington, the most among any quarterback who faced a pressure rate north of 40% in a game over the last two seasons. Dak was 17/18 for 178 yards and all 4 of his TDs when kept clean. All 4 of his… pic.twitter.com/D2aIJfWVse — RJ Ochoa (@rjochoa) September 21, 2026 Dak Prescott with an ABSOLUTE MISSILE to CeeDee Lamb 🚀 (via @dallascowboys ) pic.twitter.com/1b4N92IJBq — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) September 20, 2026 If the Cowboys’ quarterback is playing the way he did on Sunday, it’s going to be hard for any team to keep Dallas’ offense in check. If the defense can get anywhere close to league-average, with Prescott looking like a true MVP candidate, the Cowboys could be a legit contender to make a deep playoff run.
author: Matthew Holleran

title: Cowboys vs. Commanders Stock Report: Dak Prescott and offense up, defense still shaky
summary: The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Sunday. When this is true the other things that surround it are much easier to deal with. There will only be 16 winners in the NFL this week and that Dallas is one of them is what matters the most. But just because you win does not […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 20: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer looks on against the Washington Commanders during the second half of an NFL football game at AT&T Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys won a football game on Sunday. When this is true the other things that surround it are much easier to deal with. There will only be 16 winners in the NFL this week and that Dallas is one of them is what matters the most. But just because you win does not mean that everything went perfectly in the process. This was clearly the case for Dallas and that is represented by our stock report following the win over Washington. Stock Up: Dak Prescott We have to lead with the record-setter, and in case you somehow missed it Dak Prescott became the franchise’s all-time leader in passing touchdowns during this game. He entered three behind Tony Romo (248) and now has 249 total and counting. Next Gen Stats noted that Prescott generated +17.9 EPA across his dropbacks in this game, the most among any quarterback who has faced a pressure rate above 40% in a given game over the last two seasons. This is truly elite territory here. What’s more is that Dak is pushing the envelope. All four of his touchdowns traveled at least 10 yards downfield in the air, tied for his career-high. Pretty impressive stuff. Stock Up: Brian Schottenheimer When the quarterback plays well that means that the offensive play-caller is doing something right, so Brian Schottenheimer deserves credit as well. What’s more is that Schotty came off of the start line in fifth gear. It was clear that the Cowboys wanted to set the tempo in a way that they failed to do so against the Giants and they certainly accomplished that on offense. It is also worth noting that there were few silly or avoidable penalties from the team overall, something that was of concern following how the Cowboys played in the opener. Schotty clearly got through to them. Stock Up: CeeDee Lamb CeeDee Lamb finished the game with over 150 yards receiving and a pair of touchdowns. That is a solid day’s work if I have ever seen one. All of the George Pickens fanfare throughout training camp (justified fanfare to be clear) really made people kind of forget who Lamb is and what he is capable of. Nobody will forget any time soon. Stock Up: Jake Ferguson We have often said that when players like Lamb and Pickens are drawing so much coverage that someone else has to take advantage of that benefit. That person was clearly Jake Ferguson in this game. Ferguson “only” had four receptions, but half of them were scores. He could have arguably had another if Prescott had found him before a Cowboys field goal, something the broadcast talked about as they showed Dak realizing that himself while looking at the tablet on the sidelines. Having a tight end with such a high level of comfort in the middle of the field is a huge positive, and Dallas absolutely has that in Ferguson these days. Stock Up: T.J. Bass It bears repeating that T.J. Bass is playing very well in Tyler Smith’s absence. I know that many people assumed he would handle his own, but an assumption hardly guarantees anything. We have now gone two straight weeks to start the season where Bass has more than delivered. He deserves serious props given that he did not know he was going to be starting right up until the first week of the season. Stock Up: Tyler Guyton On the subject of offensive linemen who deserve love, how about Tyler Guyton? Back when the Cowboys arrived to training camp he was in contention for the weakest point on an offense that we had high hopes for. In fact, some likely said that he was potentially going to be the reason that they did not realize their full potential. Two weeks into the season, that has not been the case. Guyton is playing like a tried and true left tackle in the NFL, one who is worthy of a first-round pick. Stock Up: Jaishawn Barham It is no secret that Jaishawn Barham had a rough time last week. Following the Cowboys loss a clip of him and Christian Parker talking on the sidelines against New York went viral and all sorts of assumptions were leapt to. The Cowboys noted that they still believed in Barham and doubled down on that by having him wear the green dot in this game . Let’s be clear that the Cowboys defense has a lot of work to do and improvement to make, but Barham got the plane off of the ground, through the air travel, and to its destination in one piece. He also had a huge fumble that allowed the Cowboys to really break the game open. For this being his second game in his professional career, it sure was something. Stock Up: Caleb Downs If we ranked Cowboys players by the height of their floors then Caleb Downs might be number one. He is so reliable, so dependable, and good for consistency all throughout games. This one was special as we saw him lay some serious wood as well as playing in coverage. The biggest issue with Downs these days is that he is simply one human being. The Cowboys can only play him at one spot at a time, but wherever it is, it is taken care of as well as it can be. Stock Down: DaRon Bland The Cowboys defense played pretty poorly in this game. The startling thing is it could have been, and arguably should have been, a lot worse . Maybe you agree with Dyami Brown’s catch not being ruled a touchdown, but even if you do you can see how that could potentially go the other way. Terry McLaurin couldn’t reel in what looked like an easy pass off of a trick play. Early on Jayden Daniels had a man all the way downtown against the Cowboys but just overthrew him. Seemingly play after play, Cowboys defenders, specifically secondary ones, were getting beat and beaten badly. DaRon Bland is who he is relative to the Cowboys and they are sort of stuck in that spot, but goodness he is sort of hurting them in a serious way right now. This team needs corners badly. Stock Down: Christian Parker It is difficult to say that Christian Parker’s stock is “down” relative to last week because it was about as low as it can be. From Game 1 to Game 2 I suppose you could argue he even improved in a vacuum, but we are talking about going from an F to an F+ here. Consider that the Cowboys have played 16 defensive possessions so far this season. The New York Giants managed to infiltrate the Cowboys’ 40-yard line on six of their seven, and the Washington Commanders crossed that territory on seven of their nine. The Cowboys have allowed opposing offenses to get into field goal range on 13 of these 16 possessions! It is early in his career, he is still figuring it out, and all of that jazz, but that is in no way an excuse. The Cowboys clearly have an offense that can lead to the team accomplishing some serious things, but if the defense can’t even hold their own on the other side then it is going to be a disaster similar to last year.

title: Field concerns surround Cowboys, Ravens game in Brazil
summary: In case you forgot, this is a unique week for the Dallas Cowboys. title: Dak Prescott’s record breaking day paces Cowboys to first home win
summary: For the third straight season, the Dallas Cowboys are 1-1 after two games, getting here with their third straight win against the Washington Commanders. Sunday was also the second straight home game against the Commanders where Washington’s starting quarterback Jayden Daniels was replaced by Marcus Mariota due to injury. Daniels was injured on the final […]
full_text: For the third straight season, the Dallas Cowboys are 1-1 after two games, getting here with their third straight win against the Washington Commanders. Sunday was also the second straight home game against the Commanders where Washington’s starting quarterback Jayden Daniels was replaced by Marcus Mariota due to injury. Daniels was injured on the final play of the first half, with the Commanders threatening on three straight goal-to-go plays to tie the game down 17-10. The double-whammy of not getting any points out of this sequence and losing their starter for the rest of the game proved too much for the visitors to overcome, as the Cowboys won the second half 20-10. Brandon Aubrey’s 60-yard field goal to make it a three-score cushion in the fourth quarter gave the Cowboys 30 points in a home game for the first time since last Thanksgiving, the highpoint of that 2025 season when they beat the Kansas City Chiefs for the second to last win of that season – the last win coming at the Commanders weeks later on Christmas. Dallas wasn’t done being aggressive with the ball in their hands just yet though, as Prescott threw a fourth touchdown to surpass Tony Romo in the Dallas record books for the most passing touchdowns in franchise history. The record-breaking throw was a beauty to CeeDee Lamb for his second touchdown of the game. This was Lamb’s first two touchdown game since Week 8 of 2024 at the San Francisco 49ers, and most receiving yards since the year prior in Week 17 against the Lions with 227. The Cowboys have now put themselves in an uber-familiar position of facing a week three swing game against a quality opponent with a 1-1 record, and this time it will come in Brazil against the Baltimore Ravens. There will be so much to say about that as the week goes on, but let’s start with some notes on this win against Dan Quinn and the Commanders. One thing that was noticeable on the Cowboys opening drive, which ended in a touchdown as opposed to last week’s controversial three-and-out, was more reduced splits out wide and somewhat tighter formations. This came after Dallas did not get much of anything going all night spreading it out against the Giants. Following a miscommunication on a deep throw incomplete for George Pickens, Prescott hit Lamb for 15 yards, Lamb again down the middle for 23 yards off play-action (lined up on the opposite side of the formation this time), and then four plays later Lamb again off another play-action for a touchdown. We’ll get to the Cowboys defense which had it’s highs and lows within this game, but this battle of division foes was decided by how well both teams dictated matchups on offense to get their best players against linebackers, safeties, or corners that could be tested. The Cowboys did some encouraging things here in a bounce back performance for Brian Schottenheimer dialing up the plays to grab the lead, play from ahead, and never look back. Not only did Lamb have two touchdowns, but Jake Ferguson did as well as the Cowboys exploited a matchup we said coming in they had a chance to , throwing behind the Commanders’ linebackers. Ferguson’s first touchdown came out of an interesting look. Running back Emari Demercado motioned out wide to draw a cornerback in coverage, but remained at the line of scrimmage as a checkdown option. Luke Schoonmaker was in the slot, and Ferguson ran open down the seam for six. The Cowboys’ multiple tight end sets may not look like many of the other ones used around the league a whole lot right now, but this was a creative way to use two tight ends and a different running back to throw a look at the Commanders. In between the Lamb and Ferguson touchdowns, the Cowboys defense held the Commanders to a field goal after giving up a 3rd-and-18 off a miscommunication between Marquese Bell and DaRon Bland, plus a missed tackle by Dee Winters on a Daniels scramble. Following the Ferguson touchdown to go up 17-3 though, the defense could not respond to really keep the game firmly in the home team’s control. This time it was Bland and rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham, starting at the MIKE for DeMarvion Overshown and wearing the green dot, mixing up a coverage and ending up in the same spot, abandoning the middle of the field. Daniels again took advantage of the rush lane for a big gain on the ground, followed by Rachaad White making a chunk play on the ground when Quinnen Williams tried a pass rush move and completely lost his gap. A Jalen Thompson personal foul tacked 15 yards onto this 14-yard run by White, and two plays later the Commanders were within 17-10 on Stefon Diggs’ touchdown. Dallas was in man for this red zone play, and Washington used motion to force Caleb Downs to come all the way across the field and try to undercut Diggs at the pylon, which he was unable to do to prevent the score. The stretches of better defense were not as long as the AT&T Stadium crowd probably hoped for in this game, but there were small flashes of what the Cowboys defense under Christian Parker could be at it’s best. At times the zone drops had much better structure to them and eye discipline, plays were made in man coverage, and linebackers were able to read and react to get to the ball. Speaking of linebackers doing just that, Barham and Winters combined for the biggest splash play of the game for the defense in the third quarter. The teams traded field goals in the second half to keep the Cowboys’ lead at just seven points, but then Barham forced a fumble coming downhill for a big hit on a throwback screen pass. Winters came up with the recovery, the Cowboys had their best starting field position of the game set up at the Commanders’ 13, and in two plays Ferguson was behind the Washington zone again for a two score lead at 27-13. Considering the fact Barham was drafted for both his ability to play middle linebacker and pass rush on the outside, it shouldn’t go without noting the Cowboys just won a game with this rookie third-round pick stepping into the full time middle linebacker role. Barham was far from perfect, but the hustle that was absent in Week 1was there, and he was good enough for the Cowboys to win the pass catchers versus linebacker matchups that decide big play differential in a huge way, and in turn decide games as a result. This was the turning point in the game for the Cowboys being able to turn up the pressure defensively, although they got just one sack on Marcus Mariota that was negated by a Bland penalty. Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeuriaku, and even Kenny Clark from the interior were felt much more than last week in pass rush though, and made life hard for the Commanders backup QB. Seeing more of these rushes get home for the sack is easily the next thing to look for in signs of progress from the defense. When it comes to playing with the lead on offense, the critique here would be more positive gains in the run game. The Cowboys did run it four straight times prior to Prescott’s record touchdown to Lamb to ice the game at 37-20, but the volume at which they had to continuously throw was concerning at the same time. Prescott did have his highest completion percentage in a game since Week 18 of 2024 at 83.9%, doing so with nine yards per attempt which was also his most since beating the Eagles at home in last year’s 21-0 comeback game. The Cowboys’ 37 points are second only to the Buffalo Bills on Thursday night in a week two that saw defenses make the adjustments to a historically high-scoring week one. The fact Dallas did so while still leaving the game feeling like they can clean up a whole lot offensively to be better is encouraging, with the same going for improvements on defense – which will likely need to come quickly against the Ravens.
author: Sean Martin

title: 5 key plays that sealed the Cowboys’ first win of 2026
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are finally in the win column. After an opening-week disappointment, the offense delivered the explosive performance many expected, powering a 37-20 home win over the Washington Commanders. Dak Prescott was outstanding, completing 26 of 31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns while becoming the franchise’s all-time leader in career passing TDs. […]
full_text: The Dallas Cowboys are finally in the win column. After an opening-week disappointment, the offense delivered the explosive performance many expected, powering a 37-20 home win over the Washington Commanders. Dak Prescott was outstanding, completing 26 of 31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns while becoming the franchise’s all-time leader in career passing TDs. CeeDee Lamb led the way with eight catches for 153 yards and two scores, including a contested touchdown over Commanders cornerback Mike Sainristil that served as the exclamation point. Questions remain on defense, particularly against mobile quarterbacks and on third downs, but Dallas’ offense clicked on all cylinders while Washington repeatedly beat itself. The three-score victory hinged on a handful of pivotal plays that could have flipped the outcome. Here are five that decided the game. Jacory Croskey-Merritt’s toss play stalls a promising drive Even with a 10-0 lead, Washington showed early life. Jayden Daniels found a rhythm, mixing accurate throws with back-breaking runs. After converting a third-and-18 with a connection to Terry McLaurin, Daniels scrambled 18 yards to get Washington in the red zone. Two plays later, running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt couldn’t corral an errant Jayden Daniels’ pitch, resulting in a 13-yard loss that killed the drive. Washington settled for a field goal, and the momentum stayed with Dallas. Dan Quinn passes on points The game’s decisive swing came at the end of the second quarter. Trailing 17-10, the Commanders drove deep into Dallas territory. Daniels scrambled effectively (including a big run on the drive), and Washington reached first-and-goal at the 1 with 12 seconds remaining. Most expected at least a field goal to cut the deficit to four. Instead, Quinn went for the touchdown. Cobie Durant blanketed McLaurin on first down. Daniels threw the ball away on second down to save time. On third down, Daniels stumbled after getting stepped on by a lineman coming out from under center, injured his non-throwing elbow in the process, and flung a desperation underhanded incomplete pass as the half ended. The Cowboys escaped without surrendering points. Daniels was carted off and ruled out; the injury is expected to sideline him for a significant time. Washington also wasted a lengthy drive and the chance to receive the second-half kickoff with a chance to take the lead. Officials wipe a potential tying touchdown off the board Without Daniels to open the third quarter, Washington still answered the challenge. A kickoff penalty gave them excellent field position at their own 40, and they quickly marched into the red zone looking to tie the game. On second-and-9 from the Dallas 29, Marcus Mariota hit Dyami Brown on a pass that looked like a touchdown. Brown appeared to secure the ball with his knee down in bounds. Officials ruled it incomplete on the field. Multiple replays suggested a catch, but the call stood after review. Washington settled for a field goal, and Dallas kept the lead. Rookie Jaishawn Barham rips the ball free at the perfect time Dallas’ defense had struggled to capitalize on takeaways the previous week. This time they delivered when it counted. After trading field goals, the Commanders were still within a score and tried to exploit Dallas’ aggression with a wide-receiver screen to Brown. Rookie linebacker Jaishawn Barham read it perfectly, beat the block, and stripped the ball. Dee Winters was on the spot to recover the loose ball in Commanders territory. Two plays later, Prescott threaded a strike to Jake Ferguson for another touchdown, extending the lead and shifting the game firmly in Dallas’ favor. Antonio Williams’ near-miss to a wide-open McLaurin Terry McLaurin remains Washington’s top playmaker, but the Commanders couldn’t fully utilize him. He was targeted nine times yet finished with just two catches for 50 yards. The most painful miss came on a gadget play. Facing a growing deficit, offensive coordinator David Blough reached deep into the playbook. Mariota lateraled to receiver Antonio Williams, who then threw downfield to a wide-open McLaurin after DaRon Bland lost track of him. The pass forced an awkward adjustment and bounced off McLaurin’s fingertips. A similar trick play on the next play also failed, and a missed field goal effectively ended any realistic comeback hopes.

title: Favorite plays from the Broncos vs. Jaguars game
summary: It’s nice to enjoy the day after. Last week it was still meltdown city the day after, which is typical overreaction to one game many fans go through — especially when the game was as ugly as that one was. Not today, though. While the Denver Broncos couldn’t get out of their own way in […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the second quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s nice to enjoy the day after. Last week it was still meltdown city the day after, which is typical overreaction to one game many fans go through — especially when the game was as ugly as that one was. Not today, though. While the Denver Broncos couldn’t get out of their own way in the first half, they came back and dominated the Jacksonville Jaguars in the second. That brings me to today’s MHR Roundup topic: Favorite plays. My favorite play came during their four-minute offense. It’s rare in the NFL when you see a double-move work this well and it was so good that I initially thought the penalty on the field must have been offensive pass interference because Jaylen Waddle was so damn open. Jaylen Waddle's double-move on his last catch yesterday 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/k9N9Qf7CgO — RG 📷 (@RyanGreeneDNVR) September 21, 2026 No offensive pass interference here. Just two broken ankles. In that situation, the play was important too because it enabled the Broncos to close out the game and shut the door on any potential comeback for Trevor Lawrence. What was your favorite play from Sunday’s game? Let us know in the comments below. Broncos daily recap Broncos rise to occasion; topple Jaguars in hard-fought gridiron battle The Denver Broncos showed toughness and determination in their comeback victory against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos roster and give you stock-ups and stock-downs on every player currently on the 53-man roster. After a bounce-back performance like that on Sunday, we are going to see a lot more stock-ups than we did last week. Should Jonah Coleman be the Broncos’ starting running back? Not only did he look like a veteran player out there, but he also looked like a future starter. Potent quotables Sean Payton On how confident he is in RB Jonah Coleman’s ability to handle a heavier workload if necessary “So yesterday, [RB] RJ [Harvey] was out, and then [RB] J.K. [Dobbins] got nicked up and wasn’t able to finish. None of that today on Monday is at a place where we’re—I think all three of those players we’re discussing can be bell cow, handle a majority of the carries. Yes, I think there’s a lot ahead of us this week relative to who our runners are going to be.” On how long it takes to establish an offensive identity “I think that’s a great question. I think that it has to show itself. There has to be a sense of urgency. We’re going to play in other games where that first half, for instance, won’t get it done. So we have to have that sense of urgency so that it’s clear to everybody, this is who we are. I think that’s something that we’re working on.” On the goal-to-go series and what happened on the third-down play “It wasn’t anything good, cadence-wise, we’re at the 1 [-yard line]. I would say just overall, a real bad possession.” On the impact of the crowd noise forcing Jacksonville to use multiple timeouts “It was significant. Here’s when you see it’s significant. When you see there’s this alignment by a tight end or receiver, the quarterback looks over, tries to… So there’s a communication problem relative to the formation, and twice I saw that right in front of me, and I think that’s one of the plays you’re referencing. So a player lines up in a different spot than the quarterback expects. There’s this, ‘Hey, there’s eight seconds, we’re trying to get it fixed.’ I think our crowd was fantastic yesterday.” On what he saw from the tackling on film “It didn’t have to be a long and exhaustive film study relative to the tackling and enough to where you can’t play winning football when you’re in position and you can’t tackle. It’s one of the three or four most important things you have to do on defense.” On if Offensive Coordinator Davis Webb is settling in and congratulating him at the end of the game “Yes, it was a fist bump. It’s a sign of excitement, and we’re winning the game. To your earlier point, no different than players. We’re trying to get up to speed, improve, [Offensive Coordinator] Davis [Webb] the same way. I think there’s that sense of urgency with everyone in the jobs they have.” On the severity of his back injury and if it’s impacting his day-to-day “No, fair question. So in 2013, I had a [L4-L5], a little disc issue and it was just from too much CrossFit or working out. So that kind of calmed down and then flared up this summer. So I already had the little procedure, which is really like an injection, an epidural injection. So it really can get aggravated when you’re standing for three and a half, four hours. No, there’s no surgery for the back. I’ve got a toe issue. There are some other issues now that are [rickety], but the stress on the back can be relieved if you get into that position. That actually 13 years ago was the first time that area, your 4-5, which was a specific location that can give you more of a radiating pain than a true pain, if that makes any sense.” On if he thinks the team has built traits to compete in close games “I think in a fair response to that, I think there are two things. We know this, that if at the start of the season we’re not addressing maybe some of the things that kept games a year ago close, that analytically speaking, it’s hard to say you’re going to repeat the same call it 11 wins that you had maybe a year ago. Now each game’s different, but I also think there’s a confidence level in a team that because they’ve won before, they’ve been behind before and then how do they respond? So I think on the positive side, it’s that confidence having been here before, and then from a coaching perspective, ‘Hey, how do we find a way to not be in as many one-score games or behind in one-score games going forward?’ There are some specific areas that we outlined. Now that’s a good team we played. That’s a team that we felt on film when you watched them, even in the playoff game last year against Buffalo, that came down to a final drive. So they’ve done a good job there, and I think there was this feeling like that was a good football team and we knew it was going to be a hard-fought game.” Under the radar Fascinating answer from Sean Payton when @ZacStevens asked him about his confidence level in Jonah Coleman being able to handle a bigger workload pic.twitter.com/Ud0PVAzJmo — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) September 21, 2026 Meinerz with a pass pro pancake, backside cut-off on a 0T and another with an epic finish vs a FS 1T! pic.twitter.com/RXIsO4lEhy — Brandon Thorn (@BrandonThornNFL) September 21, 2026 #broncos Bo Nix completed 16/17 passes against four or fewer rushers for 205 yards and a TD yesterday. That's tied for the 2nd-highest completion % when not facing the blitz by any QB since 2025, per @NextGenStats While he did struggle against blitzes, I actually thought this… pic.twitter.com/D277XblFUz — Sam Jane (@sam_jane230) September 21, 2026 Reason why #Broncos have been such a good comeback/4Q team is Bo Nix. He's got that Elway/Tebow trait where he's markedly better when needing to catch up late. 4Q Sunday: Nix 8 of 10, 88 yds, TD, 136.7 RTG Lawrence 1 of 6, 28, 46.5 First 3Q: Jaguars 13-6 4Q: Broncos 14-0 — MikeKlis9NEWS (@mikeklis9news) September 21, 2026 The Feed Post your own thoughts on MHR’s Feed .

title: Broncos RB JK Dobbins is ‘good’ after leaving Sunday’s game with a hamstring injury
summary: According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, a source told him that Denver Broncos running back JK Dobbins is “good” despite leaving Sunday’s game with a hamstring injury. After the game, head coach Sean Payton made it sound like Dobbins hamstring injury was minor, and today, he did not rule out the veteran back for Sunday […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: J.K. Dobbins #27 of the Denver Broncos runs with the ball during the second quarter of the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Matthew Stockman/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to NFL insider Tom Pelissero, a source told him that Denver Broncos running back JK Dobbins is “good” despite leaving Sunday’s game with a hamstring injury. Broncos RB JK Dobbins, who left Sunday's win over the Jaguars with a hamstring injury, is "good", source said. They face the Rams next Sunday night. — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) September 21, 2026 After the game, head coach Sean Payton made it sound like Dobbins hamstring injury was minor, and today, he did not rule out the veteran back for Sunday Night’s game vs. the Los Angeles Rams . Second-year back RJ Harvey missed Sunday’s game due to a hamstring injury, so we will have to keep an eye on the injury report this week. It sounds like both are trending in the right direction for Sunday Night’s game, but we will have to wait and see. With Dobbins having a lengthy injury history, it is good to see that he escaped this without suffering anything serious. Hamstring injuries are also tricky and can be re-aggravated easily, so it’ll be interesting to see if the team plays it safe with him this week. Dobbins made a bet with reporters during camp that he would owe them all drinks if he misses a game, so that could be on the line this week. If Dobbins and/or Harvey are sidelined, or at least limited, the Broncos do have rookie running back Jonah Coleman to lean on if needed. The rookie helped ice the game late in the 4th quarter on Sunday vs. the Jaguars and showed off the talent and high football IQ that the team has praised since he was drafted. Head coach Sean Payton has repeatedly said that Coleman does not feel like a rookie out there, and he repeated that yesterday. Coleman smartly slid inbounds after picking up the first down to keep the clock running despite potentially fighting for more yards and padding his stats. That selfless play will win over coaches and teammates, and he earned real praise from Payton, Nix, and others after yesterday’s comeback victory. At the end of the day, it is great to hear that Dobbins escaped a serious injury and is doing well and still in play for Sunday Night’s game. Same goes for Harvey, who brings a speed and pass-catching element to the Broncos’ backfield. With that said, I still want to see more of Jonah Coleman moving forward, and I think he earned that right with his performance on Sunday.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Should Jonah Coleman be the Broncos’ starting running back?
summary: Entering Sunday’s game, the Broncos were already down second-year running back RJ Harvey, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. This meant rookie running back Jonah Coleman would see an elevated role on offense vs. the Jaguars. He was still behind veteran starter JK Dobbins, who took the majority of the snaps early on, but […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball during the fourth quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Entering Sunday’s game, the Broncos were already down second-year running back RJ Harvey, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. This meant rookie running back Jonah Coleman would see an elevated role on offense vs. the Jaguars. He was still behind veteran starter JK Dobbins, who took the majority of the snaps early on, but he too suffered a hamstring injury and would be sidelined for the remainder of the game. This gave rookie running back Jonah Coleman an opportunity to shine in a big moment, and he did not disappoint. He would enter the game late in the 4th quarter while the Broncos were leading, with a chance to ice the game and kill the clock. This has been a scenario that the Broncos have struggled with and have typically gone three-and-out and had to send their defense back out to close the game. Well, Coleman called game and had multiple big runs for first downs and would smartly slide down inbounds to avoid stopping the clock. Not only did he look like a veteran player out there, but he also looked like a future starter. "That didn't feel like a rookie" 🗣️ Sean Payton PRAISES Jonah Coleman after Broncos win vs Jaguars pic.twitter.com/AUvBwhWTSm — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) September 21, 2026 After the game, head coach Sean Payton told reporters that Coleman played well and that the rookie back did not feel like a rookie out there on Sunday. “He played well. Then the very end, that last carry was… We work on four-minute [situations], but that certainly didn’t feel like a rookie series, if you will. He came up big, and we needed it. You carry three [running backs] on gameday like everyone else. We were down to two and the fullback. Those guys did a good job, and then we found a couple schemes that we liked and stayed with it. His play right at the end, staying in bounds, that was something you cover, but maybe he doesn’t get those same reps in practice. He did a good job.” Payton said Coleman came up big, and he did. He closed that game out for the Broncos, made the Jaguars waste their timeouts, and did not allow Trevor Lawrence and the explosive Jaguars offense to take the field again. That is huge and something the team has struggled to do in the past. Quarterback Bo Nix also praised Coleman’s late-game IQ and told reporters that Coleman does a really good job of paying attention and that he’s really smart and that he has great football IQ. “Jonah played very smart for a young kid, especially at the end there for a minute when everybody knows we’re running the football. He has to protect the football, run in bounds, a lot of things are going through his head while he’s trying to run the ball well. So he did that extremely well, very efficient and then obviously capped it off with the run down the sideline where he slid in bounds and that’s just really good for a young guy. You can tell he does a really good job of paying attention and he’s really smart and he’s got a great football IQ.” A big part of football is trust. Can you trust a player in a big moment to come up with a big play? Nix trusts Courtland Sutton in big moments, and Payton has the players on the roster that he trusts to fill the needed roles on the 53-man roster. A performance like this in a big game and in a key late-game situation likely earned rookie Jonah Coleman some trust from Payton and Nix moving forward. So, with Dobbins and Harvey currently banged up, has Coleman earned the right to be the Broncos’ starting running back? I think as long as Dobbins is healthy, he will be the guy, but Coleman is making a strong case for that job. I don’t think Harvey’s role is in danger, but Coleman is putting everyone on the hot seat, and the reality is, it’s only a matter of time before he takes it. He looked effective in short yardage against a good run defense and scored his first career touchdown; he picked up key first downs, bounced one run outside, and looked explosive in the open field. I want to see more Jonah Coleman moving forward, and I believe a real discussion needs to be had about him becoming the Denver Broncos’ starting running back sooner rather than later.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Sean Payton on Jaylen Waddle: ‘I’m glad he is ours’
summary: 1 catch for 2 yards. That was the stat line for Jaylen Waddle’s debut with the Broncos. His lack of involvement in the offense was curious, and it was a disappointing start to his Broncos career after all the talk and hype this offseason. Well, it appears Waddle was saving his big debut for the […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jaylen Waddle #17 of the Denver Broncos celebrates during the fourth quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images 1 catch for 2 yards. That was the stat line for Jaylen Waddle’s debut with the Broncos. His lack of involvement in the offense was curious, and it was a disappointing start to his Broncos career after all the talk and hype this offseason. Well, it appears Waddle was saving his big debut for the home crowd in Mile High because the Broncos receiver exploded for 8 catches for 138 yards vs. the Jaguars on Sunday. He showed off his big-play ability with a 49-yard reception from quarterback Bo Nix while also making big plays in key moments throughout the game. After the game on Sunday, head coach Sean Payton told reporters: “I am glad he (Waddle) is ours”. "Glad [Jaylen Waddle is] ours!" Sean Payton on Waddle's impact vs the Jaguars 🔥 pic.twitter.com/PrDmLi6rX2 — DNVR Broncos (@DNVR_Broncos) September 21, 2026 Payton added that Waddle’s impact on Sunday’s game was “significant” and that he just got done giving his explosive wide receiver a game ball for his performance. “It was significant. I just gave him a game ball. You can see the explosiveness, the run after the catch, all of those things. I’m glad he’s ours.” Waddle showed off his playmaking ability throughout this one and lived up to the hype we heard all offseason. The Broncos have been lacking a true playmaker like this for years now, and it is exciting to see what Waddle can do from here on out. The players are excited too. Veteran wide receiver Courtland Sutton told reporters after the game that he has been “cheesin” and that he believes that this is just the tip of the iceberg for Waddle . He added that they have more plays in their back pocket for the Broncos’ explosive wide receiver that they haven’t even gotten to yet. Broncos quarterback Bo Nix couldn’t hold back his excitement for Waddle either. During his postgame press conference, he was initially asked about rookie running back Jonah Coleman, but Nix wanted to talk about Waddle. “First, [WR] Jaylen [Waddle] played great. He had a great game. [He] did a great job in man, did a great job in zone. Started off with that big completion down the field and that sort of got him going. He just showed his swagger all day, he showed enthusiasm, he’s got a passion about him, he’s just a great teammate and he just plays the right way, and he gets rewarded because of it.” Head coach Sean Payton is excited, quarterback Bo Nix can’t hide his excitement, and Courtland Sutton is still somewhere cheesin’. There was a lot of hype and excitement for Waddle heading into the season, and he proved why on Sunday. This should be the first of many big games for Waddle, and like Sean Payton, I am glad Jaylen Waddle is ours too.
author: Scotty Payne

title: Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars
summary: Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars What a difference a week makes. The Denver Broncos were coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, and things looked dire in Broncos Country. The offense looked bad, Bo Nix had one of […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos leaves the field after his team's 20-13 win against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Stock Up, Stock Down After the Broncos’ Week 2 Comeback Win Over the Jaguars What a difference a week makes. The Denver Broncos were coming off an embarrassing blowout loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday Night Football, and things looked dire in Broncos Country. The offense looked bad, Bo Nix had one of his worst career games, Davis Webb’s debut as a playcaller was a failure, and the defense looked bad and had a ton of missed tackles. To make things worse, the Broncos would be hosting their home opener vs. a very good Jacksonville Jaguars team that has been playing like one of the better teams in the league and beat the Broncos by double digits last season. Well, the Broncos bounced back and had one of their classic 4th-quarter comeback victories. Things started rough early on, but the defense played well, and Bo Nix, Jaylen Waddle, and rookie Jonah Coleman helped lead the Broncos to a victory. Stock up and stock down is a weekly series where I go through the Denver Broncos roster and give you stock-ups and stock-downs on every player currently on the 53-man roster. After a bounce-back performance like that on Sunday, we are going to see a lot more stock-ups than we did last week. Quarterback Bo Nix – Stock up: After having one of the worst games of his career on Monday Night, Nix bounced back and gave us a classic Bo Nix performance. There were some struggles early on, but he was moving the ball up and down the field fairly easily against the Jaguars’ defense. However, red zone struggles really hurt what could have been a big game for Nix. Still, he passed for 288 yards and a touchdown and led yet another 4th-quarter comeback vs. a pretty good Jaguars team. Jarrett Stidham – Unchanged: Remains the backup quarterback Sam Ehlinger – Unchanged: Remains the emergency third-string quarterback Running Back JK Dobbins – Stock down: The veteran back left the game due to a hamstring injury, which thankfully sounds minor, but we’ll see how it trends as the week progresses. With his injury history, it is concerning to see an injury pop up this early in the season. Pair that with his multiple goal-line failures and rookie Jonah Coleman looking really good, and you have to go stock down on JK Dobbins. RJ Harvey – Unchanged: Harvey was inactive for this game due to a hamstring injury, but he was able to put in two limited practices, so it sounds like he may not miss much more time moving forward. I am going with unchanged simply because his role is not in danger. He is the Broncos third down/pass game specialist. We saw him get plenty of touches and snaps in the opener, and when healthy, I believe his role is locked in on this offense. Jonah Coleman – Stock up: Coleman entered the game late due to JK Dobbins leaving with a hamstring injury and played really well. He scored his first career touchdown, which was the go-ahead score, and helped the Broncos ice the game late, which has been something they have struggled to do in recent history. Coleman is the future starter of this backfield; it’s just a matter of when, not if. Tyler Badie – Stock up: I thought Badie played well. He had a 27-yard catch-and-run and had a couple of nice returns in the kicking game. That’s what he’s supposed to do, and I thought he played well, all things considered. Adam Prentice – Stock down: He played just 8 snaps of offense and wasn’t used in the Broncos’ goal-line failures in the first half. He was a short-yardage specialist last season and in the preseason, but the Broncos have yet to pull that trigger this season. Wide Receiver Jaylen Waddle – Stock way up: That’s more like it. After a 1-catch for 2-yard performance in Week 1, Waddle exploded for 8 catches for 138 yards. He made multiple key plays in big moments and looked like the explosive playmaker the Broncos traded for this offseason. This should be the first of many big games from the Broncos’ explosive wide receiver. Courtland Sutton – Stock down: His role in this offense appears to have taken a step back. Had a down Week 1, and unlike Waddle, the veteran didn’t do too much in Week 2. He finished with 3 catches for 25 yards and was targeted just 4 times. I still feel like we’ll have a few big Sutton games, but his week-to-week performance is probably going to continue to be inconsistent. Pat Bryant – Unchanged: 0 targets and 1 end-around for 16 yards. It wasn’t a great game on paper for Bryant, who was also flagged for another holding call (Like the other ones on Monday Night; it seemed kinda BS), but I am not going to overreact here. The team really likes their second-year wide receiver, and this week was just the Jaylen Waddle show. Marvin Mims Jr. – Stock down: Injuries suck. The Broncos All-Pro returner has been dealing with multiple injuries throughout the summer. He missed time during camp, returned for the preseason, and then was hurt again; he played in Week 1, got hurt, and then missed Week 2. He just needs to get healthy and stay healthy. Troy Franklin – Stock up: I went with stock down due to his bad OPI on Monday Night, but I am going with stock up due to his nice one-handed catch on Sunday. He played just 13 snaps and was targeted 2 times, so the usage isn’t great, but he made the most of his opportunity on Sunday. Lil ’ Jordan Humphrey – Unchanged: He is who he is and fills a depth role on the offense and special teams. He didn’t play much on Sunday, but that was expected. Tight End Adam Trautman – Unchanged: An in-line blocking specialist who played 65% of the snaps, but you wouldn’t really know it if you watched the game. 0 targets and was strictly in for blocking. Evan Engram – Stock up: He was targeted just once on Sunday but made a tremendous catch late in the game. He played 52% of the snaps and made the most of his lone target, so I am going stock up. Nate Adkins – Stock up: Is Nate Adkins really the Joker? (Sorry). The blocking specialist led all tight ends with 3 catches for 32 yards and 1 touchdown. He actually had the second-most receiving yards on the team, only trailing Jaylen Waddle. He played 37% of the offensive snaps, contributed on special teams, and does all the dirty work that typically goes unrecognized by fans. Need games like this from your depth players throughout the year. Dallen Bentley – Unchanged: The rookie tight end was inactive and is likely having a red-shirt year for the Broncos. Offensive Line Garett Bolles – Unchanged: I’ll say this each week, I am not an OL expert, but the unit looked better this week. Nix was not sacked, and I did not see the pressure get to him as it did vs. the Chiefs. Ben Powers – Unchanged: Same story here with Powers. Did not really notice him, which is usually a good thing for a lineman. Luke Wattenberg – Stock down: Simply for the delayed snap on the 3rd-down goal-line toss play. It threw off the play from the start, which immediately doomed it from the start. Quinn Meinerz: Stock up: He pancaked a dude. Mike McGlinchey – Stock up: Struggled vs. the Chiefs but appeared to have a better game on Sunday. Alex Palczewski – Unchanged: Played just 4 offensive snaps and is your top reserve OL. Matt Peart – Unchanged: Didn’t play a single snap but is your backup tackle. Alex Forsyth – Unchanged: Did not play a single snap but is your backup center. Kage Casey – Unchanged: Inactive and likely having a rookie redshirt year. Defensive Line Zach Allen – Stock up: He’s unblockable at times and was in there on multiple pressures and sacks despite not being credited with one. DJ Jones – Stock up: The run defense was better, and he’s the man in the middle of the defensive line. I did not see him stand out much, but the overall play was better than last week, so stock up. Malcolm Roach – Stock…
