title: Chiefs’ Kenneth Walker is having a historic start to the season
summary: Two weeks into the NFL season, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker has stayed atop the mountain as the star of the football world after earning last year’s Super Bowl MVP award. The NFL leader in yards from scrimmage (365) and rushing yards (290) has run rampant over the Denver Broncos and Indianapolis Colts […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 20: Kenneth Walker III #9 of the Kansas City Chiefs runs the ball during the first quarter against the Indianapolis Colts at Arrowhead Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Two weeks into the NFL season, Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker has stayed atop the mountain as the star of the football world after earning last year’s Super Bowl MVP award. The NFL leader in yards from scrimmage (365) and rushing yards (290) has run rampant over the Denver Broncos and Indianapolis Colts defenses in primetime. Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry is second in the NFL in rushing yards, with 72 fewer than Walker. As strong as the offensive line has looked, Walker has produced a lot of yards himself. On Sunday night, he forced a career-high 15 missed tackles, according to NFL Next Gen Stats . His previous high came last week against Denver (14). If those single-game totals sound like a lot, they are. The 29 forced missed tackles lead all NFL players (heading into “Monday Night Football”) this season and are five more than any player has registered in NFL Pro’s statistical database through two weeks of an NFL season since at least 2018. Players with 150+ scrimmage yards in each of their team's first 2 games of a season over the last decade: 🔸 Kenneth Walker III (2026) 🔸 Justin Jefferson (2023) Walker is the first Chiefs player to do so in franchise history. — NFL Researcher (@NFL_Researcher) September 21, 2026 Not only was Walker one of the only modern NFL players to surpass 150 scrimmage yards in each of the first weeks of the season, but he also joined memorable Oklahoma and Detroit Lions running back Billy Sims as the only NFL players to ever begin their careers with a team s urpassing 175 total yards in the first two games played there . Ken Walker is the first member of the Chiefs to rush for 100+ yards in back-to-back games since Clyde Edwards-Helaire did so in 2021. Through two weeks, Walker leads the NFL in rushing yards (290) and scrimmage yards (369). — Matt McMullen (@KCChiefs_Matt) September 21, 2026

title: 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ Week 2 overtime victory over the Colts
summary: For the second straight week, the Kansas City Chiefs beat a team of horses. Unlike last week, the game never felt in hand. This game was back and forth — and although it wasn’t a perfect game by either team, it was quite entertaining and literally came down to the last possible second before the […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the second straight week, the Kansas City Chiefs beat a team of horses. Unlike last week, the game never felt in hand. This game was back and forth — and although it wasn’t a perfect game by either team, it was quite entertaining and literally came down to the last possible second before the Chiefs finally sealed their 33-30 victory in overtime over the Indianapolis Colts , via a walk-off field goal by Harrison Butker Here are five things we learned from Kansas City outlasting Indianapolis on Sunday evening: 1. The passing game isn’t dead. After a mostly quiet debut back from his injury last week, quarterback Patrick Mahomes — QB1 — was back to being that dude again, tossing the rock for 382 yards and three touchdowns. Patrick Mahomes famously did not complete a 10+ yard pass in Week 1. That changed tonight. On such throws: – 7/11 – 155 yards – 1 TD – 137.5 passer rating His 382 passing yards were his most in a game since 10/22/2023… and did so on an efficient 8.1 YPA pic.twitter.com/hObqfk4ue3 — Mike Kennedy (@MikeKennedyNFL) September 21, 2026 And while tight end Travis Kelce was the main beneficiary of Mahomes’ targets, the most encouraging part of this game was how many contributors Mahomes connected with to rack up nearly 400 passing yards. Mahomes completed passes to seven different receivers. Five of them had four or more receptions. It was also nice to see Jalen Royals get in the mix and score his first NFL touchdown. And as I mentioned, this was by no means Mahomes or the Chiefs’ best game, which should be even scarier for the rest of the league. The Chiefs had 523 yards of total offense, and it still felt like they left a few plays out on the field. 2. Kelce is still Kelce The Chiefs’ future Hall of Fame tight end proved tonight that he still has plenty left in the tank to play another season, and hopefully make another playoff run. Over two weeks, we’ve seen the explosive plays return to Kelce’s game. He’s not the player he once was, but he can still do the job. No matter his age, Travis Kelce remains one of the best big game players in the sport. Tonight was his first 100-yard game since 1/18/25… in the divisional playoffs Before that, he had 100 yards on MNF on 11/4/24 His last before that was the ‘23 AFC CG pic.twitter.com/QhzUUp9bjr — Mike Kennedy (@MikeKennedyNFL) September 21, 2026 After the game, former captain of the site and current Kansas City Star reporter Pete Sweeney asked Kelce about his touchdown. As the consummate team player he is, he credited wide receiver Xavier Worthy for laying the block on the Colts defender that allowed him to get into the end zone. Chiefs TE Travis Kelce’s postgame remarks in the locker room. Says the team is in a zone right now and feeding off each other. pic.twitter.com/BDzND5xxka — Matt Derrick (@mattderrick) September 21, 2026 Kelce may be Mrs. Swift’s husband, but he’s also still one of the best tight ends in the NFL. Taylor Swift points to the wedding ring after Travis Kelce scores a touchdown pic.twitter.com/RqU1GVaTcq — Bussin' With The Boys (@BussinWTB) September 21, 2026 3. Emmett Johnson will make Kenneth Walker better If you want to wear down an opposing defense, throw an absolute unit like Kenneth Walker at them 25 or more times a game and watch their will to make contact deteriorate. But if you want to absolutely obliterate them, then bring in another running back who is almost as talented as Walker. Johnson’s vision, lateral agility, and contact balance make him just as hard to bring down. Emmett Johnson DANCIN' out there INDvsKC on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/X7YXNw6QVs — NFL (@NFL) September 21, 2026 The one-two punch of Walker and Johnson is only going to get better as the year progresses, and we saw tonight what happens when an opposing defense has to respect the run first when Mahomes is on the field cooking. 4. Nohl Williams looks like a star For the second straight week, Chiefs’ second-year player Nohl Williams looked like one of the best cornerbacks in football. That matters, considering we don’t know when first-round draft pick Mansoor Delane will return to the lineup from injury. In the meantime, Williams is more than holding up his end of the bargain. He stayed in the opposing receiver’s hip pocket all night Sunday. He nearly single-handedly won the game for Kansas City, if the back of L’Jarius Sneed’s hand hadn’t grazed Colt’s receiver, Laquan Treadwell, on his way to the ground. LAQUON TREADWELL MAKES A GAME-DECIDING CATCH FOR THE COLTS, THEN ALMOST FUMBLES IT AWAY HE WAS TOUCHED pic.twitter.com/8l8uh1eVLt — NFL Drop (@TheNFLDrop) September 21, 2026 5. The ‘refs are in the Chiefs’ back pocket’ narrative is dead Listen, I’m not mad the refs overturned the call on the field in overtime to give the ball back to the Colts. I’m not angry, because the Chiefs still figured out a way to win. Now, if the game had been different. And the Chiefs hadn’t found a way to stop the Colts in the red zone, and they hadn’t figured out a way to drive down the field and win the game. I would have been fuming. But either way, this narrative is dead, or at least I don’t want to hear about it whatsoever anymore.

However, this new updated 2027 mock draft from Yahoo Sports still has the Chargers picking at No. 17, meaning they believe the Bolts will settle in and finish with around 8-9 wins this year. Defensive tackle likely isn’t the position the Chargers will need to address the most come next year’s draft, but picking a blue-chip player at an impact position in today’s NFL is always a strong backup option if there is not an elite offensive lineman or skill player available when they’re on the clock. title: Is Chargers’ season over after 0-2 start at home?
summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are waking up in a bit of a pickle after losing to the Las Vegas Raiders at home in Week 2. title: Rams-Giants final score: Defense dominates Jameis Winston in win
summary: The Los Angeles Rams (1-1) beat the New York Giants (1-1) by a final score of 28-6 in Week 2 of the NFL season on Monday Night Football. The Rams notched a much-needed win on Monday night as they avoided falling to the NFL’s dreaded 0-2 mark. It wasn’t perfect, but the Rams will take […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Aaron Donald #99 of the Los Angeles Rams warms up prior to the game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams (1-1) beat the New York Giants (1-1) by a final score of 28-6 in Week 2 of the NFL season on Monday Night Football. The Rams notched a much-needed win on Monday night as they avoided falling to the NFL’s dreaded 0-2 mark. It wasn’t perfect, but the Rams will take the win, and they’ll have their defense to thank for truly not allowing the Giants offense to get going as Jameis Winston felt the heat from the defense more of the game than not. Throw in Matthew Stafford throwing four touchdowns and it’s no surprise the Rams pulled out a win in Week 2. Regardless of the outcome, the big news out of New York was the injury to Jaxson Dart on New York’s opening possession. Dart left the game with an apparent knee injury after getting sandwiched between two L.A. defenders. He did not return and the severity of his injury is unknown. Though, Dart was seen on the sideline later in the game indicating that his injury may not be as serious. Time will tell. Big news for the Rams was that Aaron Donald made his return, and he appeared to be double and triple teamed the same as always, which opened up lanes for other defenders and with Myles Garrett injured, Donald’s return gave L.A. needed firepower. Perhaps bigger news for L.A. is that the Rams looked competitive in Week 2 after looking outclassed by the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1. The Rams showed they may belong in the NFC West afterall in this game, though they have plenty of work to do if they still want to meet pre-season expectations and get to the Super Bowl. One week at a time. The first half With Dart out for the Giants early, Winston was forced into the contest, and Winston didn’t seem to offer the mobility or overall threat level that Dart did in Week 1. L.A.‘s defense held Winston in check for the most part with plenty of pressure, but Winston also missed some throws that he certainly would’ve liked back. Would Dart have made those missed throws? It’s a fair question. On the one hand you could argue that the Rams defense was solid through two quarters by forcing punts and causing an interception, on the other hand, you could argue that better quarterback play would’ve led to L.A.‘s defense getting picked apart as plenty of Giants seemed open, but Winston struggled to hit them. Stafford and Davante Adams connected on plenty of big plays, and Stafford helped L.A. take a 14-0 lead when he found Adams for one score, and Kyren Williams for another. Stafford did later throw an interception into double coverage on what appeared to be a poor or unnecessary decision by the veteran QB. Williams also lost a fumble in the second quarter giving the Giants life when the Rams had a chance to close out the opening half. Instead, Williams fumbled, but the Rams defense held the Giants to a field goal. The Rams then responded to put together a nice drive with about 30-seconds left in the half, but Harrison Mevis missed a field goal and the score stayed 14-3 as the opening half came to its close. The second half The Rams had a nice second half, but it didn’t start that way when they came out of the half and did nothing on offense. Fortunately for the Rams, their defense continued to keep them in the game as they battered the Giants and Winston. L.A.’s defense was likely the strongest unit of the day, and that says a lot considering Stafford threw for four touchdowns. Stafford and Adams kept up their strong connection as Stafford was able to find Adams for his third passing score of the day and Adams’ second receiving touchdown. The Giants tacked on a field goal to make the score 21-6, but when Stafford found Terrance Ferguson for his fourth passing score to make the score 28-6, the game was seemingly wrapped up based on what had been seen to this point from Winston and the Giants offense. And wrapped up it was as the Rams secured the desired win. The Final All you can do is play who is in front of you and the Rams beat their opponent in Week 2. There were mistakes, yes, and there was enough there to think this Rams team is better than what was shown in Week 1. We’ll see how this team looks in Week 3 when they travel to take on the Denver Broncos for L.A.‘s third primetime game in a row on Sunday Night Football.

title: Rams takeaways we can glean from NFL Week 2 results
summary: We may look back at the end of the season and feel it is best to throw out the Los Angeles Rams’ opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Week 1 can lie. It can also be the first sign of an unexpected problem. These are a few NFL narratives that flipped on […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Justin Herbert #10 of the Los Angeles Chargers calls to his team during the first quarter of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images We may look back at the end of the season and feel it is best to throw out the Los Angeles Rams’ opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. Week 1 can lie . It can also be the first sign of an unexpected problem. These are a few NFL narratives that flipped on their head with another week of information collection: The Bills may have the best offense in football. Their defense could be trouble. Buffalo allowed 31 points in their opener to a Texans team that managed just six points in their encore against the Bengals. The Bills gave up 31 to the Lions on Thursday Night Football. Josh Allen looks unstoppable through two games. Opposing teams may be able to keep pace with how porous the defense seems without Sean McDermott. Buffalo is now an offensive team. The Rams host the Bills on Monday Night Football in Week 5. If a team came out completely flat in Week 1, the whole game may be a lie Two of the most disappointing outcomes from the opening week were the Rams not showing up against the 49ers and the Denver Broncos looking completely inept against the Kansas City Chiefs. The Broncos rebounded with a 20-13 win over the Jacksonville Jaguars, who had one of the most impressive Week 1 performances. That is an encouraging sign for the Rams, who need to bounce back on Monday Night Football against the New York Giants. Denver provides a proof of concept for LA. The real test will come in Week 3 when the Rams and Broncos clash on Sunday Night Football in Denver. We should get real answers surrounding the trajectory of both teams soon after we see how LA fares against the Giants. Justin Herbert as an allegory for Matthew Stafford The Rams entered 2026 with sky-high expectations. Similarly but to a lesser degree, most expected the Los Angeles Chargers to take a step forward this year as well. But the Chargers have now fallen to 0-2 . They’ve dropped games to the Arizona Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders, neither of which were even close to competent a year ago. It seems the expectations are getting to Justin Herbert. He looks emotional on the field and has clearly regressed at this stage of his career. It’s early. The results are not encouraging. How will Matthew Stafford perform after posting one of the worst quarterback performances in Week 1? If Herbert can suffer a fall of grace, so can Stafford—and Herbert is in the prime of his career. The Chargers face the Rams at SoFi Stadium as the road team in Week 8. Is Sam Darnold along for the Seahawks’ ride? After failing with the New York Jets and Carolina Panthers, Sam Darnold spent time rehabilitating his career with the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings before leading the Seattle Seahawks to a Super Bowl victory. But his backup, Drew Lock, has now led Seattle to wins over the last two weeks and looked strong along the way. Seattle has taken down both the New England Patriots and the Arizona Cardinals with Lock behind the wheel. Has Darnold really taken a significant step forward from his days in New York and Carolina? Or is the Seahawks’ supporting cast so good that it makes whoever is under center irrelevant? The Rams won’t see the Seahawks until Week 16 and 18 this season. Final thoughts A dominant performance by the Rams on Monday Night Football against the Giants would dispel a lot of concerns surrounding this football team. However, LA is favored by 7.5 points and should be expected to win this game. Their next stretch of contests against the Broncos, Eagles, and Bills will tell us who they really are. Based on how many teams changed their trajectory following a disastrous Week 1 loss, there is certainly hope for the Rams. They must take care of business on Monday.

title: Will Rams enter the NFC West race on Monday Night Football?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams are already behind the Seattle Seahawks, San Francisco 49ers and the Arizona Cardinals in the NFC West race with L.A.’s Week 2 game still to be played on Monday night. Even with a win Monday, the Rams will still be looking up at the 49ers and Seahawks, but a win puts […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Matthew Stafford #9 of the Los Angeles Rams passes the ball during the NFL football game at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams are already behind the Seattle Seahawks, San Francisco 49ers and the Arizona Cardinals in the NFC West race with L.A.’s Week 2 game still to be played on Monday night. Even with a win Monday, the Rams will still be looking up at the 49ers and Seahawks, but a win puts the Rams back in business with a 1-1 record. An 0-2 record could mean the end of their season. Yes, that’s dramatic, and, yes, it could be true. I don’t make the rules. The rules are you need to win the in the NFL and so far, the Rams haven’t. Can they put a winning game together on Monday night? Even if the Rams lose, what fans and the team want to see is a better effort than they showed in Week 1. If L.A. comes out flat, or just plain bad again, the concern meter will rise. Will Matthew Stafford look better? Can the Rams overcome the loss of Myles Garrett? How does Aaron Donald look? Will Puka Nacua play? If Nacua doesn’t play, how will the Rams respond? Can Chris Shula and his defense improve? How about Harrison Mevis and the special teams? The Rams have a lot of questions. They get the chance to answer some of them (for better or worse) on Monday Night Football. 2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Mike Macdonald’s defense smothers Cardinals . Arizona had one good drive – a 12-play, 61-yard, five-first down, TD possession – in the first half. The rest of the afternoon, Seattle’s defense dominated. The defensive line destroyed the Cards’ front, bringing waves of pressure and slamming the door on Arizona’s running game. Seattle allowed just 39 yards on 14 carries combined from Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Allgeier (2.8 yards per carry). With the run game silenced, Seattle was able to tee off on Jacoby Brissett . The Seahawks generated 18 QB pressures, per Next Gen Stats. On dropbacks under pressure, Seattle held Brissett to 4 of 11 for 9 yards, with an interception and a 7.0 passer rating. Give safety Julian Love some flowers for a gorgeous sliding INT, his second of the season. Facing a Cards team that put up nearly 400 yards in Week 1, Macdonald’s crew held Arizona to 151 yards, 3.2 yards per play, 10 first downs and 3 of 12 on third downs. Domination.“ 2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games (nfl.com) “ Milestone day for McCaffrey, Kittle. On a day that was all about Kyle Shanahan’s offense, it was no shock that the heartbeat of the supporting cast shined brightest. Christian McCaffrey had just 67 scrimmage yards but made the most of his touches near the goal line. His pair of rushing scores put him in elite company, as he became the third player in NFL history to record 50-plus scrimmage TDs with multiple teams, joining Hall of Famers Marshall Faulk (Rams, 85; Colts 51) and Randy Moss (Vikings, 92; Patriots, 50). But perhaps the most exciting aspect of San Francisco’s offensive frenzy was George Kittle’s return to prominence. After missing six games in 2025 with an Achilles injury and a modest Week 1 outing in Australia, the seven-time Pro Bowler led the team with 80 receiving yards and his first touchdown, a 12-yard reception on a busted coverage, since the injury. Kittle’s third catch of the day also marked his 600th career reception, the 11th tight end in league history to accomplish that feat.“ Whose house? Rams return home as Aaron Donald makes long-awaited comeback against Giants (nypost) “The Rams surrendered 174 rushing yards, failed to record a sack on 34 pass attempts and generated just two quarterback hits. Myles Garrett finished with the same statistical line as Aaron Donald, who watched from the comforts of his couch at home in Los Angeles: zero tackles, zero sacks and zero pressures. Now Garrett is on injured reserve following a knee procedure, leaving Donald to make his anticipated return after more than two years away from football. The rams have 99 problems, but No. 99 will not be one, no pressure AD.“ Notable injuries, news from Sunday’s Week 2 games: Packers WR Jayden Reed (neck) carted off vs. Jets (nfl.com) “ San Francisco 49ers receiver Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was ruled out of Sunday’s game against the Dolphins. Head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters after the game Robinson and DT James Thompson Jr. have high ankle sprains. Wide receiver Mike Evans (hip) did not return to the game but the injury doesn’t look serious, per Shanahan. Seattle Seahawks running back Jadarian Price (chest) did not return to Sunday’s game against the Cardinals. HC Mike Macdonald said after the game that X-rays came back negative on Price’s injury.“ New York Giants vs. Rams: 5 things to know before Monday night’s kickoff (giantswire) “Donald will be strapping on the pads for the first time since 2023, having retired after that season. No one knows what kind of physical or mental shape he’s in, what impact he’ll have, or how much he’ll play. He’ll be butting heads with Giants rookie guard Francis Mauigoa, which promises to be an interesting matchup. Nacua has been nursing a groin injury and is listed as questionable. He did not practice Saturday, but his track record suggests he’ll play. At what percentage is unknown. If Puka is limited, the Rams don’t have much depth behind him, with Jordan Whittington (quad) doubtful. Of course, they still have Davante Adams in their lineup, but he only caught three of six targets in the Week 1 loss to San Francisco.“ Donald in, Garrett out: How will Rams defense look with huge addition (and subtraction)? (espn) “Though the future Pro Football Hall of Fame defensive tackle said he knows it has been two full seasons since he walked off the field after the season-ending loss to the Detroit Lions , in a way, it feels like he never left. “[After] being back around, I feel like I was just here last year,” Donald said. “Time flies by so fast, and I forget that I haven’t play[ed] football for two years. I feel like I’m just back to my normal self.” Donald did not play in — or even travel to — the Rams’ season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, as he worked to get up to speed after coming out of retirement Aug. 30.“ Giants vs. Rams: What to watch as Los Angeles looks to bounce back in ‘MNF’ (cbsports) “The Giants did whatever they wanted against the Cowboys on “Sunday Night Football” last weekend. New York ran the ball 37 times for 165 yards and a touchdown. Jaxson Dart completed 23 of 29 passes for 230 yards and three scores. The Giants controlled the ball for 36 minutes and 40 seconds of the 60-minute game. They had three second-half drives; they scored a touchdown on each of the first two and ran the clock out on the third. All three drives lasted 12-plus plays. It was surgical stuff.“ Sean McVay and Rams are being tested early, but it’s far too soon to write them off (nytimes) “The numbers speak to the depths of that performance, but also to the standard that made the Rams Super Bowl favorites even before their blockbuster trade for two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett or the return of three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald from retirement. Unlike some infamous preseason “ dream teams ,” these Rams weren’t microwaved through transactions in a single offseason. This team fell just short of a trip to the Super Bowl and returned every starter except the two it replaced with Garrett and All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie.“ Criticism of Chris Shula Is Missing the Bigger Picture With Rams Defense (si.com) “However, that doesn’t make the defense blameless. The Rams trailed by three points at halftime before the 49ers scored a touchdown to start the half and then allowed a 99-yard touchdown drive following a missed fourth-down conversion from the offense. Put together, it…

title: Rams one loss from joining Chargers as early-season disappointment
summary: It’s been a rough start to the football season for Los Angeles fans, as the LA Rams and Chargers are winless so far. The Rams must win against the Giants on Monday night or risk following in the Chargers’ footsteps as an early-season disappointment. Entering the 2026 season, the Chargers had the fifth-highest odds to […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Jim Harbaugh of the Los Angeles Chargers talks to his team prior to the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at SoFi Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been a rough start to the football season for Los Angeles fans, as the LA Rams and Chargers are winless so far. The Rams must win against the Giants on Monday night or risk following in the Chargers’ footsteps as an early-season disappointment. Entering the 2026 season, the Chargers had the fifth-highest odds to win the Super Bowl, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . They also have the fourth-most wins in the NFL since Jim Harbaugh took the head coaching job in 2024. So far, this season is trending to be a bust for the Chargers, as they’ve lost their first two games to the Cardinals and Raiders despite being favored in both matchups. View this post on Instagram Neither Arizona nor Las Vegas is expected to be a juggernaut or finish with a winning record this season. It was already bad (and odd) enough for the Chargers to lose 26-14 in the first two games. The other LA losing games to teams they should have beaten could spell the end of their season before Week 3. Their schedule is set to get EXTREMELY BRUTAL. The Chargers will play five teams that made the playoffs in 2025 in their next seven games, including the Rams and the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks. Holy strength-of-schedule, Batman! The Chargers are now 0-2. Their next 7 games are: At Bills At Seahawks Vs Broncos At Chiefs At Rams Vs Texans At Ravens — Field Yates (@FieldYates) September 20, 2026 Los Angeles won’t start 0-9, as they’ll figure out a way to win maybe one or two of those matchups. Either way, it doesn’t matter, considering the Chargers shouldn’t be in this position in the first place. The Rams cannot afford to stumble like their roommate any further. They have far more on the line than the Chargers. Falling short of expectations isn’t an option for the Rams. LA’s front office poured too many resources into the roster — trading for Myles Garrett and signing Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson, for example — to allow that to happen, recent injury concerns be damned. As it’s been stated many, many times since the Rams lost to the 49ers, it was undoubtedly a major setback to begin the season. It certainly took the wind out of the sails of what could be a special season in Hollywood. Yes, the Niners are way better than both teams the Chargers have lost to, yet the Rams were still favored, so there are no excuses. The Rams can’t let that season-opening failure define them, as the Chargers have essentially allowed it to happen through the first two weeks. Similar to the Chargers, the Rams have a tough upcoming slate. Following the Giants game, the Rams will face four playoff teams from last season in their next seven, including the Chargers. They will also play the Raiders, who the Chargers lost to by 12 on Sunday. Simply put, the Rams must win on Monday night to avoid becoming an early-season disappointment like the Chargers. It might already be too late for the Chargers this early in the year, and the Rams could suffer a similar fate if they can’t beat an opponent in New York that they should be able to beat.

full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 26-14 win at the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2 and what to look for Sunday at the New Orleans Saints: Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick served as Kirk Cousins backup. He did not play. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick played 31 defensive snaps before leaving with a concussion. His availability for Sunday will be determined later this week. Stukes was good when he did play against the Chargers as he had four tackles. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick played two plays at guard and he played four plays on special teams. He did not play on offense in Week 1. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick played 18 defensive snaps and he played three snaps on special teams. He did not play at all in Week 1 despite being active. He will likley continue get get some rotational defensive snaps at New Orleans. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played 19 percent of the offensive snaps for the second straight game. He didn’t make an impact as he had seven yards on three carries. He had seven carries for 41 yards in Week 1. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was a healthy scratch for the second straight game. If Stukes is out Sunday, Johnson has a chance to be active. If not, that would not be a great sign. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick started for the injured Darien Porter and made a huge impact. He had two interceptions and played well overall. if wouldn’t be a shock tp see him become a full-time starter. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played 8 offensive snaps. He was targeted once but appeared to run the wrong route. He has one catch on three targets in two games. He had one punt return for 16 yards in Week 2 and is averaging 17 yards a punt return on three returns this season.

title: Tyree Wilson quiet so far with New Orleans Saints
summary: It’s only been two weeks, but the Las Vegas Raiders are already surprising people this season with a 2-0 record, including Sunday’s big win over the Los Angeles Chargers. So, the Raiders aren’t really missing any offseason losses/subtractions, but let’s take a look at how a few old friends fared this week. Tyree Wilson Score: […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s only been two weeks, but the Las Vegas Raiders are already surprising people this season with a 2-0 record , including Sunday’s big win over the Los Angeles Chargers. So, the Raiders aren’t really missing any offseason losses/subtractions, but let’s take a look at how a few old friends fared this week. Tyree Wilson Score: 24-17 Saints win Stats : 0 tackles Seeing as Las Vegas heads to New Orleans to take on the Saints next week, Wilson seems like a good player to start with. However, he isn’t making much of an impact in the Big Easy. The 2023 No. 7 overall pick had just two tackles in the season opener and didn’t even register a stat in Week 2 against the Baltimore Ravens. Wilson was active; he just wasn’t doing much. The Saints sent a fifth-round pick to get the defensive end, which the Raiders used to draft safety Dalton Johnson, who has been a healthy scratch in both games. However, Johnson at least provides some future value while Wilson is in a contract year. Geno Smith Score: 20-17 Jets lose in OT Stats: 27/41 (65.9%), 247 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT The New York Jets held a late-fourth-quarter lead but couldn’t hold on, giving up 10 points in the final frame and three more in overtime to drop to 1-1. Smith didn’t play poorly by any means, taking care of the football with no turnovers on a rainy day while throwing for nearly 250 yards. However, taking too many sacks was one of his big issues in Las Vegas, and he hit the ground four times against a Micah Parsons-less Green Bay Packers defense. Smith was sacked twice on the Jets’ failed overtime drive. K’Lavon Chaisson Score: 37-20 Commanders lose Stats: 3 tackles, 1 sack Speaking of sacks, Chaisson notched his first of the year against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. Granted, that didn’t matter much since the Cowboys controlled this game pretty much from start to finish, scoring on the opening drive and winning by three possessions. But after having just having five sacks in four seasons before heading to Las Vegas, Chaisson has gotten to the quarterback 13.5 times in two seasons and two games. That’s a testament to former defensive line coach and current Raiders defensive coordinator Rob Leonard.
author: Matt Holder

title: Nakobe Dean saves win for Las Vegas Raiders in Week 2 against Los Angeles Chargers
summary: Not many people had the Las Vegas Raiders starting the season 2-0 and, more specifically, beating the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2. But after a 26-14 victory, here we are! What’s impressive about the Raiders’ pair of wins is that they did it in two different ways, with a variety of players stepping up […]
full_text: (Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images) | Getty Images Not many people had the Las Vegas Raiders starting the season 2-0 and, more specifically, beating the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2. But after a 26-14 victory , here we are! What’s impressive about the Raiders’ pair of wins is that they did it in two different ways, with a variety of players stepping up in the contests. That leads to a few changes from last week’s winners and losers . WINNER: Nakobe Dean To be clear, Dean was sharp against both the Miami Dolphins and the Chargers. He’s currently tied with fellow linebacker Quay Walker for the team lead in tackles ( 16 ) after notching a double-digit performance in Los Angeles. On top of that, Dean made plenty of quality tackles last Sunday by posting four ‘ defensive stops ’ and made an impact as a pass-rusher with half-a-sack and three pressures on five pass-rushes, per Pro Football Focus . But what really stood out about the free-agent signing’s performance against the Bolts was a clutch play in a massive moment. The Raiders were clinging to a three-point lead while the Chargers were driving about halfway through the fourth quarter. A Malcolm Koonce strip-stack on third down bounced LA’s way, allowing the offense to gain yards to set up a fourth-and-one, where Las Vegas was flagged for having too many men on the field. After a first down, it started to feel like the game was going to slip away from the Silver and Black. However, on the next play, Dean crashed downhill and delivered a big hit on running back Omarion Hampton to force a fumble and create a turnover. That led to a touchdown to give the Raiders a two-possession lead and put the game on ice. LOSER: Offensive Line The offensive line, rightfully, drew plenty of praise for their Week 1 performance. However, it was a completely different story against the Chargers, as the unit struggled mightily. Quarterback Kirk Cousins was hit 10 times (two sacks) and was under pressure on 43.8% of his dropbacks, according to PFF . Additionally, the Raiders averaged just 2.0 yards per carry as a team , with running backs Ashton Jeanty (2.3 ypc) and Mike Washington Jr. (2.3 ypc) consistently facing defenders in the backfield. To add some more context, Jackson Powers-Johnson was PFF’s highest-graded offensive lineman for Las Vegas, and even he was below their baseline grade of 60 at 56.6 . Even reliable veterans Tyler Linderbaum (51.2) and Kolton Miller (49.7) had rough outings. If Vegas’ offense is going to have sustained success throughout the season, the line has to get back to its Week 1 form rather than taking a step backward. WINNER: Kirk Cousins Much prettier passing chart from Kirk Cousins in Week 2 -9/14 with 3 TDs (1 INT) on passes 10+ yards downfield #RaiderNation https://t.co/MoxZbJSCew pic.twitter.com/3LcBW60CxC — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 21, 2026 Cousins took more flak than anyone after last week’s win, primarily due to his lack of success pushing the ball down the field. However, he proved a lot of doubters, myself included, wrong with an excellent performance in Los Angeles. The 38-year-old showed he still has some life left in his right arm, completing nine-of-14 passes 10 or more yards beyond the line of scrimmage for three touchdowns, per Next Gen Stats . And the interception wasn’t his fault, as wide receiver Tre Tucker slipped coming out of his break, leading to a diving pick from the safety who was behind Tucker. It felt like the Chargers’ game plan was to force Cousins to beat them, and, putting it simply, he did. LOSER: Isaiah Pola-Mao The past month or so hasn’t been very kind to Pola-Mao, beginning with losing his starting spot to rookie Treydan Stukes at the end of training camp. But with Stukes suffering a concussion around the halfway point of Sunday’s game, Pola-Mao had a chance to show the coaching staff that he at least deserves more reps. However, the veteran safety was targeted three times and gave up two catches for 61 yards, per PFF , including a blown coverage that led to a 53-yard gain and set up one of the Chargers’ two touchdowns. After not getting any defensive snaps in Week 1, Pola-Mao will likely revert to being a special teamer exclusively once Stukes clears concussion protocol. WINNER: Tre Tucker Tucker was the primary pass-catcher on the receiving end of Cousins’ deep shots, catching four of five targets 10 or more yards past the line of scrimmage for 110 yards and a touchdown, according to PFF . Add in a nine-yard grab on a short target (0-10 yards), and the fourth-year veteran had the second-highest single-game receiving yards of his career. What’s even more impressive is that Tucker continues to show growth as a route runner and is becoming a more polished receiver. What made this play work and Tucker wide open is the condensed alignment from the WRs. Motion from Bech to the flat holds the outside corner vs C4. Tucker gets the 1 on 1 vs a safety Easy money pic.twitter.com/HStyDEZetG — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) September 21, 2026 LOSER: Ashton Jeanty While Jeanty’s lack of success on the ground can be excused since he had flashbacks to last year with little breathing room before touching the ball, three drops in the passing game cannot. On top of that, they were drive-killers, with two coming on third downs, and the other on second-and-nine during a two-minute drill right before halftime that would have given the Raiders a first down and put them in position for a touchdown. Granted, Las Vegas managed to get a field goal after the latter. But it took Matt Gay hitting a career-long 59-yarder, and there’s no denying that the running back left some meat on the bone in Los Angeles. WINNER: Hezekiah Masses It wasn’t a perfect outing for Masses, but coming away with two interceptions in your first NFL start is certainly worth celebrating. Especially since the latter pretty much closed the door on the Chargers, as the Raiders were protecting a two-possession lead with 2:29 left on the clock in the fourth quarter. On top of that, the rookie corner accounted for three defensive stops, per PFF , two of which came against the run. That helped silence some doubts about his tackling, and it will be interesting to see what the coaching staff does at cornerback when Darien Porter returns from injury. Masses made a strong statement to keep the starting spot moving forward.
author: Matt Holder

title: Cody White, Hezekiah Masses double up to help Raiders zap Chargers 26-14
summary: If Klint Kubiak and John Spytek showcase supreme auras of confidence, it’d be hard to criticize the Las Vegas Raiders head coach and general manager, respectively, for doing so. Because in an AFC West matchup between the Raiders and Chargers, an undrafted wide receiver that Kubiak is all too familiar with during his Seattle Seahawks […]
full_text: (Photo by Jeff Antenore/MediaNews Group/Orange County Register via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images If Klint Kubiak and John Spytek showcase supreme auras of confidence, it’d be hard to criticize the Las Vegas Raiders head coach and general manager, respectively, for doing so. Because in an AFC West matchup between the Raiders and Chargers, an undrafted wide receiver that Kubiak is all too familiar with during his Seattle Seahawks days and a rookie fifth-round cornerback Spytek and his personnel room scouted and drafted in the 2026 NFL Draft both doubled up helping power Las Vegas’ 26-14 road win over Los Angeles on Sunday afternoon. Cody White, a 6-foot-3, 227-pound 27-year-old wideout from Michigan State that I dubbed as a “Seattle import”, seemingly came out of nowhere to haul in two key second-half touchdowns. His first was an excellent 13-yard diving reception in the third quarter that capped an 11-play, 74-yard drive to give Las Vegas back the lead — 17-14 — to answer a Los Angeles touchdown. White’s second was a textbook 11-yard reception where the Chargers defense forgot about the big wide receiver altogether. Kirk Cousins finds Cody White in the end zone for the second time today 🔥 LVvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/y2dIEVHxaC — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 To cement White’s status as a practice squad call-up to significant game day contributor, the CBS broadcast wasn’t even prepped for a standout performance from him that the initially graphic shown on TV read “Corey Rucker” and not White. (Rucker, by the way, is an undrafted free agent out of Arkansas State that landed on injured reserve after an undisclosed injury in early June.) CBS’ faux paus doesn’t excuse Los Angeles’ gaffe, however. The Bolts supremely looked like dolts as defenders covered tight end Michael Mayer and wide receiver Jack Bech got the bracket coverage treatment resulting in no defensive back accounting for the Raiders’ big wideout — wide open touchdown and a 24-14 lead. White even had a good sense of humor after the game regarding CBS’ mistake with this post: Shoutout Corey Rucker😂 — Cody White (@codywhite_82) September 21, 2026 The other portion of the Raiders double-double arrived in the form of Masses. The Cal cornerback drew the start with Darien Porter inactive and the 22-year-old showcased confidence and took full advantage of the opportunity presented to him like White did. Masses knew he would be targeted as a late-round rookie getting his first NFL start and Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert obliged, resulting in a pair of interceptions. The initial pick arrived in the first quarter on a rep where Masses got caught looking in the backfield before sprinting to catch up to Chargers tight end David Njoku. The veteran bobbled the ball popping it up allowing Masses to catch the ricochet. Masses’ second takeaway happened in the fourth quarter with the Bolts looking to come back as the 6-foot-1 and 185-pound ballhawk stepped in front of the pass for the interception. Hezekiah Masses gets his SECOND interception of the day 🙌 LVvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/u1kiUQUflN — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Two standout performances from two unheralded players in a division matchup was an impressive sight as was another exhibit of complementary Raiders’ football. It all resulted in the Raiders starting the Kubiak era 2-0 with the Silver & Black showing the ability to collectively win. Let’s hit the quick slants as fast as White and Masses made themselves fan favorites in Week 2: —Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins threw a trio of touchdowns again going 19 of 29 for 253 yards with one interception. The 38-year-old signal caller showed plenty of arm strength on a pair of 40-yard passes to wideout Tre Tucker but did have a misfire on wide open rookie wide receiver Malik Benson. —Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty was bottled up by the Chargers defense producing just 48 yards on 21 carries. At times, it looked like we were watching the Brennan Carroll coached ground game as opposed to what Las Vegas produced in Week 1 against the Miami Dolphins. —But the Bolts couldn’t contain the Raiders’ air attack paced by Tucker (five catches for 119 yards and a score) and White (two receptions for 24 yards and two scores). Jeanty hauled in four passes for 15 yards but had a case of butterfingers dropping would-be first downs. —Rob Leonard’s Raiders defense is certainly an attacking type this is aggressive and swarms to the ball. Nakobe Dean and Quay Walker — the high-priced linebackers added in free agency — paced the group with 10 total tackles, apiece. Dean had the big forced fumble in the fourth quarter to help seal the deal. What a play by Nakobe Dean 💪 LVvsLAC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Yj0jyIdbrn — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 —In a rarity, Raiders punter AJ Cole III was outperformed. While he did have six punts for 227 yards (46.2 yards per boot average) with four of them dropped or down inside the Chargers’ 20-yard line, Bolts punter JK Scott had a higher average on his five boots (for 258 yards) at 51.6 yards per punt. Quotes of Note “It just meant the world. Just being able to go out there and make the plays when Kirk was able to give me some opportunities. It just felt amazing to go out there and get a win.” —Las Vegas Raiders wide receiver Cody White on his two-touchdown performance “I couldn’t even sleep last night, man. I was like, ‘I can’t let my team down.’ I knew they were going to try to come at me being a rookie and I just had to make plays on the ball. I just want to get the ball. Wherever the ball’s at, that’s where I’m trying to be and just make plays.” —Las Vegas Raiders rookie cornerback Hezekiah Masses on his two-interception performance Up Next The Raiders (2-0) continue the road show with a date at the New Orleans Saints (1-1) next Sunday afternoon. Kellen Moore’s Saints dropped the Baltimore Ravens 24-17 this past Sunday scoring 15 fourth-quarter points while blanking the home team in that final stanza for a big road victory. Expect another tough test for Kubiak’s Raiders as the Saints could easily be 2-0 heading into the Week 3 matchup instead of 1-1.
author: Ray Aspuria

title: Las Vegas Raiders overreaction to Week 2 26-14 victory
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are on pace to be a top-5 defense in the league, if not the best defense in the league. So dominant against the Los Angeles Chargers on the road that it begs the question: just how good are they? Especially when even the oddsmakers placed the spread at -6.5 for the […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders are on pace to be a top-5 defense in the league, if not the best defense in the league. So dominant against the Los Angeles Chargers on the road that it begs the question: just how good are they? Especially when even the oddsmakers placed the spread at -6.5 for the Chargers. It was supposed to be a get-right game for Justin Herbert and Mike McDaniel’s offense. Rob Leonard and the Raiders defense didn’t subscribe to that rhetoric; they came in and took the Chargers to the woodshed. Defensively, the Raiders continued their unexpected second week of dominance, forcing turnovers and pushing the Chargers into mistake after mistake. Herbert finished with 192 passing yards, two interceptions, one touchdown, and a 59.5 Rating. They kept running back Omarion Hampton under 100 yards rushing and limited him to one rushing touchdown. Maxx Crosby made Joe Alt submit to his greatness. Crosby beat him like a drum time and time again, causing Alt to stop relying on his technique and get discombobulated. Alt had an uncharacteristic three false-start penalties; two in a row, and ultimately finished off the game for the offense by being flagged for holding Crosby in the end zone. By rule, it was a safety, awarding the Raiders two points and a kick return opportunity. When the dust had cleared and the clock showed :00, the defense had produced three sacks, six total fumbles (four forced), two interceptions and a safety. Coaching matters Beating a division foe on the road without your best player on offense isn’t a small feat. When the defense loaded up the box intending to smother the short-yardage plays, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak got into his bag of tricks. Calling toss sweep flea flickers, the wildcat, set up deep shots and maintaining aggressiveness in his play calls. Bailing out his players in the most beautiful ways possible, there appears to be nothing that Kubiak can’t overcome thus far. When his quarterback displayed a lack of ability to push the ball downfield last week he called him out. This week, his quarterback unleashed a 40-yard touchdown pass to Tre Tucker, the smallest guy on the field and another 42-yard pass to Tucker, on a yolo ball. Activating practice squad receiver Cody White and feeding him multiple red zone opportunities, which he converted into touchdown passes, was next level. Whether defensive coordinators watch film and study past games, Kubiak always manages to have something new to throw at them. Over reactions The Raiders are getting better on a week-to-week basis and doing it without Brock Bowers. Does that mean they are compiling massive stats? No, not quite, but Bowers nearly played Sunday against the Chargers. When he takes the field and becomes a chess piece at Kubiak’s disposal, the Raiders will become an even more difficult opponent to contend with. At this point, the Raiders are tied with the Kansas City Chiefs for the division lead, with a head-to-head matchup in two weeks. The remaining schedule is a virtual murderer’s row of last year’s playoff teams, but at this point there isn’t a team they can’t beat. If they keep pace with what is being done and how it is being done, it’s very possible the Raiders could start getting flexed into primetime down the road.

title: Raiders News: Week 2 AFC West roundup, Kansas City Chiefs’ overtime win keeps pace with Las Vegas
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders have plenty of momentum in the AFC West after a big Week 2 win over a division rival, the Los Angeles Chargers, which keeps the Raiders in first place and pushes the Chargers to the bottom of the standings at 0-2. On that note, let’s check in on how the Denver […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders have plenty of momentum in the AFC West after a big Week 2 win over a division rival, the Los Angeles Chargers, which keeps the Raiders in first place and pushes the Chargers to the bottom of the standings at 0-2. On that note, let’s check in on how the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs fared on Sunday. Broncos vs. Jaguars Score: 20-13 Broncos win Key Stats: QB Bo Nix: 22/31 (71.0%), 288 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT RB Jonah Coleman: 10 carries, 39 yards, 1 TD WR Jaylen Waddle: 8 catches, 138 yards DT Malcolm Roach: 4 tackles, 1 sack, 2 QB hits, 2 TFLs CB Riley Moss: 2 tackles, 3 PDs Unlike the Chargers, the Denver Broncos managed to escape and avoid digging themselves into a 0-2 hole during their home opener on Sunday. But “escape” is the keyword there, as Denver trailed by two possessions early in the second half and didn’t take the lead until about halfway through the fourth quarter. The Broncos haven’t looked very impressive during the first two weeks, getting blown out by the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 1. Then again, they have played a pair of good opponents, and this is a team that one-possession won its way to a 14-3 record and the AFC Championship last year. The scary part about Denver’s victory over Jacksonville is that Waddle, the club’s big offseason addition, announced his presence on Sunday. Next Week: vs. Los Angeles Rams (SNF) Chiefs vs. Colts Score: 33-30 Chiefs win in OT Key Stats: QB Patrick Mahomes: 32/47 (68.1%), 382 yards, 3 TDs, 0 INTs RB Kenneth Walker: 24 carries, 117 yards, 6 catches, 61 receiving yards TE Travis Kelce: 9 catches, 101 yards, 1 TD LB Nick Bolton: 13 tackles, 1 TFL LB Drue Tranquill: 8 tackles, 2 TFLs, 1 PD After Week 1, this game looked like it would be a cakewalk for the Chiefs. However, it was anything but, with an overtime victory that required two scoring drives from Mahomes and Co. Kansas City’s defense showed some cracks, giving up 119 rushing yards (92 to Jonathan Taylor) and 30 points while failing to sack Indianapolis Colts’ quarterback Daniel Jones. However, the Chiefs’ offense appears to be back after a couple of down years, especially with Walker accounting for nearly 180 yards from scrimmage after 191 last week. That could set up for an interesting battle at Allegiant Stadium in a couple of weeks… Next Week: @ Miami Dolphins Standings Las Vegas 2-0 (+26 point differential) Kansas City 2-0 (+24) Denver 1-1 (-14) Los Angeles (-24) In Other Raiders’ Links: Pressure is up: “The Las Vegas Raiders defense generated a 45.2% pressure rate (81st percentile) against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 2,” per Sumer Sports’ Shawn Syed . “The Raiders defense currently ranks 2nd in the league with a 51.5% pressure rate (98th percentile over two games since 2022).” Brock Bowers close to returning: The tight end was spotted running routes (without pads) during pre-game warm-ups, and Klint Kubiak told reporters Bowers was “very close” to playing in LA, via ESPN’s Ryan McFadden . Raiders look well-coached: “But, they were, by far, the better, more efficient team Sunday as they beat the Los Angeles Chargers 26-14 to improve to 2-0 under new head coach Klint Kubiak,” S&BP’s Bill Williamson wrote. “…Yes, it’s early, but the Raiders appear to be a much improved team and, just as importantly, a well-coached team by Kubiak and his staff.” Raiders still underdogs: Despite being 2-0, the opening odds have Las Vegas as 3.5-point underdogs against the New Orleans Saints next week.

The team looked somewhat promising in the first half — moving the ball well against a stout Niners defense. They trailed by just 8 points at halftime — merely a single touchdown, plus two-point conversion away from making it […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NV - SEPTEMBER 13: Miami Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez (10) walks off of the field after a NFL regular season game between the Las Vegas Raiders and Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium, Sunday September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins were steamrolled in Northern California against the San Francisco 49ers this past Sunday. The team looked somewhat promising in the first half — moving the ball well against a stout Niners defense. They trailed by just 8 points at halftime — merely a single touchdown, plus two-point conversion away from making it a nail-biter. Unfortunately, the Dolphins came out flat in the second-half — both on offense and on defense — and were ultimately trounced by a score of 35-13. Choosing a Most Valuable ‘Phin for Sunday’s game against the 49ers was not an enviable task. There wasn’t much “good” to go around against San Francisco. But… that’s just how this season is going to go, and this job must be done, so I will do it to the best of my ability. Miami Dolphins Week Two MVP – LB Jacob Rodriguez Plenty of people mentioned how Dolphins rookie linebacker Jacob Rodriguez should have won team MVP for his week one performance that saw the youngster notch 14 combined tackles against the Las Vegas Raiders. Well, on Sunday against San Francisco, Rodriguez followed up his stellar week one performance by adding another 8 combined tackles against the 49ers — good for second on the team behind safety Michael Taaffe. It is the second week in a row where a rookie has taken my weekly MVP award, which exemplifies what this season is all about for the Miami Dolphins. This young team needs to establish a solid foundation before it can get flashy. If Miami’s rookies become major contributors this season — and it already looks like Rodriguez is going to be one of those top contributors — the Dolphins will be better in the future for it. MVP TRACKER Week One – WR Caleb Douglas Week Two – LB Jacob Rodriguez

title: Pattern Degradations and Bad Dresses; Miami Dolphins stumble against 49ers
summary: Wow! I wrote about pattern recognition last week and boy did I see some patterns. Bad ones. My grandmother was a seamstress by trade and watching her work when I was boy was very educational. She said “Paul, cut out this pattern section for a dress or blouse and then I will sew them together […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Christian McCaffrey #23 of the San Francisco 49ers stiff arms Chris Johnson #3 of the Miami Dolphins in the first quarter of a game at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wow! I wrote about pattern recognition last week and boy did I see some patterns. Bad ones. My grandmother was a seamstress by trade and watching her work when I was boy was very educational. She said “Paul, cut out this pattern section for a dress or blouse and then I will sew them together and measure for the final fitting. Measure twice. Cut once.” Basic stuff. That was the first time I ever heard the word “pattern.” I did my best but, my grandmother always said you can undercut the pattern but never overcut the pattern because I can’t add the small sections back and the blouse will look silly. This Miami Dolphins team is a bad pattern that is overcut, undercut and not measured properly. Yes, we have terrible scissors, materials and needles. IMHO, this situation is worse than Flores’ first season. Why yes, the situation is different. But I don’t see much to build upon. We should be able to see one small but strong piece. Maybe I just don’t see it. But like back then under Flores, this is a “start from the foundation process” but I feel more scared. The question is why. Darryl Johnston made great points about the “process.” and we have to be okay with suffering under the process. And I get it but I don’t get mistakes from nearly every single position group. Sunday, against the 49ers, it is very hard to tell if it is the talent (or lack thereof) or the schemes/coaching. There were so many bad mistakes that I am not sure where to start to fix. There were simply numerous blown assignments, numerous lack of playmakings and numerous “out-classings.” Example, Michael Taafe tried to go high on Deebo Samuel or George Kittle (can’t remember) and fell off like a baby stroller trying to tackle a freight train. Welcome to the NFL, rookie! Before going any further on the defense, I will give a 15% curve upgrade score to the entire secondary because the pass rush is completely non-existent. We have zero pass-rush talent even when Chop is in there. The last two QBs have not had to worry about getting hit and the WRs know they can run all of their “ingenious routes” according to Darryl Johnston. This is simply ludicrous because ANY offensive system will work, when there is no pressure on the QB or on the RBs. Darryl Johnston probably knows this but has to build up Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan to prop up the NFL lore of how great the players are. Brock Purdy isn’t one-tenth the QB that Dan Marino was. He can run, yes, but his throws are all perimeter precision throws backed by a superior rushing attack. I really do like Brock Purdy but the Wing-T or Run-n-Shoot would have worked perfectly well again this defense. How do we fix the defense? What if we had very good players at every position? Could this coaching staff coach them up? You can’t blame every single defensive SNAFU on the players, many yes but not all of them. What new breakdowns will we see next week against Mahomes? Rest assured, we will see Mr. Kenneth Walker ad infinitum. My last column mentioned how special teams should be the easiest thing to fix. Boy was I wrong!!!!! This punter can’t even hold on to a ball to punt it. How does this happen? Lack of concentration, I think. Yes, I still believe they are using the “K” balls which were originally supposed to come out of the box and handed to the kicker right before it was kicked. I think the NFL has eased up on that (please correct me) so the ball is slickish( I just coined that word ). Last week we couldn’t stop the long returns; for now that seems to be fixed. For now. I should wager which special teams mistake(s) will we make next week. Why in the name of Garo Yepremian has one of our kicker/punter been needed to make a tackle the first two weeks? Who is in charge of special teams? This takes me back to the trepidation about coaching. I contend that special teams is one-third of the game. If you come out neutral on special teams, that is good enough for me. At the National Championship at the Rose Bowl, I watched Auburn lose to FSU on two game changing special teams plays: a fake punt AND a kickoff return. Other than that, Auburn was better than FSU but FSU DOMINATED special teams and deserved to beat Auburn. I don’t want that to happen to the Dolphins and I don’t want mediocrity to be accepted on special teams, offense or defense.
author: Paulie Dorsal

title: Miami Dolphins Week 2 reactions: Tuesday Miami Thoughts With The Earl
summary: That was… I mean… well… what can I say about that?  I had zero expectations about a win, but I hoped it would be somewhat competitive.  It was not.  That just plain sucked.  That is all.  Thank you for reading. Oh, you’re still here?  In that case, I’ll hit on a few things I noticed […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jordyn Brooks #20 and head coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins talk before a game against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images That was… I mean… well… what can I say about that? I had zero expectations about a win, but I hoped it would be somewhat competitive. It was not. That just plain sucked. That is all. Thank you for reading. Oh, you’re still here? In that case, I’ll hit on a few things I noticed from a quick watch of the game. As usge, I will preface by saying the best way to dissect the game if through All-22 film, which I will not get to watch today. Setting the table This loss sucked, but let’s look at it with some aqua-colored glasses for a moment. The 49ers are a Super Bowl contender. The Dolphins are not. There was plenty of discussion this week about the total number of Pro Bowls on the San Francisco 49ers roster versus the Miami Dolphins roster . There was the payroll discrepancy discussion. The broadcast highlighted how the 49ers were the oldest team in the league facing the youngest team in the league. The week prior, the 49ers went across the world to face the Los Angeles Super Rams and left with a 27-7 win. Reigning MVP Matthew Stafford went 15-of-25, 155 yards, no touchdowns, one interception, a passer rating of 61.2, and a QBR of 37.5. He had current 1st-team All-Pro Puka Nacua and three-time 1st-team All-Pro Davante Adams. They were limited to 290 yards of offense, 2-9 on 3rd down, and ran 57 total plays. The Super Rams defense allowed 379 total yards, 27 points, and generated 3 pressures with no sacks despite having the reigning DPOY and single-season sack leader Myles Garrett on their team. The Super Rams were considered THE top contender for the Super Bowl championship this season, and they were shut down by the 49ers. Enter the rebuilding Dolphins. They have a QB with limited NFL snaps, 3 rookie WRs, a ton of rookies on the defensive side of the ball, and are considered THE top contender for the 1st overall draft pick. Remember back in the day when kids would make those paper shuriken ? The Dolphins brought THAT to a nuclear war. Calling this an unfair fight is an understatement. Still, the Dolphins produced 284 yards of offense, were 7-15 on 3rd downs, and Willis had an arguably better stat line than Stafford against this same team in THEIR building. My point is that fans should not view this through the lens of how far away the Dolphins are from contention. We know that – and more on that later. The point is that the 49ers did the same thing to a far superior opponent the week before, and they’ll likely do it to others most weeks. The offense can move the ball One of the few positives from this game is that the Dolphins offense showed they can move the ball. At least in the first half. The Dolphins controlled the clock and generated 155 of their 284 yards in 3 drives. I don’t think it would have changed the outcome, but how different would it have felt if they could have scored a TD or two on those drives? Imagine if they entered halftime 17-14, 14-13, or 14-10 instead of 14-6. I don’t think the defense was stopping the 49ers at all, but let’s say the score after the 49ers’ opening 2nd-half drive is 21-14. Wouldn’t that change how the offense plays? Instead of being down 21-6 and having to force things, they could run a more balanced offense and grind down the clock. Maybe the score still ends up wild, but we would feel a little better knowing they performed well against a top tier opponent. The non-existent pass rush The elephant in the stadium for this Dolphins team isn’t the secondary or Malik Willis. It’s the pass rush that does not exist. Pro Football Focus did not have the advanced stats at the time of writing, but they now show Miami had two QB hits. That’s it. Purdy had all day to throw, and it showed. He had only two incompletions that day. The San Francisco OL is pretty good, and they limited the LA Super Rams to 3 pressures, so let’s not forget that part. But the Dolphins did not generate much pass rush against the Raiders last week. PFF has a preseason ranking of offensive lines , and Miami only plays 1 team listed outside their top 20 – Green Bay at 27th. They face 8 of the top 11 ranked OLs, including the two games against Buffalo (6th) and New England (11th). Based on a quick Google search, the lowest number of sacks ever recorded in a season was the 1956 Packers with 9. In recent history, the 2008 Chiefs only recorded 10 sacks. The 2026 Dolphins will be flirting with this record. I can’t see a game soon where the Dolphins have a good opportunity to get a sack. The Chiefs have a good OL and a QB that can avoid sacks well. The Vikings also have a good OL. This secondary needs all the help it can get and without any pressure up front, games are going to look more like this one. This and that Caleb Douglas was quiet, then got injured. That’s bad news for a team that has nothing at pass catcher. Chris Bell is still working his way back, and he should become a bigger factor. But no one else can get open. Turns out having adequate offensive skill players IS important. Willie Gay Jr. had too many mistakes in this game, and his playing time should be reduced. In fairness, I would expect a rookie like Trey Moore to make mistakes. But WGJ is a veteran and at this point, should be depth and not a starter. Malik Willis is making some inexperienced mistakes that need to be cleaned up. He ran out of bounds behind the line of scrimmage not once, but twice. Those should be throwaways. Those lose yardage and count as sacks on the stat sheet. The box score says he sacked 4 times, but only 2 of those were actual defenders getting him to the ground. These moments are coaching moments, and I kinda understand what he may be thinking. He’s likely thinking “I can make it on the run”, but that window closes quick. He is also missing some throws he should not miss. But that may be because of… The offensive line sucks again. Namely, the right tackle position. Willis and the Dolphins cannot drop back into standard passing situations without getting pressure almost immediately. Jackson is healthy but has now become a liability. For what he gives you in the running game, you lose in pass protection. At some point, the Dolphins really need to consider moving Kadyn Proctor to RT and letting DJ Campbell start at LG. I know that goes against what they said earlier this offseason, but the status quo isn’t working. Caedan Wallace may be the next guy up, but he hasn’t shown enough to feel confident he’ll be an upgrade. The Dolphins may be patient with Jackson, but they may also trade him as soon as they feel it’s necessary. Jackson will not be back in 2027. The Dolphins recently amended his contract, which makes it easier to trade him this season . Now, they won’t get much for him. Maybe a later-round pick swap or perhaps a player-for-player swap. But in a season where the Dolphins will not be competitive, getting something for a player who will be leaving anyway would be a smart move for the GM to make. I said what I said Ok… here is the “more on that later” material. I could write a couple of articles about the draft, free agency, and stuff like positional value. I will wait until the appropriate time for that. But after two weeks, some areas of need for the 2027 offseason are obvious. The Dolphins will need a new right tackle. They will need 2 new edge rushers. There are a few more needs that may become apparent. That is wide receiver, cornerback, safety, guard, tight end, and sigh… quarterback. Last week, I mentioned that Hafley could be on the hot seat quickly if the Dolphins go winless. In a glitch in the matrix, even ct1361 agrees with me . Sorta. I’m not saying he SHOULD be fired, but that is a problem for another day. Back during the draft season, I mentioned how a poorly ran…

(Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins’ 2026 season has started with two straight losses by an average of 18 points. First, the team lost to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 1, then was manhandled by the San Francisco 49ers in Week 2. Heading into Week 3, when they host a rolling Kansas City Chiefs team, the immediate future is a little bleak. That is what happens when a team undergoes a deliberate and deep rebuild. After years of adding high-priced veterans to patch issues with a win-now mentality, the Dolphins have torn apart their roster, turned the game over to younger, developing players, and are taking their lumps with the salary cap. The goal is to continue to get better week-to-week this year, but the South Florida Sun Sentinel’s Chris Perkins suggests things are going to get worse before they get better for Dolphins fans: Rebuilds often suck. That’s just a brutal reality in sports. They are usually painful, which was the case in the Miami Dolphins’ 35-13 loss at the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, and there’s no guarantee of success. I’ve been through enough of these restarts, rebuilds, recalibrations or whatever you want to call this thing that the winless Dolphins (0-2) are undergoing, to know that the fact is this is going to hurt for a while… And the worst part of it is this isn’t rock bottom.
