title: Eagles News: Philadelphia should lean on Jalen Hurts and the passing game more
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Remember the “Let Russ Cook” movement? When Russell Wilson was in his prime as a passer but the Seattle Seahawks insisted on the running the ball over and over, even if it wasn’t working? Feels like we’re reaching that point in […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Remember the “Let Russ Cook” movement? When Russell Wilson was in his prime as a passer but the Seattle Seahawks insisted on the running the ball over and over, even if it wasn’t working? Feels like we’re reaching that point in Philly. The run game isn’t there for the Eagles right now. Maybe it’ll eventually come together … but maybe not. Hurts is looking great. Lean into that on early downs instead of regularly forcing him to bail the offense out on 3rd-and-long! Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … The Day After – Hurts So Good – Iggles Blitz It sure feels like that could be happening again. Hurts has a new scheme and a new OC in Sean Mannion. Hurts is driven to show the world, especially his doubters, that he can be a top flight QB in the NFL. He’s thrown 5 TDs so far this year. He didn’t hit that number until Week 4 last season. The Eagles came into the season expecting to rely on their 2024 formula. Combine a top OL with a dominant run game and a stifling defense. That idea hasn’t worked so far. The Eagles coaches need to consider changing their approach. They should lean on Hurts and the passing game more. Attack on early downs instead of running into loaded boxes. I don’t know that Nick Sirianni would be willing to do this, but he really ought to consider it. Hurts is the team’s best player right now. Embrace that and see what he can do in a more aggressive offense. He’s shown in the past that he can thrive in the right situation. Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 3 – ESPN I think … Jalen Hurts is settling into the Sean Mannion offense. At a team level, I do not love what I’m seeing from the Eagles’ offense. The offensive line looks worse even than it did in 2025, and the running game is suffering as a result — fifth-lowest yards before contact per rush among all teams through two weeks. For the amount of money poured into that unit, that’s scary. Hopefully, guard Landon Dickerson comes back from his injury looking back to form, but we haven’t seen that form in a while; same for center/guard Cam Jurgens. I’m not holding my breath. But Hurts’ Week 2 performance against the Titans was about as good of a game a quarterback can have with a dead-in-the-water rushing attack. Hurts had nine third-down conversions in this game, the most single-game third-down conversions he has had. With no running game, Hurts averaged 7.9 yards to go on third down, well above his career average, and still got big gains in the air, converting three third-and-12 or longer downs (the most in a game in his career). Perhaps most notable of these late conversions was the first one. Hurts hits an intermediate in-breaker to Dontayvion Wicks between the layers of the defense. Updated: Caleb Williams avoided serious injury; is likely ‘week-to-week’ – Windy City Gridiron Hard to imagine Williams playing if he doesn’t even practice for the game at all. UPDATE: Johnson said Williams probably won’t practice this week, but he won’t rule him out for Monday night against the Eagles, adding, “We’re saying week to week with him right now. We’ll see where he’s at as the week progresses and how long that means… It was somewhat encouraging, the report we got.” “He’s right now working through every avenue that he’s got available to get back on track here,” Johnson said about Williams. “We’ll see what that looks like. Here’s what I know. This guy’s a little bit different than the average human being. I said that last night, I’ll double down on that. He gets back – he has in the past – a lot faster than what people can anticipate and so I’m not putting a timeline on this. We’re going to say week to week. He’s going to attack this with everything that he knows.” NFC Hierarchy/Obituary: Week 3 edition – PhillyVoice 4) Eagles (2-0): The Eagles have significant issues, most notably that their run game stinks and the offensive line in general is not playing well. Also, the defense has underwhelmed, although that’s not out of the ordinary early in the season under Vic Fangio. BUT… the major box that has been checked so far is the play of Jalen Hurts, which is kind of a big deal. Zach Ertz arrives in Philly, ‘honored’ to be back in Eagles green – NBCSP “My mom was in tears. My wife was ecstatic,” Ertz said. “My kids, they don’t really understand but I already had the boys practicing the E-A-G-L-E-S chant. So overall it was good. It’s exciting times and, like I said, just really happy to be back. And honored to be back in the Eagles green. But at the end of the day, I’ve got to go earn whatever role I can. So that’s the goal right now.” Ertz, 35, is signing to the Eagles’ practice squad to start. But his arrival comes as we learned on Monday that starting tight end Dallas Goedert will miss the next few weeks with an MCL sprain. If Ertz can get caught up to speed quickly, he’s going to have a chance to contribute as early as Monday night in Chicago. Bowen: Maybe the Eagles could just try to be normal, for once? – PHLY Eagles One consequence of this is that the Eagles are constantly in third-and-long, asking Jalen Hurts to bail them out. So far, he has done that, but an offense that lives in third-and-long is an offense that is ripe for disaster. Comrade EJ Smith’s excellent postgame piece from Nashville noted the SumerSports observation that the Eagles have the largest difference between early-down offensive success rate vs. Late-down success rate to start a season since 2022. It’s 31.5% on first down, 60.6% on third down, a tribute to Hurts and to his receiving corps. (Which now seems likely to be missing Dallas Goedert, at least for a little while). Left tackle Jordan Mailata’s postgame comments were encouraging, pointing out that an O-line needs continuity, and that presumably, the current unit can now get some time on task. Eagles survive Titans behind Jalen Hurts. Here’s what Philadelphia must fix next – The Athletic The Eagles averaged 2.5 yards on their stretch run concepts. The tape again showed blockers failing to secure the seam that could break a big run. Cam Jurgens, playing left guard for the first time, whiffed on linebacker Cody Barton, who limited Tank Bigsby to a 4-yard gain on a play that had room to be much more. The Eagles later attempted two stretch plays behind right guard Tyler Steen. The runs totaled three yards. The plodding concepts seemed to lead the Eagles into a first-and-10 toss play in the second quarter in which Will Shipley gained seven yards. Mannion also ran the pistol for the first time — apparently to stimulate the run game. They ran four plays in the set. They brought in a tight end as a fullback on two of the plays. Mundt was in the backfield when Hurts pulled a third-and-4 zone-read keeper and gained the four yards he needed. Bigsby gained 11 yards on three rushes. At times, the Eagles found more success running the ball inside from the shotgun. Bigsby gained four yards on a second-and-10 run on the first drive. Shipley later gained five yards on a similar first-down run. The offensive line also wasn’t always at fault. Running backs seemed to shift away from intended holes in search of the big run. Barkley cut rightward into the backs of blockers on the first play. Bigsby did a similar thing on a later second-and-8 run, cutting rightward into traffic when a narrow hole was available to the left. The Eagles had no rushes of 10 or more yards for only the fifth time since 2021. Such explosive runs are vital to a system that intends to play pass and run off each other by creating similar looks. “Our runs are all three or four yards,” Johnson said. “Hardly any explosives, which was tough for us. When…

title: Nick Sirianni thinks the Eagles’ run game is close
summary: The Eagles run game has struggled through two games to open the 2026 season, and that was the main focus when head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters on Monday, following the team’s win in Tennessee. Sirianni highlighted the sacrifice that Cam Jurgens made by being willing to move over to left guard, acknowledging that […]
full_text: The Eagles run game has struggled through two games to open the 2026 season, and that was the main focus when head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters on Monday, following the team’s win in Tennessee. Sirianni highlighted the sacrifice that Cam Jurgens made by being willing to move over to left guard, acknowledging that the majority of his time this offseason and through training camp was at the center position. He noted that there are opportunities for some cross training within walkthroughs, and Jurgens did play right guard in the past. “But, [Cam Jurgens] sure got a lot of reps this week at [left guard] and thought he came out against a really good defensive front and played a solid game.” As for the slow start for the Eagles run game, Sirianni said that it’s a collaborative effort, from coaches to players, so it’s not just on the running backs or offensive linemen. He explained that it takes every player on the field to be successful in the run game, and it’s a full team effort to be better – which he knows they are capable of doing. “And we’re close. We are close. But it goes back to when you’re close, it’s never just one thing. It’s the entire group working as a whole. We have to be committed to it still and keep grinding away at it, but we know we have room to improve there in our run game.” The head coach also talked about the number of negative plays through two games, to which he pointed mostly to the run game, but also blamed penalties and sacks. “Negative plays, you always want to stay on track. It’s hard to move the ball forward. Let’s say you get a kickoff at the 30-yard line, and you’ve got to go 70 yards. Well, it’s hard to go those 70 yards if you’re moving backwards. Regardless of if it’s a sack, a negative run, a penalty, even a drop pass that doesn’t move it forward at all, a missed throw, whatever it may be; It’s hard to go the length of the field when you’re moving backwards. That’s always going to be a point of emphasis of what we need to do.” Sirianni took an opportunity to applaud Tank Bigsby for always playing extremely hard and having some dirty runs. “I think about that one that’s down near the goal line where he keeps his feet driving and gets us all the way down to the three and then caps it off [with] the touchdown. Obviously, a great sequence there for Tank. Tank made a tackle on special teams yesterday on punt that was pretty awesome to see. Tank’s a guy that constantly — he’s such a good teammate and he’s constantly doing the little things he needs to do to help the team win. It’s great to see him be rewarded with a touchdown yesterday and a couple nice runs. You knew he would be ready to go. I thought he played solidly.”
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Zach Ertz is back!
summary: There’s been a lot of speculation this offseason about whether the Eagles would bring Zach Ertz back, especially given the lack of depth in the tight end room. After learning that Dallas Goedert will miss several weeks following an MCL sprain, the reunion with Ertz is happening! This always made a lot of sense, even […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 14: Tight end Zach Ertz #86 of the Philadelphia Eagles celebrates with quarterback Jalen Hurts #1 after catching a first quarter touchdown pass against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Lincoln Financial Field on October 14, 2021 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images There’s been a lot of speculation this offseason about whether the Eagles would bring Zach Ertz back, especially given the lack of depth in the tight end room. After learning that Dallas Goedert will miss several weeks following an MCL sprain , the reunion with Ertz is happening! Three-time Pro-Bowl tight end Zach Ertz, who played in Philadelphia from 2013-‘21 and helped the team win its first Super Bowl, is returning to the city and signing with the Eagles practice squad, per sources. The Eagles lost TE Dallas Goedert to a sprained MCL and now are… pic.twitter.com/535cB3Kaio — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 21, 2026 This always made a lot of sense, even before Goedert was sidelined. The team placed rookie TE Eli Stowers on IR at the start of the season, and Grant Calcaterra was put on IR at the end of training camp. With just Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins left, the TE room gets an immediate boost by adding Ertz. The former Eagles draft pick has spent his time away from Philly with the Cardinals and Commanders, and has been a consistent factor in the redzone — regardless of the overall effectiveness of those offenses. Ertz is also just 11 receptions away from breaking Harold Carmichael’s franchise record (589) in Philadelphia to become the team’s leader all-time in catches. Ertz has shown the City of Philadelphia and the Eagles nothing but love since he left several years ago, and has grown emotional several times when talking about the appreciation he has for the team. This reunion is the perfect way for him to finish out his career, while also being an instant contributor once he’s acclimated and brought up to speed.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Dallas Goedert injury: Eagles tight end will miss time with MCL sprain
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are suddenly dealing with a problem at tight end. Starter Dallas Goedert left the team’s Week 2 game early with a knee injury and additional testing revealed he suffered a sprained MCL and is expected to to miss several weeks. Whether or not the team decided to put Goedert on injured reserve […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dallas Goedert #88 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are suddenly dealing with a problem at tight end. Starter Dallas Goedert left the team’s Week 2 game early with a knee injury and additional testing revealed he suffered a sprained MCL and is expected to to miss several weeks. #Eagles TE Dallas Goedert, who continues to be a big part of their offense, suffered a sprained MCL in Sunday’s win over the #Titans , test revealed today. He’s expected to miss a few weeks, sources told me and @AdamSchefter . pic.twitter.com/VPllwDXLi8 — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) September 21, 2026 Whether or not the team decided to put Goedert on injured reserve remains to be seen. If they do go that route prior to Week 3, Goedert will miss at least the following four games: Week 3 at Chicago Bears Week 4 vs. Los Angeles Rams Week 5 at Jacksonville Jaguars (London) Week 6 vs. Carolina Panthers The earliest he would be eligible to return is for the Eagles’ Week 7 game against … Dallas. (How fitting.) In the meantime, the Eagles are looking very thin at tight end. Johnny Mundt, who entered the season as TE2, is currently the top option. He’s clearly not much of a pass-catching threat, as evidenced by his career average of 5.7 yards per game. E.J. Jenkins made the roster as a blocking tight end and special teams contributor. The Eagles currently have two tight ends on injured reserve: Eli Stowers and Grant Calcaterra. Both players are ineligible to return to the active roster until Week 5 at the earliest. And the rookie Stowers didn’t exactly show much promise in training camp (he never even repped with the first-team offense to work with Jalen Hurts) while Calcacterra has developed a reputation as a blocking liability. The Eagles’ best course of action, it seems, would be to bring Zach Ertz back to Philly . It remains to be seen how much Ertz, who turns 36 years old in November, has left in the tank while coming off an injury that cut his 2025 season short. But prior to getting hurt he still looked pretty capable of making meaningful contributions. We’ll see how the Eagles end up going about this.

title: Jalen Hurts finally beat Robert Saleh
summary: Everyone was focused on Jeffery Simmons’ comments heading into the Week 2 Eagles-Titans matchup and how Jalen Hurts might respond. It turns out the Eagles QB proved himself, but Simmons may have just been collateral damage for whom Hurts was really focused on beating. “Got a lot of respect for Coach Saleh. [It’s] finally good […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Head Coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans congratulates Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles with their 24-20 win after the game at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Everyone was focused on Jeffery Simmons’ comments heading into the Week 2 Eagles-Titans matchup and how Jalen Hurts might respond. It turns out the Eagles QB proved himself, but Simmons may have just been collateral damage for whom Hurts was really focused on beating. “Got a lot of respect for Coach Saleh. [It’s] finally good to get him. He’s posed some great challenges, obviously, but kind of checked that off.” His comments reflected a greater awareness of the coaches he’s struggled against and a commitment to making sure he gets the last laugh. The Eagles beat the Jets in 2021, Saleh’s first year as head coach, but Hurts was inactive due to an ankle injury. Then, in 2022, it was Saleh’s Jets in the preseason that hit Jalen Hurts late out of bounds, and led to Sirianni screaming at Saleh across the field — it’s also the reason Sirianni doesn’t play starters anymore in the preseason. The next two times Philly faced a Saleh-led team or defense, the results were not great. In 2023, the Eagles lost to the Jets, 14-20, in what would be their first loss of the season and the only loss through 12 games for the Birds. Aside from the final score, it was a rough day for Hurts, who finished 28-of-45 for 280 yards, one touchdown, and three interceptions. Hurts had another chance for redemption against a Saleh defense less than a year ago, when the Eagles faced the San Francisco 49ers in the first round of the 2025 playoffs. The Eagles lost 19-23, and while Hurts was able to avoid so many turnover traps, he had rough day opposite DC Saleh, finishing 20-of-35 for 168 yards and just one touchdown. Now with the Titans, Saleh once again made things challenging for Hurts and the Eagles offense, but this time, Philly’s quarterback was able to put the game on his back and carry the team to a win. The QB finished 26-of-37 for 264 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions — although, one of those wasn’t his fault. And as a result, Hurts can check off “Beat Robert Saleh” from whatever list of revenge he’s keeping.
author: Alexis Chassen

title: Eagles-Titans snap counts: Darius Cooper makes the case for more playing time
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans are in! Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Andy Dalton INACTIVE: Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, Elijah Moore, Jonathan Greenard, Micah Morris
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Darius Cooper #80 of the Philadelphia Eagles catches the game winning touchdown during the second half of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans are in! Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Drew Kendall made his second career regular season start at center. He previously made his first in Week 18 last year when the Eagles were resting starters. Cam Jurgens made his first career start at left guard. He struggled but he barely has any experience in that specific spot. As expected, DeVonta Smith led all Eagles skill players in playing time once again. His team-high 13 targets were more than double the next closest player, which was Dontayvion Wicks with six. Smitty logged 11 receptions for 117 yards and a touchdown. Dallas Goedert’s knee injury led to Johnny Mundt taking over as the top tight end option. That’s just not ideal. The Eagles need to get serious and add more help at this position, especially if Goedert has to miss significant time. Get Zach Ertz on the phone. Makai Lemon’s snap count percentage in Week 1 was 64%. That figure basically remained unchanged in Week 2. But whereas the rookie saw four targets against the Commanders, he only had two total touches against the Titans. Dontayvion Wicks actually played slightly less than Lemon but he was apparently a little banged up at one point during the game before being able to return. He was WR2 in terms of usage with his six targets producing 74 yards … and all on either third down or fourth down. Hurts is demonstrating that he trusts Donny Candles. With Saquon Barkley suffering a stinger injury on the first play of the game, the Eagles split his workload between Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby. Bigsby had more total touches with 15 (for 38 yards and a touchdown) to Shipley’s nine (for 29 yards). But the Eagles trust Shipley more in pass protection, so, that’s why he ultimately played more often. Great to see the Eagles get Darius Cooper more involved in this game. In Week 1, he played just eight snaps and saw zero targets. Against the Titans, his snap count percentage increased by 26% as he logged three targets for 26 yards and the game-winning touchdown! He would’ve had even more yardage had Hurts not thrown a pass a little too far out in front of him at one point. Good things happen when the Eagles throw the ball to DC. They should continue to give him a role in this offense. Between flashing potential on offense and working hard on special teams, he’s earned it. E.J. Jenkins moved up the depth chart from TE3 to TE2 with Goedert getting hurt. Still has yet to see a target this season, which is to be expected. Hollywood Brown played zero snaps on offense or special teams despite being active in Week 1. The Eagles got him more involved in Week 2; he took two handoffs that gained 12 yards. Not bad. DEFENSE Cooper DeJean was able to handle 100% of the Eagles’ defensive snaps despite being listed on the injury report leading up to Week 2. But this was the first time in his career that he played in a game and did not appear on special teams at all. DeJean, Zack Baun, and Quinyon Mitchell are the only Eagles defenders to not miss a snap so far this season. Andrew Mukuba missed just one snap despite entering this game questionable to play with a knee injury that he apparently picked up in practice. Riq Woolen had another good outing while playing most of the game. Moro Ojomo overtook Jalen Carter as the Eagles’ top defensive tackle in terms of playing time. Carter did play this game with a cast on his hand and he also cramped up in the fourth quarter. Jalyx Hunt continues to be the Eagles’ top edge rusher in terms of playing time. It looked like he got banged up later in the game. Nolan Smith wasn’t far behind Hunt in terms of playing time. Marcus Epps’ snap count percentage was similar to what it was in Week 1. Unlike last weekend, however, he really struggled. Jordan Davis’ snap count percentage dropped by about 5% from Week 1 to Week 2. Arnold Ebiketie continues to be the third edge rusher with A.J. Epenesa as the fourth guy in the rotation. Byron Young had a bigger role in Week 2 than he had in Week 1. Perhaps due to the combination of the heat and Carter cramping. Might be time soon, if it’s not already, to get Michael Carter II more involved at safety. Ty Robinson actually saw some playing time on defense this week. It wasn’t much. Jonathan Jones logged his first career defensive snaps with the Eagles. SPECIAL TEAMS Jeremiah Trotter Jr. looked good on special teams coverage, logging two ST tackles. Britain Covey continues to serve as the Eagles’ punt returner. Maximus Pulley was limited to special teams duty in his NFL regular season debut after being temporarily elevated from the practice squad. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Andy Dalton INACTIVE: Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, Elijah Moore, Jonathan Greenard, Micah Morris Dalton was QB2 once again with McKee serving as the emergency third quarterback. Moore was a healthy scratch behind six receivers who played in this game. Greenard might be able to return in Week 3? It’ll be interesting to see if he’s able to ramp up to full participation in practice as the Eagles prepare to face the Chicago Bears. The pass rush could sure use him. Morris was a healthy scratch behind eight active offensive linemen, as expected. The Eagles still have one open roster spot to fill.
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Eagles News: “Sean Mannion took a big step forward this week”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Music City Magic – Iggles Blitz I thought Sean Mannion took a big step forward this week. The Eagles gained 341 yards and had 23 first downs (only had 10 last week). There are still things to work on, like getting […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 04: Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 4th, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Center in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Music City Magic – Iggles Blitz I thought Sean Mannion took a big step forward this week. The Eagles gained 341 yards and had 23 first downs (only had 10 last week). There are still things to work on, like getting rid of the passes to Makai Lemon behind the line of scrimmage. But overall Mannion did a good job. The run game was more creative. We saw Hollywood Brown on a couple of end around plays. And Mannion made a nice adjustment on the winning TD. Judging the biggest overreactions to NFL Week 2 games – ESPN Sure, Hurts was pressured a lot, but he was awesome Sunday when pressured. He was 11-for-20 for 137 yards and two touchdowns, including the winning TD in the final seconds. Saquon Barkley left this game early with an injury, and although he came back briefly in the second half, he wasn’t able to finish the contest. That surely emboldened the Titans’ pressure plan. I get that it doesn’t look great or smooth. But it’s Week 2, and the Eagles are 2-0 while they’re putting things together. Two of the big questions coming into this season were whether Hurts could thrive with all the change that was made around him and whether DeVonta Smith could fill the No. 1 receiver role with A.J. Brown traded to New England. Well, Hurts was heroic in leading the comeback, and Smith caught 10 passes for 117 yards and a touchdown. There are a lot of offenses with a lot less hope than the Eagles deserve to have in theirs right now. Eagles vs. Titans: 7 winners, 5 losers, 5 IDKs – BGN If you didn’t watch the game and only looked at the box score, you might think Hurts had a relatively pedestrian day at the office: 26/37 (70.3 completion), 264 yards (7.1 average), 2 TD, 2 INT, 85.9 passer rating … 5 carries, 16 rushing yards. But such a sentiment couldn’t be further from the case. Hurts was a huge reason why the Eagles won this game. Let’s start at the end. The Eagles were down three points at their own 35-yard line with 1:56 on the clock and zero timeouts to work with. Hurts led a nine-play, 65-yard drive where he accounted for all of those yards (61 passing, four rushing) and the game-winning touchdown pass. His only two incompletions were a short drop by Dontayvion Wicks and a throwaway to avoid a sack with pressure quickly reaching him. Hurts delivered in the clutch. It was a well-deserved ending for him, too, since he was tasked with carrying the offense for most of the game. The Eagles did Hurts no favors by insisting on sticking with an ineffective running game on early downs … which forced the offense into way too many third-and-longs. Hurts made some really good throws in those situations to sustain drives. Eagles 24 Titans 20 quick recap – Music City Miracles There are no moral victories in the NFL, but the Tennessee Titans, as a team, have a lot to be proud of even in the 24-20 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. After the way they played last week, I was 100% sure they were going to lose by 3 touchdowns. They fought all the way to the finish today. There is still a lot of stuff to clean up. The defense was on the field the entire first half. They have to find a way to get off the field. To their credit, they were much better in the second half. They also picked Jalen Hurts off twice in the loss. They still need more from the offense. Part of the reason the defense was on the field so much in the first half was because the offense couldn’t sustain a drive. Eagles-Titans Postgame: Eagles 2-0, Jalen Hurts Delivers Game-Winning TD To Darius Cooper – PHLY Eagles Super Bowl champion Vinny Curry is with us to break down Jalen Hurts’ game-winning drive that delivered the Eagles a 24-20 win and included two spectacular DeVonta Smith catches. We break down a wild game that included two interceptions by Jalen Hurts, injuries to Saquon Barkley and Dallas Goedert, and some weird football. No matter, the Eagles escaped to stay undefeated. Miles Johnston, Brandon Lee Gowton and Bo Wulf join Curry, with insight from EJ Smith from the Eagles locker room and Fran Duffy on the plays you need to know. Eagles and Titans players had their cleats melting in 157-degree heat – SB Nation Not only did players see their cleats physically melting on the field, but the heat caused the composition of the cleats to change, with Jordan Mailata saying that he rolled his ankle twice on Sunday — and believed it could have been caused by the plastic of his cleats becoming soft due to the heat. Conditions were so extreme that Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni got an IV at halftime to prevent dehydration, which came from just standing on the surface for 90 minutes. Players struggled to keep cool, and it’s raising more questions about player safety due to weather-related events, especially as it pertains to playing surfaces. Given the chance to mask Eagles’ offensive woes, Jalen Hurts ‘didn’t flinch’ in clutch time vs. the Titans – PHLY Eagles He found Dontayvion Wicks for a 20-yard completion with the Eagles facing third-and-6 near midfield and hit DeVonta Smith, who pulled off two acrobatic catches on the final drive, for a 19 yard completion facing the same down and distance a few plays later. And with the Eagles facing first-and-goal from the three-yard line, Hurts rolled to his right and found Darius Cooper wide open in the middle of the end zone to secure the decisive lead. “That motherfucker balled out today,” Eagles left tackle Jordan Mailata said. “Jalen really got in his bag today and just started dialing everything up and hitting everyone.” Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Titans game – PhillyVoice 4) The ‘Dirty Work’ Award 🧹🧽: Darius Cooper. Being the dirty work receiver is hard. You play special teams and when you get in the game on offense you’re usually just blocking or running pick plays for the star players. And yet, when you get your opportunities, you sure as hell better be ready because you’re not going to get many of them. Cooper had two catches for 26 yards, and the game-winning TD. 2026 NFL season, Week 2: What We Learned from Sunday’s games – NFL.com Hurts comes in clutch after tough outing. It wasn’t the best day at the office for Jalen Hurts, but when met with a deadline — needing to lead a game-winning drive with 1:56 remaining — the Super Bowl LIX Most Valuable Player delivered. Hurts, who threw a bad interception in the end zone during his first possession and another pick during the drive immediately preceding his last, led Philly on a nine-play, 65-yard drive to take the lead and the win from the Titans. He did so by becoming laser-focused on DeVonta Smith, throwing to the Eagles’ No. 1 wide receiver on four of eight passes, including a pretty 19-yard gain on third-and-6 to set up Philadelphia at the goal line. On the next play, he hit Darius Cooper for the wideout’s first career touchdown to propel the Eagles to a surprisingly difficult win. He wasn’t nearly perfect Sunday, going 26 of 37 for 264 yards, two touchdowns and the two picks, but he was clutch as ever when called upon to leave Titans fans with some achy, breaky hearts. The Eagles need Jalen Hurts 2.0 now more than ever. His evolution and clutch gene are carrying a rough offense. – Inquirer But there was something unique about Hurts carrying the offense at the scorching Nissan Stadium on Sunday. He’s strapped the Eagles on his back before. He’s had better games against better opponents when the stakes were much higher. He’s been clutch on many previous occasions. No, this was a different Hurts. This was the 2.0 version. This was Hurts evolving as a quarterback in a new scheme that gives him more freedom as a…
author: Brandon Lee Gowton

title: Eagles-Titans Takeaway: Jalen Hurts can handle the heat
summary: They wanted to make Jalen Hurts beat them as a quarterback. That’s what Tennessee star defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons (who was a monster on Sunday) said about the Eagles’ star QB ahead of the Birds’ come-from-behind 24-20 win on Sunday that was orchestrated by Hurts’ arm and, in no small measure, a wonderful game by […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks to pass the ball against the Tennessee Titans during the second half of the game at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) | Getty Images They wanted to make Jalen Hurts beat them as a quarterback. That’s what Tennessee star defensive tackle Jeffrey Simmons (who was a monster on Sunday) said about the Eagles’ star QB ahead of the Birds’ come-from-behind 24-20 win on Sunday that was orchestrated by Hurts’ arm and, in no small measure, a wonderful game by a wide receiver corps filled with question marks. The plan was simple: keep Hurts in the pocket and, as Simmons said, “make Jalen Hurts be a QB.” Hurts was not perfect. He almost never is. He threw two interceptions, one of which was almost returned for a 90+ yard pick-six and the other late in the fourth quarter as he was hit while he was throwing. They were uncharacteristic of him, but in the new Sean Mannion offense, we may have to get used to things like this. But for most of the game and, most importantly, in their final drive, Hurts was masterful. He was 26-for-37 passing with 264 yards and two touchdowns and, with under two minutes remaining and trailing 20-17, went 6-for-8 on a 65-yard drive that culminated in 3-yard touchdown to Darius Cooper with 9 seconds left. View this post on Instagram It was not an easy game. The Titans were fired up and the Eagles had never won a game in Tennessee since the Houston Oilers moved to Nissan Stadium in 1999. It was also about 357 degrees Farenheit on the field. Players’ cleats were melting. Hurts also had to deal with an offensive line that is still finding its footing in the new Mannion scheme. He was under pressure for much of the day, yet managed to pass his way through it. Jalen Hurts' passing chart vs. the Titans. Per @NextGenStats , Hurts was pressured 17 times on his dropbacks, including 14 of them vs. four-man rushes (three sacks too). Hurts completed a career-high 18 passes on 28 attempts and both TD throws that took longer than 2.5 seconds to… pic.twitter.com/8wWwQjnyDd — Devin Jackson (@RealD_Jackson) September 20, 2026 With Landon Dickerson out, the Eagles moved Cam Jurgens from center to left guard and started Drew Kendall at center. That didn’t seem to work out too well. The running game provided little support, averaging 2.8 yards per attempt. Saquon Barkley missed almost the entire first half with a stinger and finished with just 9 yards on 4 attempts. Tank Bigsby scored a touchdown on the ground but managed just 33 yards on 13 carries. Will Shipley added 24 yards on 7 carries. So, it was all on Hurts. Hurts threw over the middle of the field more, threading the needle in some cases and layering passes over linebackers in others. There were times he took too long to get rid of the ball, but also seemed more inclined to let it rip than in seasons past. He was also aided by his top two veteran wide receivers, as well as a second-year training camp star. DeVonta Smith showed why everyone was excited for him to take over as WR1. He hauled in 10 of his 13 targets for 117 yards and a touchdown, making several acrobatic catches in traffic along the way. Especially clutch was his last catch of the day on the final drive. View this post on Instagram One of the more important developments early in the season is the play of Dontayvion Wicks, who is emerging as a more-than viable No. 2. He caught 5 of his 6 targets for 74 yards, including a 27-yarder that helped get the Eagles’ offense moving early. And while Cooper did not pile up big stats on Sunday, he did come up with the biggest catch of the day in the game’s final seconds, and even Makai Lemon showed up with a clutch 14-yard catch. Hurts completed passes to nine different players, an offensive coordinator’s dream. Hurts will never be confused with Joe Montana, but he is proving to be one of the most adaptable QBs in franchise history. It’s only been two games, and we haven’t truly seen Mannion’s offense “work” yet. The running game needs to be functional in order for that to happen. In the meantime, Hurts is doing more than enough inside the system and, improvisationally, to win. Yes, it feels a lot like last year still. It seems unlikely the Eagles are going be blowing people out this year, at least not yet. In the meantime, Hurts is showing that, after an off-season of uncertainty, he can handle the heat.
author: John Stolnis

title: Steelers vs. Bengals: Opening odds for Week 3 matchup
summary: Nothing seemed to go right for the Steelers as they fell to 1-1 after an embarrassing loss to the New England Patriots in Week 2. Aaron Rodgers and the offense struggled to move the ball downfield against a stout Patriots defense. Rodgers and the offense have a new challenge ahead this week as they are […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 16: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers throws a pass against the Cincinnati Bengals during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium on November 16, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin Berl/Getty Images) | Getty Images Nothing seemed to go right for the Steelers as they fell to 1-1 after an embarrassing loss to the New England Patriots in Week 2. The Bengals are off to a red-hot 2-0 start to their season with wins over Tampa Bay and Houston. FanDuel Sportsbook is thinking we will see more dominance from Cincinnati in Week 3, as they favor the Bengals by -3.5 points on the road. You can get the Steelers to win outright at +144 here. Will we see some offensive explosives from these teams in Week 3? The total for the game is currently set at 42.5. These teams split their games last season, with Cincinnati picking up a 33-31 victory on October 16th, before Pittsburgh responded with a resounding 34-12 victory later in the season on November 16th. Getting back on track with a win at home over a division opponent would restore faith in a lot of Steelers fans. title: The morning after: Steelers need to make sweeping offensive line changes
summary: Sometimes when you add new people to new roles, it ends up working seamlessly. There is no layover of production, there is no adjustment period, it’s just full steam ahead and a big success that leaves everyone looking smarter because of it. Other times, you’re the Pittsburgh Steelers offensive line. Pittsburgh’s front five have been […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 23: Spencer Anderson #74 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on November 23, 2025 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Sometimes when you add new people to new roles, it ends up working seamlessly. There is no layover of production, there is no adjustment period, it’s just full steam ahead and a big success that leaves everyone looking smarter because of it. Other times, you’re the Pittsburgh Steelers offensive line. Pittsburgh’s front five have been largely abysmal through two weeks, but Week 2 in their 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots was especially bad. If you spent the afternoon screaming at your TV about how bad Spencer Anderson was playing, your eyes certainly weren’t deceiving you. Anderson allowed seven pressures from the right guard position, which was the most of any right guard in the NFL, per Sumer Sports . No other player at his position allowed more than four pressures in Week 2, and he is currently third in the NFL in pressures allowed through the first two weeks. Zach Frazier was also credited with five pressures – and you know it’s a bad day when even Frazier is getting beat. However, how much of that can be credited with having Anderson next to him? I’d say that’s certainly not a small factor. Right tackle Dylan Cook hasn’t been any better, allowing six pressures through two games. Additionally, the Steelers cannot run to the right side. After two games, Rico Dowdle has just 13 rushing yards on seven carries when running to the right side – good for the fifth worst EPA per rush to that side in the NFL (min. 10 touches). Jaylen Warren has been slightly better, but he only has 37 yards on seven carries to the right side. The Steelers’ running backs also haven’t been able to get to the second level before getting hit by defenders. Through two weeks, Warren and Dowdle have a combined eight yards before contact on runs. EIGHT! That is comfortably the worst mark in the NFL. The Steelers’ plan at offensive line entering the season was one that left many skeptical and we’re now seeing why. They moved their rising star right tackle and quality right guard to the left side for precisely no reason, moved the former practice squad fill-in to right tackle after he played well at left tackle, and didn’t find a suitable replacement for Isaac Seumalo. All of these moving parts have led to a very discombobulated unit that can’t block its way out of a wet bag, and it’s destroying the offense. Under the previous regime, this would be a leak in the boat that wouldn’t get fixed for weeks on end. If Mike McCarthy wants to show that things truly will be different, he’ll ensure that both Anderson and Cook don’t start in Week 3. It’s the morning after game day, and your concerns are absolutely justified. Germie Bernard arrives There were very few aspects of Week 2 that could be considered good for the Steelers, but one of those things was the play of Germie Bernard. Entering Week 2, his counterpoint, Roman Wilson, had just one career game where he had four or more receptions – Bernard accomplished that feat in his second game. Aaron Rodgers found him three times on one drive that looked poised to end in points, but then the 3rd-and-7 sack happened and knocked the Steelers out of field goal range. Bernard did have a blunder at the end of the game that saw a ball bounce off his chest for an interception, but the game was already decided. We need to see more of No. 17 on the field going forward. Defense continues strong play Through two games, the Steelers’ defense has been great. They’ve allowed 26 points, taken the ball away four times, and lead the NFL in defensive EPA. per play. They comfortably have the best pass defense in the league from an efficiency standpoint, allowing -0.5 EPA per pass, and they are third in defensive pass success rate. T.J. Watt has 3.5 sacks – he had seven all of last season, and currently sits at No. 2 in the NFL behind only Greg Rousseau of the Buffalo Bills. Additionally, of all edge rushers with at least 25 snaps, Watt and Alex Highsmith are No. 1 and No. 2 in the NFL in sack percentage. The defense is more than holding up its end of the bargain, and Patrick Graham has already proven to be a massive improvement over Teryl Austin. The offense is holding back any potential of Pittsburgh being a real competitor. If they can fix it and become just a mediocre offense, they can win games. title: Mike Macdonald says ‘there’s a chance’ Sam Darnold practices in Week 3
summary: The Seattle Seahawks didn’t miss a beat without their starting quarterback, Sam Darnold. Drew Lock deputized for Darnold and threw three touchdowns to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Seattle’s 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals. While Lock showed he’s more than capable of running the offense in Darnold’s absence, Darnold’s return could happen as early as Week […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Sam Darnold #14 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up before kickoff against the New England Patriots during an NFL football game at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks didn’t miss a beat without their starting quarterback, Sam Darnold. Drew Lock deputized for Darnold and threw three touchdowns to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in Seattle’s 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals. While Lock showed he’s more than capable of running the offense in Darnold’s absence, Darnold’s return could happen as early as Week 3 versus the Washington Commanders. There has been constant speculation and reporting regarding Darnold’s timetable to return from his glute injury, with the worst case scenario in the 4-6 week timeline . More recent reports have been more optimistic, with Week 4 against the Los Angeles Chargers as the targeted return for Darnold. Based on Mike Macdonald’s comments following Sunday’s game, Darnold may be able to return to practice this week. “We’re optimistic,” Macdonald said. “We’ll see. I think there’s a chance that he comes back and practices at some point., but I think the timetable has shifted quite drastically in 10 days or whatever. We’ve got 30% of that time to kind of see where it’s going between now and Wednesday.” Coach Macdonald also added that “it’s possible” he plays against the Commanders. I’m willing to bet that they’ll give Darnold one more week on the sidelines, even if he does get some practice reps in this week. Worst case scenario was avoided for the Seahawks on multiple fronts. Darnold does not have a long-term injury and Lock was fantastic against the Cardinals. With Dan Quinn’s Commanders pass defense struggling to do almost anything right, Lock could be in for another big afternoon.

title: This jaw-dropping stat sums up Seahawks defensive dominance vs. Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks routed the Arizona Cardinals by a score of 31-7 on Sunday, marking their 10th consecutive win over their NFC West foes. We’ve seen our fair share of Seahawks blowout wins over Arizona, most famously the 58-0 annihilation back in 2012, but the defensive performance by Seattle is worthy of a special mention. […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals runs with the ball against the Seattle Seahawks at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks routed the Arizona Cardinals by a score of 31-7 on Sunday , marking their 10th consecutive win over their NFC West foes. We’ve seen our fair share of Seahawks blowout wins over Arizona, most famously the 58-0 annihilation back in 2012, but the defensive performance by Seattle is worthy of a special mention. Outside of one garbage time run by Bam Knight, the Cardinals did not have a single offensive play gain more than nine yards. Jacoby Brissett completed 17 passes for a grand total of 95 yards, while Trey McBride’s eight catches (and touchdown) traveled a combined 41 yards. This incredible stat by Cardinals beat writer Theo Mackie shows that Mike Macdonald’s defense did something to the Cardinals not seen since they were still in St. Louis… and using replacement players during the NFL strike. Today was the first time the Cardinals did not complete a pass for 10+ yards since Oct. 11, 1987. Their replacement players beat the Saints in that game despite completing three passes for 11 yards. It was their last season in St. Louis. — Theo Mackie (@theo_mackie) September 21, 2026 The box score for the New Orleans Saints and Cardinals is absolutely hilarious when you consider the Saints would finish the season 12-3. Replacement quarterbacks Shawn Halloran and Sammy Garza combined for 3/10 for 11 yards, but the Cardinals won 24-19 thanks to a pair of fumble return touchdowns and a 26-yard touchdown drive in which nearly every play was a rush attempt. The Cardinals as a franchise have been extremely inept, so the fact that the Seahawks managed to create a level of ineptitude not seen for decades is remarkable. Explosive plays? Arizona didn’t even come close to a semi-explosive pass. Mike Macdonald has the reigning champions off to a hot defensive start, which is terrifying for the rest of the league considering Nick Emmanwori is slowly making his way back from injury and Ty Okada has been out with a hamstring pull.

title: Snap Reactions: Seahawks show depth in stomping Cardinals
summary: The Seattle Seahawks went on the road to take on the Arizona Cardinals Sunday in the first divisional match up of the year for either team. Arizona kept things close early, but Seattle pulled away in the second half, with the final tally giving the Seahawks a 31-7 win to keep pace with the San […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Abraham Lucas #72, Christian Haynes #64, Jalen Sundell #61, Grey Zabel #76, and Charles Cross #67 of the Seattle Seahawks look on during the first quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Seattle Seahawks went on the road to take on the Arizona Cardinals Sunday in the first divisional match up of the year for either team. Arizona kept things close early, but Seattle pulled away in the second half, with the final tally giving the Seahawks a 31-7 win to keep pace with the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC West. That final score is so lopsided it makes it easy to forget that the many of the players who were on the field for the Seahawks for much of the game were expected to spend most of the season on the bench. Quarterback Drew Lock needed a little time to get loose when he was forced into action against the New England Patriots in Week 1, but has played some of the best football of his career since halftime of the opener. Third year offensive lineman Christian Haynes, a third round pick out of UConn in 2024, started for the first time in his career while rotating with 2026 Day 3 selection Beau Stephens, who made his regular season NFL debut against Arizona. Running back Emmanuel Wilson, whose 92 yards on the ground were the second best of his career, carried 21 times during the game, compared to 13 attempts for the first round pick of the Seahawks in the draft in April, Jadarian Price. Add in significant snaps for Brady Russell, Nick Kallerup and Eric Saubert, and it’s easy to see why other teams have been quick to improve their roster by claiming former Seahawks off the waiver wire. (Author’s Note: There is perhaps no better example of this than the Raiders, a team which won all of three games during the entire 2025 season, starting 2-0 after claiming Bryce Cabeldue off the waiver wire ahead of Week 1.) On the defensive side of the ball, practice squad elevatee Rodney Thomas led the group in snaps played, staying on the field for all 50 snaps the defense logged. Nick Emmanwori had a very light workload in his first action of the season, as there was no need to risk rushing things against Jacoby Brissett and the rest of the Cardinals offense. When the Seahawks special teams took to the field, just as it has been in years past, it was Brady Russell leading the way with 22 snaps. Right behind Russell were Tyrice Knight, Chazz Surratt, Patrick O’Connell and George Holani, with 17 snaps each. As for players who only saw the field on special teams and did not play a single snap on offense or defense, former Los Angeles Chargers cornerback Avery Smith led the team with 14 special teams snaps as he continues to learn the system and scheme after arriving in a trade on the day of roster cuts. And with the ghosts of Glendale in the rear view mirror, it’s a trip east to the DMV in Week 3 to take on Dan Quinn and the Washington Commanders.

title: Seahawks Droppings: New starting quarterback, same results for streaking Seahawks
summary: It doesn’t matter who’s playing for the Seattle Seahawks right now…they’re on a freakin’ roll! Drew Lock stepped right in for Sam Darnold and led the Seahawks to a 31-7 drubbing of the Arizona Cardinals in the desert. This win pushed Seattle’s winning streak to a franchise record 12 games in a row, and was […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Drew Lock #2 of the Seattle Seahawks warms up during the second quarter of the game against the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images It doesn’t matter who’s playing for the Seattle Seahawks right now…they’re on a freakin’ roll! Drew Lock stepped right in for Sam Darnold and led the Seahawks to a 31-7 drubbing of the Arizona Cardinals in the desert . This win pushed Seattle’s winning streak to a franchise record 12 games in a row, and was also the 10th consecutive victory over the Cardinals. The Seahawks are on an absolute heater right now. Seattle got off to a hot start on the first drive with an 82-yard TD pass from Lock to Jaxon Smith-Njigba. From then on until halftime, it was a bit of a struggle with some drops, fumbles, and a failed 4th down play. Heading into halftime, the score was 7-7 with the Cardinals hanging around and feeling good. Then, the Seahawks threw the Cardinals out the front door like Uncle Will from Fresh Prince of Bel Air . Seattle rallied off 24 straight points including a soul crushing drive that took up most of the fourth quarter. They kept ramming it down Arizona’s throat, and finished it off with a 1-yard AJ Barner “Barn Yard” TD. It was Seattle imposing their will and it was glorious! What a statement. Seahawks Droppings Drew Lock played a fantastic game, throwing for 3 TDs and taking care of the ball . His completion percentage would’ve been even better if not for some uncharacteristic drops by JSN and Rashid Shaheed. Lock was poised, escaped pressure, and whistled some truly beautiful throws in there. Sam Darnold will still be the QB when he’s healthy, but the Seahawks have to feel pretty good about their QB situation. Brian Fleury showed that he runs a QB-friendly system. Remember when Mac Jones looked great playing in the place of an injured Brock Purdy for the San Francisco 49ers? Same system. Fleury called plenty of run plays to soften the Cardinals defense before hitting them with the pass. Then, he used the run game to deliver the knockout blow. Just a beautiful execution of the game plan. JSN is inevitable . No matter how many people you put on him or how you try to stop him, it seems impossible right now. 9 catches on 11 targets for 155 yards and 3 TDs. Within those catches were some vital third down conversions. JSN can literally do everything at the wide receiver position, a total luxury for Seattle. Let’s give it up one time for the RBs! Price’s fumble notwithstanding, the RB room showed out. Emmanuel Wilson led way with 92 yards while Price chipped in 52 of his own. The rookie injured his chest, so hopefully that won’t hold him out. Wilson, taking the lion’s share of the carries after Price went out, looked quick, decisive, and powerful. He always fell forward and rarely was tackled by the first defender. When Charbonnet comes back, the Seahawks might now have a three-headed monster in the backfield. Seattle’s defense absolutely suffocated Arizona’s offense after allowing a TD on 4th down to Trey McBride . They shut down the run, only allowing 70 rushing yards, which was padded by a garbage time explosive run on the last drive. Jacoby Brissett didn’t do much better throwing the ball, managing 81 yards passing with an interception. In the postgame presser, Leonard Williams (who had a fantastic sack by the way), mentioned how they want to play defense like a boa constrictor. Mission accomplished today. I feel like I need to mention Julian Love once again . That was one of the best INTs I’ve ever seen, getting his hands underneath the ball and keeping it off the turf while sliding towards the boundary. Love has always been a good player, but I feel like he’s entering the blue-chip territory. It was good to see both Tory Horton and Nick Emmanwori get some snaps . They’ll be worked in even more in the coming weeks and will both provide explosive potential on each sides of the ball. The Seahawks made a statement with this victory. No matter what the starting lineup looks like, when they play like Seahawks, they’re going to be tough to beat. Relentlessly physical and opportunistic in all three phases, this 31-7 beatdown is an example of the tidal wave that Seattle can bring on their opponents. What a beautiful representation of the game of football!

title: 49ers’ upcoming stretch will test Trent Williams’ exciting Brock Purdy claim
summary: Even though his latest superb showing came against significantly inferior opposition in the form of the Miami Dolphins, the excitement around what 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put together through the opening two weeks of the season is understandable. Purdy was near-perfect in the 49ers’ 35-13 rout of the rebuilding Dolphins, rewriting several pages of […]
full_text: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) scores a touchdown against the Miami Dolphins in the second quarter during an NFL game at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara on Sunday, Sept. 20, 2026. (Photo by Santiago Mejia/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images) Even though his latest superb showing came against significantly inferior opposition in the form of the Miami Dolphins, the excitement around what 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has put together through the opening two weeks of the season is understandable. Purdy was near-perfect in the 49ers’ 35-13 rout of the rebuilding Dolphins, rewriting several pages of the record books in going 20 of 22 for 287 yards and two touchdowns. Purdy also led the 49ers in rushing with 30 yards and a rushing score. Those numbers saw Purdy become the first player in NFL history to complete at least 90 percent of his passes, throw for at least 285 yards and two touchdowns and rush for a score in the same game. With a completion percentage of 90.9, Purdy now owns the top two single-game completion percentage marks in 49er franchise history. He completed 95.2% of his passes against the Arizona Cardinals in a 35-16 win in October, 2023. In addition, he joined Derek Carr as only the second player to have multiple games with a completion rate of 90%-or-higher and at least 250 passing yards. His passer rating of 149.1 gave Purdy an eighth career game with a rating of 140-or-higher and a 13th game with a rating of at least 130-or higher, both NFL records for a player in the first five seasons of his career. Unsurprisingly, the praise for Purdy after the game from his teammates was effusive, though it was the comments of Trent Williams that were the most eye-catching. Asked what impressed him most about Purdy’s showing, the left tackle said: “It’s hard for me to tell because I just see the ball coming over my head, but it was extremely accurate. He looked like he was just at practice out there, wheeling and dealing. Like I said, we’re starting to witness Brock’s prime and I think it’s going to be a sight to behold. To me, I’ve always loved Brock, but I think he’s starting to get his respect now. He doesn’t even relish in it. It’s all about next week, going 1-0, and that’s why he’s a great leader.” Williams’ remarks about Purdy hitting his prime suggest even more impressive games are to come from the 49ers’ signal-caller, but those exciting claims will be severely tested over the coming weeks. An exacting three-game stretch San Francisco’s schedule over the next three games is very tough, with the 49ers hosting the Cardinals and the Denver Broncos before making the trip up to the Pacific Northwest for a matchup with the Seattle Seahawks. While the visit of the Cardinals is not a fixture to inspire much fear, a divisional game against an opponent that has played the 49ers tough in recent years is not be taken lightly, though it is the meetings with the Broncos and Seahawks that will provide the sternest early examinations of Purdy’s progress this year. Facing a Denver defense that led the NFL in sacks (68) last season promises to be an extremely difficult challenge for Purdy, as does a reunion with a Seattle unit that overwhelmed the 49ers in Week 18 and in the divisonal round last season. And the severity of the test he will face is potentially exacerbated by the 49ers’ injury issues at wide receiver, where Demarcus Robinson is the latest player to head to be sidelined, having suffered a high-ankle sprain . Robinson joining De’Zhaun Stribling and Chirstian Kirk on among the injured players at receiver is a huge hit to the 49ers’ depth at wideout and, while San Francisco still has high end weapons in the likes of Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans and George Kittle, a paucity of supplementary options makes Purdy’s job in overcoming two vaunted defenses that much harder. The 49ers’ 2025 season ended in ugly fashion with Purdy out of answers against the Seahawks as injuries left San Francisco with a skill-position cast ill-equipped to keep their playoff game competitive. The Niners still have enough weapons to trouble both Denver and Seattle but, with injuries impacting the depth, this upcoming slate and Purdy’s ability to find solutions amid the offense’s injury woes will provide an indicator as to the prescience of Williams’ comments about his quarterback.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: 49ers News: We’re on to Arizona
summary: The NFL is such a brutal war of attrition. The New York Giants almost gave us a solid but they couldn’t really ever get going once their quarterback went down with a knee injury, early in the first quarter. The Giants and the Arizona Cardinals seem to be in this same class of team, where […]
full_text: The NFL is such a brutal war of attrition. The New York Giants almost gave us a solid but they couldn’t really ever get going once their quarterback went down with a knee injury, early in the first quarter. The Giants and the Arizona Cardinals seem to be in this same class of team, where they should never ever beat you if you treat them like a good team. But if you treat them like the bad teams that they actually are, you might get in trouble. Jeremiyah Love and Trey McBride can still win enough match-ups on offense to cause issues. I’m not worried about the Cardinals but I also hope the 49ers keep up this incredible focus and determination. It’ll serve them well against the big match-ups the following two weeks. Kyle Shanahan shares 49ers updates one day after Week 2 win vs. Dolphins “Yeah, that’s actually why I made that slip-up there, what’s on my mind right now. As soon as I’m done with you guys, I get to move on to Arizona. So, it’s lunch here and then we’ll start.” 8 winners that helped the 49ers beat up on the Dolphins: There are no losers when you win by 22 “Stout was a bit confused about the touchdown he gave up, but less than three minutes remained in a 35-6 game at that point. I’m going to forgive the second-year pro for not being focused at that point in the game. Stout topped 20 miles per hour on the GPS, which was the second-fastest time on the team this week. That speed, paired with his intuition, is how you end up with a tackle for loss and a pass breakup in the same game. Aside from the touchdown, Stout allowed 39 yards in coverage on six targets. He has a lot on his plate, and it’s not slowing Stout down, literally or figuratively. He’s a keeper who hasn’t come close to reaching his ceiling….You don’t want to make any grand proclamations after eight quarters of the season. But Mykel’s return should shore up some of the run-defense issues. The offense’s exceptional production feels like an outlier, but it’s really not. They’re loaded with great players at every position. This is a team that is supposed to play like they’re destined for the NFC Championship. That’s what it looks like after two weeks.” 49ers vs. Dolphins PFF grades: Best and worst from the game, plus snap counts “Cornerback Renardo Green earned a 75.1 coverage grade, the best of the game, despite not being targeted. The next-highest coverage grades belonged to San Francisco’s linebacker duo of Dre Greenlaw at 73.4 and Fred Warner at 72.8. Cornerback Upton Stout earned the 49ers’ lowest coverage grade at 31.6. He was targeted seven times, allowing five catches for 116 yards and a passer rating of 153.3.” Exactly 1 takeaway from 49ers-Dolphins (paywall) “Brock Purdy is playing at an elite level. Nick Bosa is consistently creating pressure, even if he’s not finishing it. Fred Warner’s still the best linebacker in football and Dre Greenlaw, if nothing else, fills a gap and hits extremely hard (so does Marques Sigle, with increasingly regularity). There are potential issues defensively, as there always are. The run game was a concern, even with five-man fronts (which makes sense in some ways as there’s actually one less person at the second level). Left guard is still not fully “solved,” and Connor Colby’s weaknesses could be exposed against a team like Seattle (I’ll keep saying it even if no one else will). But San Francisco is a well-oiled machine. This was an exercise in the institution of Kyle Shanahan. It was experience and talent plus scheme against an opposition that is still trying to figure out what it wants to be other than an MLM operation with De’Von Achane at the top.” How Brock Purdy throttled the Dolphins — and jet lag — for a near-perfect game (paywall) “Teammates said Purdy, who’s never lacked confidence, seems to have reached a new level of poise this season and that the third-quarter throw to Evans was a prime example. “He rolls out, pump-fakes a guy and keeps his eyes downfield,” Kittle said. “Quarterbacks who don’t have confidence don’t make that pass. He says, ‘Oh, Mike Evans is down there. He has a step on the guy. I can make that throw.’ And he was doing that all day.” Even Purdy’s seemingly bad passes turned out to be good ones. Juszczyk thought that might have been the case when Purdy threw in his direction in the middle of the third quarter. What the fullback forgot, however, is that when Evans is pressed at the line of scrimmage, Juszczyk is supposed to alter his route so that he and Evans don’t end up in the same area. He didn’t, and he thought for a moment the ball heading his way had been misfired and was too high. Then he saw Evans snatch it for a 17-yard gain. “I thought Brock just overthrew me,” Juszczyk said. “So the wave of emotions — I see the ball going past, of being upset that I missed my opportunity and then seeing it land in Mike’s hands and being so excited we got a big play.” 49ers minutia minute: Romello Height improved in Week 2 but needs surgery on broken hand (paywall) “The 49ers allowed no sacks for the second consecutive week. Per the Elias Sports Bureau, it’s the first time San Francisco has surrendered no sacks in its first two games since sacks became an official stat in 1982. Williams and Brendel, the oldest members of the offensive line, essentially played two-thirds of a normal outing. Lowe took over for Williams at left tackle in the fourth quarter and Patterson filled in for Brendel at center…. …Height played with a broken hand in the second half and will have surgery Tuesday, Shanahan said. Still, the coach said there’s an “outside chance” Height can suit up in Week 3, and he praised the rookie for his performance against the Dolphins….. The 49ers began the game with a five-man defensive line — Height, Halton, West, Odighizuwa and Bosa — and used it through the first quarter. It wasn’t very effective, with the Dolphins successfully attacking it with quick throws and dump-offs, like on an 18-yard catch-and-run by fullback DJ Herman on the second snap of the game. The 49ers largely went back to a more traditional four-lineman, three-linebacker look in the second quarter and onward. Though Bosa is looking for his first sack of the season, he was the catalyst on two of the team’s four sacks. He flushed Malik Willis out of the pocket deep in the red zone in the second quarter, allowing Height to escort the quarterback out of bounds for the third-round rookie’s first NFL sack. Bosa later steered Willis toward safety Marques Sigle for a sack, also the first of Sigle’s career, in the third quarter. Though Mykel Williams is eligible to begin practicing this week, Shanahan said the plan is for that to happen next week. Williams can come off of the physically unable to perform list as early as the Week 5 game in Seattle.” Why Brock Purdy has his 49ers teammates in awe: ‘We’re starting to witness Brock’s prime’ (paywall) “Afterwards, Purdy explained how he has improved. He said he and quarterbacks coach Mick Lombardi pored over film in the offseason and identified ways in which Purdy could be more surgical. Efficient. Purdy said he too often hung too long in the pocket, hunting for a big play. “It’s like, if I’m hanging on a guy in a progression — how can I find an outlet (pass) or check down and stay ahead of the chains?” Purdy said. “It’s OK to be in 3rd-and-medium rather than forcing a ball and being in 3rd-and-long.” It sounds a bit boring when spoken from a podium. But it was anything but on the field Sunday. In the first quarter, on 3rd-and-5 from the Dolphins’ 32-yard line, Purdy looked dead shortly after the snap: Unblocked defensive end Zeek Biggers was bearing down on his blindside. But Purdy lost Biggers with a pirouette to the sideline, did a rope-a-dope to elude linebacker Jordyn Brooks and planted his feet to fire a 10-yard strike to Evans to extend the first of five straight game-opening touchdown drives.”
author: Yinon Raviv

For the second week in a row, the 49ers are home favorites by more than a touchdown. This time, it’s against a division opponent. At FanDuel Sportsbook, the Niners are 8.5-point favorites, […]

If we’ve learned anything about San Francisco through two weeks, it’s that the offense has one of the highest floors in the NFL. Kyle Shanahan called Brock Purdy’s Week 2 performance close to “flawless.” The Cardinals allowed the Seahawks to rush for 123 yards after contact. So, we may not need to see an encore performance from Purdy. Drew Lock still finished fourth in total EPA among all quarterbacks in Week 2. He had a 51.9% passing success rate and completed 73.1% of his passes with three touchdowns. Seattle let the Cardinals tie the game at seven, then went on to score 24 straight points. The final score didn’t reflect the product on the field. The stats were actually worse. The Seahawks outgained the Cardinals by +2.5 yards per play. They ran 20 more plays and held the ball for 13 minutes longer than the home team. It helps to have Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who had 155 receiving yards on 11 targets. JSN finished with three touchdowns. Arizona should be able to put more points up against the Niners, but I’m not sure they have the defense to keep Purdy and company in check. This has the makings of an over game, with the home team once again winning by double digits. Even in a different environment with an upgrade at quarterback, it’ll be interesting to look back on the common opponent between the 49ers and Seahawks a couple of weeks from now.
