title: Rams' jab at Jameis Winston, Giants leads NFL Week 2 trolls
summary: Teams across the NFL came with petty postgame energy after wins in Week 2, led by the Los Angeles Rams.
full_text:
With half of the league's teams looking for their first wins of the season heading into Week 2, a victory could lead to an even sweeter troll. Case in point? The Los Angeles Rams .

 

 The Rams dominated the New York Giants on "Monday Night Football," winning 28-6 at home. Coming off a loss, Los Angeles put up 481 yards of offense with wide receiver Davante Adams outgaining New York's offense by himself -- he had 195 receiving yards, and the Giants had 182 as a team. Adams also added two touchdown receptions. Quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns.

 A major reason for New York's struggles on offense were the result of quarterback Jaxson Dart suffering a knee injury on the team's first drive. Dart exited and never returned , forcing backup Jameis Winston  under center the rest of the way. Winston struggled, throwing for 111 yards on 11-of-27 passing with one interception.

 The 12-year NFL veteran became the theme of the Rams' postgame jab. Los Angeles shared an image of a bitten apple with the Giants' "NY" logo on it, a nod to New York being known as the Big Apple. However, in its caption, the team wrote: "Ate the W," a reference to the  "Eat a W" speech  Winston delivered while starting for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2017. 

 

 Here are more of the top trolls from NFL Week 2.

 

 Philadelphia Eagles 24, Tennessee Titans 20 
 The Philadelphia Eagles used a late two-minute drive to steal a win against the Tennessee Titans in Nashville.

 Tennessee took a 20-17 lead with 1:56 left and needed one stop for its first win of the season. But Philadelphia quarterback Jalen Hurts led his team down the field with a nine-play, 65-yard drive that ended with a 3-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Darius Cooper with nine seconds left. It marked the Eagles' latest winning passing touchdown since 2012, according to ESPN Research.

 Nashville is home to the famous Broadway Street, but Philadelphia has its own notable street too: "Broad Street." Therefore, the Eagles posted a graphic of an Eagle on a "Broadway" street sign but covered "way" with a sticky note that read: "Street," putting a spin on Nashville's area.

 

 

 Carolina Panthers 34, Atlanta Falcons 3 
 Carolina defeated its NFC South foe on the road Sunday in convincing fashion.

 Panthers quarterback Bryce Young passed for 287 yards and three touchdowns, two of which went to tight end Darren Waller . Carolina forced five turnovers -- three interceptions and two fumbles -- as Atlanta had only 286 total yards of offense.

 Carolina's blowout win came with an equally dominant social media performance. It first shared a victory post with the score and caption: "Feelin' Peachy," a reference to Georgia being known as the Peach State. The Panthers then posted a graphic of a Panther eating a bird's egg with the caption: "We cooked."

 

 
 New Orleans Saints 24, Baltimore Ravens 17 
 The Saints faced a 17-9 deficit heading into the fourth quarter but responded with consecutive touchdowns -- the final one coming with 1:28 left. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson threw an interception on the ensuing drive, and New Orleans secured the victory.

 The NFC South team directed its troll toward an unlikely source: a Baltimore fan who had choice words for Saints fans on X. They wrote that Saints fans were "talking crazier than Colts  fans," the Ravens' Week 1 opponent, and they'd similarly learn the "hard way" like Indianapolis' followers. Baltimore defeated Indianapolis last Sunday.

 New Orleans remembered the slight, quoting the post with a video of wide receiver Chris Olave celebrating his fourth-quarter touchdown with the caption: "Love those crazy Saints fans."

 

 
 Minnesota Vikings 9, Chicago Bears 3 
 Another divisional game brought another troll, this time from the Minnesota Vikings .

 Minnesota kept Chicago in check after the Bears put up 59 points in a Week 1 victory. The Vikings forced two turnovers, including one as Chicago running back D'Andre Swift  fumbled while diving for a touchdown. The Bears reached the red zone again but had a field goal attempt blocked with 6:23 left. Minnesota got one more stop to claim the win.

 The Vikings kept it simple after the victory. They shared a "W" graphic with the caption: "WINdy City DUB," emphasizing the "win."

 

 

 San Francisco 49ers 35, Miami Dolphins 13 

 San Francisco is off to a dominant start to the season with consecutive double-digit wins -- this time against Miami.

 The 49ers erupted in the third quarter with three touchdowns, two of which were delivered by quarterback Brock Purdy . Running back Christian McCaffrey added the final one after he had a score in the first quarter. Purdy threw for 287 yards and and completed 91% of his pass attempts with 30 rushing yards and a score. He's the first player with 250 passing yards on 90% completion and 30 rushing yards in a game in NFL history.  

 Consistently petty, San Francisco had trolls lined up postgame for Miami. The 49ers referenced the Dolphins' namesake, referred to making "a splash" and posted an image of a dolphin pool float.

 

 

 Las Vegas Raiders 26, Los Angeles Chargers 14 

 The Raiders are 2-0 for the first time since 2021 after a big win against the Chargers.

 Las Vegas pulled ahead in the fourth quarter behind consecutive turnovers by Los Angeles -- a fumble by running back Omarion Hampton then an interception thrown by Justin Herbert . Hampton's fumble resulted in a Raiders touchdown to put them up 10 with 2:59 remaining. Las Vegas quarterback Kirk Cousins had 259 yards passing and three touchdowns, and wide receiver Tre Tucker led the team with five receptions for 119 yards and a score.

 A massive victory came with a straight forward troll as -- not far from Hollywood -- the Raiders captioned their win post: "Roll credits." As Cousins walked off the field, he took a video thanking the fans who showed up at Sofi Stadium and said it "felt like a home game," which Las Vegas wrote in its caption. 

 

 

 Seattle Seahawks 31, Arizona Cardinals 7 

 It has been almost 10 months since Seattle lost a regular-season or postseason game, and Arizona is the latest to be on the other end of a victory.

 The Seahawks outscored the Cardinals 24-0 in the second half behind a stellar performance from Jaxon Smith-Njigba . The wide receiver had nine catches for 155 yards and three touchdowns. He has scored Seattle's first four touchdowns of the season, becoming only the second player in NFL history to record each of his team's first four-plus touchdowns of the season, according to Elias Sports Bureau.

 And like the Seahawks have done during their win streak dating to last season, they made sure to troll their opponent. They first shared a comic of their mascot posing in front of a buried Big Red, the Cardinals' mascot. Seattle then posted an image of a burnt tortilla with a "W" grilled on it and the caption: "That's a wrap."

 

 

 Cleveland Browns 23, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 19 

 The Browns are in the win column following a late defensive stand against the Buccaneers.

 Lightning delayed the game by 2 hours, 12 minutes, resuming while Tampa Bay held possession at the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter. The Buccaneers had a chance to take the lead on fourth-and-11 with 22 seconds left. But quarterback Baker Mayfield threw an interception and Cleveland came up with a clutch victory.

 The Browns poked fun at the Buccaneers' classic "Bucco Bruce" logo postgame, sharing a meme that pointed at Bruce and asked: "What does he even do?"

title: NFL Week 2's best arrivals, led by Aaron Donald and Jaxson Dart
summary: Rounding up the top pregame and tunnel arrivals from around the league.
full_text:
There are no rules for the best NFL gameday arrival fits, but there is certainly an unspoken competition, and the judges are often a player's football peers.

 An animated discussion among Cincinnati Bengals  defenders in the locker room after a win illustrated this.

 The source was cornerback DJ Turner II 's custom bold double-breasted suit by fashion designer Pharoah Kirk -- the unofficial fit of the day. Respect was given to Turner's fit, with one player promising to top his arrival the following week.

 "I'm always about that action," Turner said. I gotta put it on."

 Week 1 started with a bang, as many players put on their Sunday best to open the season, but just like on the field, consistency is king. This Sunday could provide much stiffer competition.

 Here are some of the most interesting NFL arrivals from Week 2.

 

 Monday night fits 
 Playing in his first game in over 900 days, Los Angeles Rams star Aaron Donald wore a simple black jacket and shorts with black-rimmed glasses. The player he'll be looking to bring down, New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart , rocked a bomber jacket from the brand Nahmias and camouflage pants.

 The Giants made the most of the "Monday Night Football" stage.

 Backup quarterback Jameis Winston angora sleeveless shirt was the highlight of this all-cream fit. Linebacker Brian Burns ' Loewe's blue pinstripe jacket was strong -- a sophisticated energy from one of NFL's best pass rushers. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor 's lime green splatter jacket with beige pants from Gentleman's Playbook was unique and bold. A big man going shirtless under a jacket is a different level of confidence.

 Here are the tops looks from "Monday Night Football."

 

 

 Sunday night drip 
 Indianapolis Colts defensive lineman DeForest Buckner might have had the best outfit ahead of Sunday's matchup against the  Kansas City Chiefs . Buckner wore a navy and black silk suit made by Gentleman's Playbook . It was a bold and unique choice.

 

 Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce  also showed up in style with a Louis Vuitton collarless jacket and matching belt. His teammate, Patrick Mahomes , rocked Adidas from head to toe with Oakley sunglasses.

 Here are the top fits ahead of "Sunday Night Football."

 

 

 Sunday afternoon arrivals 

 Dallas Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens kept it simple up top, with a pop of color below for his arrival ahead of a divisional game against the Washington Commanders on Sunday. Pickens wore a solid black T-shirt, multicolored striped shorts, and purple-and-black Nike Dunks on the feet.

 

 Commanders' rookie linebacker Sonny Styles was among the best dressed players during the arrivals for the Sunday afternoon games. Styles arrived in a grey suit, with his initials embroidered on the collar in gold.

 Here are more notable arrivals from the 4 p.m. slate:

 

 

 Best of 1 p.m. arrivals 
 Cincinnati Bengals defensive lineman Myles Murphy was the best dressed during Sunday's early slate. Murphy arrived wearing a Gallery Department Logan canvas trucker vest with black cargo pants. His Bottega Veneta woven duffle bag was a strong complementary piece.

 

 Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield was dressed to impress, arriving for a home game against his former team, the Cleveland Browns . Mayfield wore a cream polo with khaki and green striped and white shoes.

 Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson wore a red letterman jacket and loose-fit khaki pants ahead of a road matchup against the Chicago Bears .

 

 Here are some of the other memorable fits from Sunday's 1 p.m. slate:

 

 

 Thursday night's best fit 

 To kick off Week 2, Buffalo Bills edge rusher Bradley Chubb arrived in a plaid Archival button-down shirt paired with dark denim jeans.

title: How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list
summary: Myles Garrett's torrid pace up the all-time sack list paces seven active players making their moves among the greats.
full_text:
Last season, defensive end Myles Garrett won his second Defensive Player of the Year award after setting the NFL's single-season record with 23 sacks with the Cleveland Browns . 
 
 This season, he'll continue his climb up the NFL's all-time sack list as a member of the Los Angeles Rams  after a blockbuster trade  in June -- making the Rams favorites to win the Super Bowl, according to DraftKings Sportsbook, heading into the season. 
 
 Garrett entered the season with 125.5 career sacks, which was tied for 20th in NFL history and third among the other six active players --  Von Miller  (No. 9), Cameron Jordan  (No. 17), Calais Campbell  (No. 25), T.J. Watt  (No. 26), Danielle Hunter  (tied for No. 27) and Khalil Mack  (T-29th) -- in the top 30.  
 
 Joining the top 30 soon could be  Aaron Donald , who un-retired  to join Garrett on the Rams' defensive line. Donald's 111 sacks currently sits two behind 30th.  
 
 As for Garrett, he entered his 10th season in the NFL averaging approximately 14 sacks per season. If he were to replicate that production, he would tie Pro Football Hall of Famer Jason Taylor, who currently sits at No. 7 all-time. If Garrett were to have another historic season, he would surpass Michael Strahan (No. 6) and approach top-five all-time territory. 
 
 
 
 Miller, who signed with the  Dallas Cowboys  in August, can also pass Strahan in his 15th season -- as he sits only three sacks behind him.   
 
 But Garrett's 125.5 career sacks were 10.5 more than any other player since his rookie season in 2017, according to ESPN Research, heading into the seaosn. The pass rusher recorded at least 14 sacks in each of the past five seasons, the longest such streak by any player since 1982. 
 
 If Garrett has 18.5 or more sacks this season, he will hold the record for the most over a two-season span since 1982, according to ESPN Research, and his current ascension up the all-time list ranks as the second-fastest pace among the top five all time behind only Reggie White.  
 
As we look at how the sack list is redefined this season, we'll highlight milestones across the NFL landscape 
 We will update this file as the active players move up, and we'll add nuggets and milestones throughout the season. 
 

 

 Week 2 update 

 The second week of the season saw little movement near the top of the all-time list, but Watt's hot start continues, with the defensive end recording 1.5 sacks to now put him at 3.5 through two weeks (No. 2 in the NFL this season) and break a tie with Campbell to move to 25th. 

 Hunter (27th) and Mack (29th) also recorded 1 sack over the weekend to break ties and move up one spot on the list. 

 Donald (33rd) made his  season debut on "Monday Night Football" against the Giants after taking two years off. He finished with three tackles, one for a loss, but did not record a sack. 

 

 Week 1 update 

 Of all of the active sack leaders, Watt was the only one to record a sack, finishing the game with two to move to a tie with Campbell for 25th. 

 And while Donald was held out of the Rams' Week 1 game, Garrett will be out for at least the next four after failing to record a tackle in Australia and landing on injured reserve after having to have arthroscopic surgery on his knee.

 After the Rams' opening loss, Garrett said this was " the worst version of myself that I've put out there."

title: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 3
summary: Can Baker Mayfield rebound? Are the Chargers doomed? Is the Eagles' new offense actually encouraging for Jalen Hurts? Get ready for Week 3 with seven takes.
full_text:
Week 2 is in the books! It came with big upsets ( Raiders over Chargers ! Browns over Bucs !) and devastating injuries (such as Commanders QB Jayden Daniels and Giants QB Jaxson Dart ). Week 3 feels like as murky a future week as ever.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 This week, I'm starting with my concern for a big-ticket quarterback contract signed not even a month ago, my concern for one key AFC contender and my lack of concern for two others. Here are seven things I think ahead of Week 3.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Bucs regret the Mayfield deal 
 Chargers to pick top-10 in 2027 
 Patriots offense is fine, everyone 
 Hurts is settling into Eagles' offense 
 Jaguars trenches will be postseason downfall 
 Henry won't solve Ravens' late-game issues 
 Donald's workout regimen paid off 
 Five extra inklings 

 

 
 

 I think ... the Buccaneers are already regretting that Baker Mayfield deal 
 Mayfield has not played well through the first two games of the season.

 This does not mean he is a bad quarterback who is undeserving of a nice contract. Two game samples are, in a vacuum, barely above meaningless. (They're just meaningful enough that you should keep reading this column.) But it would have been nice to see how this season played out, to see if this two-game trend continued, before signing an extension.

 Mayfield and the Buccaneers looked destined for a prove-it season before the Buccaneers "surprised" Mayfield with an eleventh-hour offer that clearly met his expectations. It is a three-year deal , as Mayfield wanted, though it's really a two-year deal with a $55 million team option in 2029. Still, at $55 million per year, Mayfield is making Matthew Stafford and Trevor Lawrence sort of money ... Joe Burrow and Josh Allen sort of money.

 Mayfield's play has been decidedly below that level to start the season. Through two weeks, Mayfield is 29th among 32 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback and 27th in success rate. Of course, two-game samples are useless, so let's add last season. Since the start of 2025, Mayfield is 24th among 32 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback and 25th in success rate.

 

 But last season was a down year. Mayfield played through a strained knee that he suffered in Week 2 and endured shoulder pain (non-throwing side) after a big hit in Week 12. His 2025 offensive coordinator, Josh Grizzard, was fired at the end of the season. So, let's throw in 2024 as well. Since the start of that season, Mayfield's career year with offensive coordinator Liam Coen, Mayfield is 13th in EPA per dropback and 13th in success rate. There he is,  the guy the Bucs paid. We just had to go back a couple of seasons to find him.

 But even including the 2024 season, we find some problems. A big part of Mayfield's success in that season, and in the seasons to follow, is how well he played when pressured. His dropback success rate (34.9%) is eighth; his first-down/touchdown rate (29.7%) is third behind Burrow and Brock Purdy .

 But play under pressure tends not to be sticky. Pressured plays are either big wins (the passer beats the blitz with a deep throw) or disasters (the passer gets sacked), and that creates large swings in the outcome. Good play against pressure also relies heavily on athleticism. Mayfield has scrambled on 17.9% of his pressured dropbacks since the start of the 2024 season, second to Jayden Daniels . Mayfield's numerous 2025 injuries reflect his toughness, but they also reflect his playstyle. He gets sacked a lot (22.8% pressure to sack ratio, eighth highest) and takes more hits on scrambles down the field. It is reasonable to expect Mayfield's effectiveness against pressure to decline with age and accumulated hits; he's 31 years old! I'd argue it already has.

 This season, Mayfield's scramble rate has almost halved (9.2%) as the Buccaneers have prioritized throws behind the line of scrimmage, but his ability to escape is also underwhelming, leading to a 9.2% sack rate.

 Here's one of three sacks he took against the Browns. Cool concept here on third-and-7 from new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson, who motions receiver Emeka Egbuka into the bunch to create a natural pick for Chris Godwin Jr . to get into the slant. The Buccaneers get the hoped-for man coverage. This ball should be out to Godwin immediately.

 

 Mayfield is aggressively climbing the pocket despite the fact that there's plenty of room to stand and throw, and accordingly, he's too late to get the ball to Godwin by the time he reaches a throwing platform. Watch safety Ronnie Hickman , meant to rob the middle of the field, burn right by Godwin and give Mayfield hot pursuit; Hickman knows the scouting report on the quarterback. As Mayfield tries to escape, Hickman hawks him down.

 Here's another simple one from Week 1 against the Bengals. Rookie wideout  Ted Hurst III has a vertical route to the bottom of the screen, and the single-high safety is on the opposite hash when Mayfield drops back. A veteran quarterback needs to land on his back foot and send this throw, beating the deep safety to the spot by pulling that vertical route outside the numbers. Not an easy throw, but one a $55 million quarterback should be expected to attempt. Instead, he hitches, double-clutches and gets sacked

 

 Mayfield's attempts breakdown has become worryingly polarized through two games of the Robinson offense. A harrowing 37.1% of Mayfield's pass attempts are behind the line of scrimmage, more than all quarterbacks save for Aaron Rodgers and Patrick Mahomes . But 16.1% of his throws go more than 20 yards downfield, as well; that's fifth-highest in the league. Such a spray chart is unhealthy. It indicates a quarterback is uncomfortable testing coverage and either checks it down in front of all defenders or sails it deep beyond all defenders.

 Again, this is a small sample. Seven of these eight deep throws came in Week 2 against the Browns, and the lack of success had more to do with miscommunications than anything else. If you're looking for a sunny side in the Buccaneers' offense through two games it's that clearing up those little mistakes should lead to big downfield connections.

 This is why the Buccaneers might regret that Mayfield deal. Not because his bad play through two games is written in stone, but because they could have collected a season's worth of additional data to inform their contract decision, and at little cost. What was Mayfield going to demand if he had a good year? Maybe $60 million instead of $55 million? Actual guarantees in 2029?

 

 These are peanut problems compared with the larger issue: Mayfield is a late-career breakout who relies heavily on his athleticism and accordingly is on a shorter time horizon than most quarterbacks over 30. He also plays an inherently erratic style, and Robinson has had little success tamping that down through two weeks. I enjoy when Mayfield is at his best and look forward to seeing it again, but paying for peaks makes the valleys difficult to endure. The Buccaneers likely never had a better alternative than paying Mayfield a sizable veteran contract, but I sure would have liked to turn every stone before I consigned myself to that path.

 

 

 I think ... the Chargers will pick in the top 10 of next year's draft 
 I can't name 10 teams worse than the Chargers (0-2) through two weeks. I'm not even sure if I can name five.

title: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
summary: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
full_text:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

 Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window (44 points) came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly's  Darius Cooper .

 The scoring picked up in the late window Sunday, as the Cowboys and Commanders combined for 57 points. However, Washington lost QB Jayden Daniels to an elbow injury in the second quarter -- hours after Chicago lost QB Caleb Williams to a right hamstring injury. Meanwhile, the 49ers dominated the Dolphins in their first game back from Melbourne, Australia. And the Seahawks won their second straight game with backup quarterback Drew Lock . And the night game featured a wild ending, but ultimately the Chiefs improved to 2-0 with an overtime thriller over the Colts.

 Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

 
 Jump to: 
 KC-IND |  WSH-DAL | LV-LAC 
 SEA-ARI |  MIA-SF 
 JAX-DEN  |  CLE-TB  |  PHI-TEN

 Kansas City 33, Indianapolis 30 (OT) 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Chiefs 
 Did Patrick Mahomes' performance demonstrate the Chiefs are back as contenders? That appears to be the case after two weeks. In overtime, Mahomes orchestrated the 25th winning drive of his 10-year career, which is tied with Kirk Cousins for second most in that span. Last season, the Chiefs were bad in one-score games, finishing with a 1-9 record. Mahomes, though, proved he's capable of carrying the Chiefs yet again to another dramatic win. In just his second game after recovering from the torn ACL and LCL in his left knee, Mahomes finished with 382 passing yards and three touchdowns without committing a turnover.

 Most surprising performance: Of course, Mahomes spent most of Sunday relying on tight end Travis Kelce , who led the Chiefs with 101 receiving yards and a touchdown. Yet receiver Tyquan Thornton was just as impactful for the Chiefs' offense. At pivotal moments, Thornton was impressive in catching all four of his targets for 86 yards, including a 45-yard reception. That highlight was the first time in the game that the Chiefs' offense converted on third down. -- Nate Taylor 

 Next game: at Dolphins (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 
 

 

 Colts 
 Is this defense salvageable? The Colts' defense gave up its most yards in a game in three seasons in a Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens (506 yards). And the prospects for that unit didn't get better Sunday night, when the Colts consistently struggled to get stops against the Chiefs (523 yards). The question now is whether this is the permanent state of this defense, and if so, what does that mean for the 2026 Colts? Indianapolis approached this season knowing it needed a bit more from its defense to take some of the pressure of an offense led by QB Daniel Jones , who is coming off a torn Achilles tendon. But as of now, that plan is not panning out.

 Most surprising performance: The Colts got a valiant effort from backup cornerback Kapena Gushiken , who came off the bench after injuries to starters Charvarius Ward and Sauce Gardner to make two clutch plays. One of them, a pass breakup on a third down late in the fourth quarter, was one of the biggest plays of the game. The stop against Rashee Rice ended the Chiefs' best last chance in regulation. -- Stephen Holder 

 Next game: vs. Texans (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

 

 Fantasy football takeaway: Travis Kelce's 25.1 points were the second most among tight ends through the Sunday night game. Kelce caught nine of a team-high 11 targets, finishing with 101 yards and a touchdown. What stood out here? The play speed. We saw it with Kelce within the route and after the catch. Add that to his elite coverage awareness, too. It was a big night for Kelce, who is firmly in the TE1 ranks for the Week 3 game at Miami. -- Bowen 

 

 

 Dallas 37, Washington 20 
 Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap 

 

 Cowboys 
 Are the Cowboys going to need QB Dak Prescott to outscore teams again this season? It looks that way. Prescott broke the Cowboys' record for touchdown passes in a career with four Sunday, eclipsing Tony Romo. But Prescott needed to be everything for Dallas, completing better than 80% of his passes, throwing the four scores and running for 26 yards. The defense had issues again, losing safety P.J. Locke (foot) and corner Cobie Durant (hamstring) in the first half. The Cowboys continue to struggle on third down, contain a running quarterback and turn pressures into sacks. Washington had three chances for touchdowns wiped out, but Prescott bailed the Cowboys out ... again.

 Trend to watch: The Cowboys want to be a team that relies on the running game to get things going. Through two games, that has not happened. A week after running 18 times for 69 yards against the Giants, the Cowboys followed with 66 yards on 21 carries. No Cowboys running back has a rush of more than 9 yards. The Cowboys miss Pro Bowl left guard Tyler Smith , who will be out for at least the next two games because of thumb surgery, but they shouldn't miss him this much. -- Todd Archer 

 Next game: vs. Ravens (Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, 4:25 p.m. ET)

 

 
 

 Commanders 
 What's next for Washington after QB Jayden Daniels' injury? This game resembled many from last season -- porous defense, an injured quarterback and a double-digit defeat. Daniels' status and length of absence remains uncertain. And he'll have to answer one giant question whenever he returns: Can he stay healthy? He has now exited four of his past five games with an injury. Also, the defense has struggled. In two games, it has forced zero turnovers and hasn't lived up to internal expectations. If the team is not careful, the season could get ugly.

 Trend to watch: The Commanders' pass defense has allowed seven touchdown receptions in the first two games -- including four Sunday. The offseason overhaul on defense was supposed to help the coverage with intense pressure and disguised coverages. However, the pressure has been sporadic and too many targets are left open -- whether from coverage confusion or botched assignments. Cornerback Mike Sainristil has been a frequent target, and he's not the only one breaking down. -- John Keim

He will remain a touchdown-dependent player in this offense, but he is a priority target in scoring position. Ferguson already has three red zone targets over his first two games after seeing 23 last season. -- Bowen

On Sunday, wide receiver Tre Tucker caught five passes for 119 yards and a touchdown. Las Vegas had eight players record a reception, including wide receiver Cody White , who had two touchdown catches. With Bowers expected to return for Week 3, the optimism for…

title: How Cowboys prepared for Brazil trip to face Ravens
summary: Dallas picked up a key win Sunday against the Commanders before the focus quickly turned to Baltimore and Rio de Janeiro.
full_text:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- Normally, Jerry Jones carries the confidence of a man sure of many things, but as the Cowboys' owner and general manager arrived at  AT&T Stadium on Sunday for the home opener against the Washington Commanders , he wasn't.

 As he got out of his SUV, Jones walked over to a group of fans taking a tour of the stadium when he spotted a Commanders supporter.

 "Tell 'em to be sweet to us," Jones laughed.

 About five hours later, with the Cowboys beating Washington 37-20 , Jones was able to smile.

 "I really was worried about what it was going to be like if we did end up 0-2," Jones said. "And I can't say that I was a color of strength in my mentality coming into the game because I've got a lot of respect for the coaching over on the Washington Commander side. But having said all of that, this was a very important win for us, important to these guys who put the work in, the coaching staff for [coach Brian Schottenheimer], and I'm really proud of him."

 A 10-hour flight to Rio de Janeiro on Thursday would have felt even longer had the Cowboys lost to Washington and dropped to 0-2 with two NFC East losses. Quarterback  Dak Prescott knew the importance of the victory as they get ready to play the Baltimore Ravens  on Sunday ( 4:25 p.m. ET, CBS ).

 "We need to get this win. We need to get in the win column. We're back home. We need to win all of our games at home," Prescott said. "And you can't go 0-2 in the conference or the division, so, yeah, this was a must-win."

 

 The preparation for the Cowboys' trip to Brazil started in March when the organization caught wind that it would be selected to play its first international "home" game. Dallas sent a team from the operations department to Brazil to look at the practice facilities and hotels. They sent materials via cargo ship starting in June. Another plane filled with gear will arrive before the team this week.

 After flying through the night Thursday, the Cowboys will have a quick workout on Friday at the training center for Flamengo , one of Brazil's first-division soccer clubs. On Saturday, they will get a brief look at Maracanã Stadium, where Sunday's game will be played, before holding a walk-through in their hotel.

 The players were off Monday and Schottenheimer is following a short-week plan with practices on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday before they board their flight on an American Airlines Boeing 777-300ER. Most of the players will have a first-class-type seat for the journey.

 Schottenheimer has been mindful of how the Cowboys have worked since training camp. The game in Rio will be followed by a Week 4 trip -- albeit a short one -- to the Houston Texans and then a four-day turnaround to play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers  on Oct. 8, a Thursday night.

 

 With the Texas heat, the Cowboys have not had a full practice outdoors. Schottenheimer's sports science team -- which includes the athletic training staff, strength coaches, nutrition staff and analytics department -- has made recommendations the coach has followed.

 "I think the cool thing is the players have really bought in to the recovery aspect of this; massages and we spent a bunch of money on recovery things and new resources with the saunas and stuff in the train room," Schottenheimer said.

 The Cowboys are accustomed to altered schedules with their annual Thanksgiving game and plethora of primetime games, but playing in Rio will be an adjustment. When the Cowboys played the Jacksonville Jaguars in 2014 at Wembley Stadium, the team flew to London for the entire week, practicing at the home of a rugby club.

 "[Routine is] very important because I feel like routine is preparation" receiver  CeeDee Lamb said. "Preparation is everything. Preparation is more confidence for me because once you go out there every day in practice and you're running these routes, from our perspective, you run these routes all week long, you got your trial and errors, you've ran it versus different coverages, so you got a feel for it.

 "I feel like just being prepared in the moment and going out there and letting loose, I feel like that's when the game is the most fun. You're not thinking too much and [you're] playing a child's game."

 How will it be this week?

 "We'll get to that," Lamb said.

 

 Linebacker  Von Miller has played in two international games in his career and admits he might have a different perspective than some.

 "To grow our game, we've got to have international games," Miller said. "So when somebody comes to a football game and is able to witness football for the first time, that's how we grow our game, that's how we get teams overseas, that's how we continue to make and keep our league the best league on earth. So even though I understand it's a challenge for the players, I know it's worth it. I know it's worth it for the future of the game."

 Defensive tackle Kenny Clark and edge rusher Rashan Gary played in São Paulo two years ago with the Green Bay Packers against the Philadelphia Eagles . The field for that game was an issue, and reports came out late last week of complaints about the state of the field at the Maracanã with it being bumpy and uneven.

 "The way we play, it's unbelievable that we're playing on a field like this," Flamengo goalkeeper Agustín Rossi said  in Portuguese. "Both penalty areas are bad as [expletive]. If you look at it, there are bumps everywhere. There's still going to be an NFL game here during the international break. After that game, I hope the field is in better shape."

 Schottenheimer has heard the complaints.

 "I trust that the league's going to make the right decision and they'll get the field up to standard," Schottenheimer said.

 NFL field director Nick Pappas said Monday there are "no concerns right now" about the field conditions.

 Kicker Brandon Aubrey  might be most impacted by the status of the field. The former pro soccer player trained with São Paolo FC when he was with the Dallas Texans soccer club as a youngster. He knows the history of the Brazilian national soccer team, if not their club soccer.

 "I know a lot of people have told me it's a big deal to be there," Aubrey said. "It's a big deal to play soccer in Brazil. Hopefully football means the same. It won't mean the same to them as soccer, but hopefully they come out in the same way and support us. Hopefully we earn some new fans. Excited to play in front of fresh eyes and show them a game that we love here and hopefully they can fall in love with it as well."

title: Newcomers Jaylen Waddle, Jonah Coleman lead Broncos to win
summary: The Broncos mostly stood pat this offseason, keeping most of the 2025 roster together. But it was two newcomers on offense who helped them beat the Jaguars.
full_text:
DENVER -- The Denver Broncos had a couple things atop their to-do list entering this past offseason. They wanted more impact at wide receiver and more production behind running back J.K. Dobbins . And the players they brought into fill both those needs -- veteran wide receiver Jaylen Waddle and rookie running back Jonah Coleman -- were integral in helping the Broncos (1-1) to their first win of the 2026 season.

 "I'm proud of those guys," Broncos All-Pro left tackle Garett Bolles said. "That's why they're here, to do what they do."

 In Denver's 20-13 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday, Waddle finished with eight catches for 138 receiving yards, including a 49-yard catch in the second quarter and a key 29-yard reception on the Broncos' final, seal-the-win possession. And they asked Coleman to carry the running game when it was time to close out the Jaguars (1-1).

 Waddle had the most receiving yards by a Bronco in a single game since Jerry Jeudy had 154 in the 2022 season finale. It was also the most receiving yards by a Broncos player in his home debut since Rick Upchurch had 153 in 1975.

 

 "Significant, right?" Broncos coach Sean Payton said of Waddle's impact, for which the sixth-year receiver earned the game ball. "You can see the explosiveness, run after the catch. Glad he's ours."

 Waddle's explosion came after a quiet Week 1 debut in which he had only one reception for 2 yards in a loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on "Monday Night Football." Sunday was exactly what the Broncos envisioned when they sent three draft picks, including a first-rounder, to the Miami Dolphins this past March to  acquire the 27-year-old .

 Payton said Sunday that Waddle's impact goes beyond stats because his explosiveness forces defenses to make decisions about when and where to bring more defenders to help on the receiver. The Broncos' only touchdown in their season-opening loss in Kansas City came when multiple defensive backs bracketed Waddle, leaving tight end Evan Engram open for a receiving score. The Broncos were able to isolate Waddle in several 1-on-1 match-ups Sunday, including the 49-yarder.

 "They're a zone coverage team by nature, [but] we caught them in some man looks," Payton said. "... [Waddle] had one of those breakout games, it was great to see. He's kind of infectious, he doesn't have bad days, he likes football, he's a real good teammate. We needed it."

 The Broncos also needed a spark in the running game on Sunday after Dobbins left in the third quarter with a left hamstring injury . Second-year running back RJ Harvey was already unavailable, also due to a hamstring injury. The Broncos struggled in the run game last season after Dobbins suffered a season-ending foot injury in Week 10, which caused Payton to search for a reserve running back with similar traits to Dobbins.

 The Broncos selected Coleman in the fourth round in April, making the instant comparison to Dobbins after the pick. The rookie became the primary ball carrier in the second half Sunday, finishing with 10 carries for 39 yards, including a 3-yard touchdown run to give the Broncos the lead with 7:21 left. It was Denver's first rushing touchdown of the season.

 

 "J.K. always preach to me, be ready for your opportunity, be ready for your moment, you never know when your number is going to be called," Coleman said. "... It felt good to be able to do that."

 Coleman's work on the Broncos' final possession was the most important takeaway. In a situation where Payton covets reliability and ball security above all else, Coleman had six carries for 33 yards, including a 12-yard run on a second-and-11 that got Denver to the Jacksonville 18-yard line. He showed veteran awareness on that run, going down in-bounds once he had the first down, allowing the Broncos to kneel out the clock. Thanks in large part to Coleman's efforts, the Broncos were able to kill the last 4:41 of the game.

 "Very proud of him, we haven't necessarily been great in the four-minute offense in the past," Broncos wide receiver Courtland Sutton said. "That was an opportunity to go showcase what we want to be as an offense. I think he handled that situation perfectly, the best you possibly can."

 That drive capped a win against the only team that beat the Broncos at home in the regular season last year. And on a Denver team that was brought back mostly intact, two new guys made the difference.

 "It's awesome to watch young dudes make plays and we get the win," Bolles said. "... There's no better formation than the victory formation."

title: Sauce Gardner's journey with Colts is stuck in a 9-game rut
summary: The Colts are off to an 0-2 start, which doesn't bode well for the front office and doesn't sit well with the players.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS --  Sauce Gardner 's New York Jets lost 66% of their games during his tenure with the club from 2022 to Week 9 of 2025. It was a cascade of misery, with New York posting the fourth-worst record (20-39) in the NFL during that period.

 It's why Gardner, a former All-Pro cornerback, was so eager to join the Indianapolis Colts when he was traded midway through last season. In a remarkable shift, he found himself playing a key role for the team with the best record in the NFL at the time (7-2).

 These days, things couldn't be more different.

 The Colts won their first game following the trade, and they haven't won since. The losing continued Sunday night with a 33-30 overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs .

 "It doesn't sit good," Gardner said. "I'd be lying if I told you it did. We've got to turn it around.

 "It's definitely something that I was excited about. Excited to win, expecting to win. When I got here, like I said, we've got the guys, we've got the players, we've got the coaches. We've just got to actually win when the clock hits zero, zero. It's definitely crazy, though."

 The Colts are on a nine-game streak that dates to a Week 12 loss to Kansas City last season, also in overtime. That was the start of a season-ending seven-game losing streak due in part to a rash of injuries.

 But now, even with quarterback Daniel Jones back from his Achilles tear, Gardner mostly healthy (he was injured off and on late last season) and veteran defensive tackle DeForest Buckner recovered from neck surgery, little has changed.

 No team has a longer current losing streak than Indianapolis (0-2).

 

 Pressure is mounting.

 "We are right there," coach Shane Steichen said. "We have to find a way to win at the end. That was one of those games. It is a freaking hard-ass league, and you have got to find a way to win these tight games."

 The backdrop behind all of this is the intense scrutiny on Steichen, general manager Chris Ballard and many of the veteran players. Extensive changes and firings are considered likely if the Colts don't show improvement in 2026. Owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon is on record saying that expectations of progress are in place during this, her second full season as the team's primary leader alongside her two sisters.

 Steichen has a 25-28 record since his hiring in 2023, and the Colts haven't made the playoffs since 2020. They haven't won the AFC South since 2014, three years before Ballard was hired.

 Now, in Year 10 under Ballard, the Colts find themselves with a defense that is off to a historically poor start. Just one team in NFL history has allowed more total yardage in Weeks 1 and 2 than the Colts' 1,023 yards. The 2016 Oakland Raiders allowed 1,035 yards. Indianapolis has allowed more than 500 yards of offense in each of its two games this season.

 All of which makes winning unlikely. Winning is a feeling the Colts haven't tasted in far too long.

 

 "I don't think we even won any preseason games," safety Cam Bynum said. "We've just got to get back to that expectation of winning and that swag we had in the first half of last season when we were rolling. That's just a mindset."

 As for Gardner, he's playing well. He battled through a rib injury Sunday, sensing the game was slipping away. He has been solid this season, targeted five times on 78 coverage snaps and allowing four catches for 57 yards. His target rate is just 6.4%, well below his career low 9.3% in 2023.

 But he has nothing to show for it. And that's tough to swallow for a guy who thought winning was in his future.

 "I was just trying to make myself stay on that field, do whatever it takes for us to win," Gardner said. "And we still came up short."

title: Questions emerge about the Jaguars' lack of pass rush
summary: After a promising opener, the Jaguars' pass-rush issues from last season re-emerged in Sunday's loss to the Broncos.
full_text:
DENVER -- The Jacksonville Jaguars didn't sack Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix  on Sunday. They hit him only three times, including just once in the fourth quarter (by edge rusher Travon Walker ).

 The lack of pressure -- especially late in the game -- was a major reason the Jaguars (1-1) blew a 10-point third-quarter lead and lost 20-13 at Empower Field at Mile High Stadium. Was it an aberration or a sign that 2026 will be a repeat of what happened in 2025?

 And more importantly, can it be fixed -- and how?

 "Hey, that's a damn good offensive line," Jaguars coach Liam Coen said of Denver's front. "I don't want to take too much away from them, but if we're going to beat a team like that, then we're going to have to create some pressure. Something that we all kind of saw Kansas City do in the game on Monday night [in Week 1 against the Broncos], and we weren't able to do that."

 

 The Jaguars sacked Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson five times and recorded eight QB hits in Week 1 . Walker and Josh Hines-Allen each had 1.5 sacks, and it was fair to begin to question whether the concern about the pass rush looking like it did in 2025 -- when the Jaguars ranked third in pressures but 27th in sacks -- was overblown. But those worries are back after Sunday's performance.

 Per ESPN Research, Nix was 16-of-18 for 205 passing yards and a touchdown when the Jaguars sent four or fewer rushers. That means he was 6-of-13 for 83 yards and an interception when the Jaguars rushed five or more.

 But it's a gamble to rely too much on blitzing to get pressure because it opens the defense up to big plays, especially if the rush doesn't even get to the quarterback. That happened several times against the Broncos, Coen said, but it's something the Jaguars might consider going forward.

 "I think they caught us in a couple blitzes that they identified pre-snap when we were going to blitz and bring more," Coen said. "They ended up flipping the protections to pick some of that stuff up. So that's something we got to look at as well in terms of when we're bringing pressure."

 Linebacker Foyesade Oluokun said the blame for the lack of pressure belongs to the entire defense, not only the pass rushers. Being better on first and second downs would have helped.

 "We've got to own our details [on] first, second down," he said. "Now you're in third-and-passing situations. Sometimes they threw the ball out quick, but if you get them third and what, 12, third-and-[long], now you're really putting your ears back. We did not do that [Sunday] because we didn't own our details all the way through the downs."

 

 Sunday's scenario was like the AFC wild-card playoff loss to the Bills in January. The Jaguars sacked Josh Allen once and hit him three times -- none of which came in the fourth quarter. Allen drove the Bills to two touchdowns to erase Jaguars' fourth-quarter leads.

 "I thought that [the Broncos] did a nice job of mixing [the pass plays]," Coen said. "Not just straight dropback, right? There were play-action, moving the launch point, boots, getting them on the move a little bit. I thought they did a nice job with that. But we didn't do enough in the rush, specifically in the second half when you needed to play."

 Finding a way to do that quickly will be a priority considering the Jaguars face Drake Maye , Joe Burrow , Jalen Hurts and C.J. Stroud the next four weeks. But Jacksonville isn't overly worried.

 "It's early in the season," nose tackle DaVon Hamilton said. "We've got a lot of ball to play."

title: Rams defeat depleted Giants 28-6 on 'Monday Night Football'
summary: L.A. exceeded expectations after its Week 1 loss, while New York saw injuries to its stars and couldn't keep up with Matthew Stafford & Co.
full_text:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- The Rams ' offense struggled to get into a rhythm during the season opener, but over the week that followed, Los Angeles wide receiver Davante Adams cautioned against overreacting to that small sample size.

 "Everybody's freaking out, which I understand," Adams said last week. "We didn't put together the greatest showing out there. But you're a fool if you think that that's what it's going to look like every single week."

 On Monday night against the  New York Giants , quarterback Matthew Stafford and Adams showed off the connection that flashed midway through last season, the wideout's first with the Rams. Adams logged eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns during  a 28-6 win in which L.A. was without wide receiver Puka Nacua .

 Adams' performance sparked a return to the offense the Rams were expecting going into the season. It was Adams' 29th career game with multiple receiving touchdowns, tied for fourth most in NFL history.

 Adams' 195 yards were the most receiving yards by any player in a game so far this season, and without Nacua, second-year tight end Terrance Ferguson was the Rams' second-leading receiver. Ferguson tallied six catches for 54 yards and a touchdown. 

 Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

 

 

 

 Los Angeles Rams  (1-1) 
 What to make of the QB performance: Stafford, who had a passer rating of 61.2 in the Game 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , registered a passer rating of 131.3 on Monday night by completing 22 of 31 passes for 327 yards and four touchdowns with one interception. Stafford had success throwing 10 or more yards downfield, something he struggled with against the Niners. After going 3-for-10 for 74 yards with one interception on those passes in the opener, Stafford went 9-for-13 for 219 yards and two touchdowns with one pick in Week 2.

 

 Trend to watch: What will Aaron Donald 's workload look like going forward? On Monday night, he played 32 defensive snaps (58.2%). He was credited with three tackles, one run stuff and no quarterback pressures. It was the defensive tackle's first game in 981 days, as he initially retired following the 2023 season. 

 Stat to know: Adams' first-quarter touchdown was his first with the Rams that came on a pass not thrown into the end zone, according to ESPN Research. Each of Adams' 15 receiving scores last season (14 in the regular season, one in the playoffs) was thrown into the end zone. -- Sarah Barshop 

 Next game:  Sunday at Denver Broncos , 8:20 p.m. ET 

 

 

 

 New York Giants (1-1) 
 The Giants might have dodged disaster with injuries to star quarterback Jaxson Dart and wide receiver Malik Nabers . They still couldn't avoid a reality check in the 22-point defeat at Sofi Stadium.

 Their secondary couldn't hold up against Davante Adams (eight catches on 10 targets for 195 yards and a pair of TDs), and their offense didn't look the same without Dart.

 

 Dart left after taking a hit to his left knee on the opening drive.  While he didn't return to the game, he did appear on the sidelines in street clothes. Dart wanted to get back into the game but the Giants thought better of it, according to sources.

 Nabers also had an injury scare in the first half when he hurt his shoulder. He later returned, but the Giants managed just  182 yards of offense  once backup Jameis Winston entered, and they didn't look anything like the team that dismantled the Cowboys' defense in Week 1.

 What to make of the QB performance: Winston looked shaky. He struggled with his accuracy and threw a bad interception in the red zone. It didn't help that the Rams' pressure was relentless. In the first half alone, Los Angeles had 10 pressures in 18 dropbacks. Winston finished with 111 passing yards.

 To make matters worse, left tackle Andrew Thomas and outside linebacker Brian Burns  were banged up in the fourth quarter of the blowout loss. 

 Most surprising performance: The Giants rushed for 165 yards and 4.5 yards per carry against the Cowboys. They were banking on their physical style to do the same against a Rams defense that was run over by the 49ers in the opener. It didn't turn out that way: New York rushed for just 52 yards and 2.5 yards per carry versus L.A.

 Stat to know: Seven catches on 10 targets for 143 yards and a touchdown against  Tyler Nubin , according to NFL Next Gen Stats. It was a rough game in coverage as the nearest defender for the third-year Giants safety. -- Jordan Raanan 

 Next game: Sunday vs. Tennessee Titans , 1 p.m. ET

title: Tyler Shough's late-game heroics have Saints confidence soaring
summary: The second-year quarterback has been at his best this season when the game is on the line. Can he keep it up?
full_text:
BALTIMORE -- New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough wouldn't quit.

 Shough and the Saints lined up for a potentially game-sealing touchdown against the Ravens (1-1) on fourth-and-goal in Baltimore. As Shough dove for the plane of the goal line, a defensive player swiped at his face mask and yanked his head back.

 Shough gripped the football hard as he was swallowed up in a mass of bodies, but he didn't let go.

 The officials signaled touchdown, giving the Saints (1-1) the go-ahead score and eventually a 24-17 win , their first of the season.

 "Yeah, that one hurt a little bit," Shough said later with a smile. "Yeah, I got kind of folded a couple times, but I was able to get in there. So we'd like to not make it as close. ... I was going to reach for it, but getting your head pulled off, it's tough."

 

 For Saints coach Kellen Moore, it was a moment that showed Shough is "as tough as they come."

 "He's a really special player, but his willingness to hang in there and play the really hard downs, I think the rest of the team sees that, recognizes that. There's a lot of respect for what he's doing right now," Moore said.

 It took the Saints five tries to get into the end zone after backing up from the Baltimore 2-yard line due to a penalty. But pushing through and getting the job done was a reversal of last week.

 In Week 1, the Saints came up just short of beating the Detroit Lions in overtime, losing 31-30. That result might have been acceptable for last season's Saints, who were already in a 1-7 hole by the time Shough made his first start in Week 9. Getting any momentum from their rookie second-round pick felt like a win.

 But the Saints knew they had something special in Shough going into this season, and edge rusher Chase Young said the time for accepting moral victories was over.

 But after Sunday's win, the Saints blasted music in the locker room so loudly it could be heard in the adjoining conference room. Going toe-to-toe with the Ravens proved the Saints' confidence in Shough was deserved. So now New Orleans will aim to build on that momentum heading into its first home game of the season against the  Las Vegas Raiders  on Sunday ( 4:25 p.m. ET, CBS ).

 "We can hang with anybody. Sometimes you have to learn how to win, learn how to finish. And I think we right on time," Young said. "... No more moral victories, man. We want W's, and if it come down to the wire, then we just got to tough it out. We want to win."

 It was the Saints' biggest win since Shough was named the starter. He won five games leading the team in 2025, all against teams that finished the season with a losing record.

 Since 2022, the Saints have beaten only four teams that finished the season with a winning record (the 2022 Seattle Seahawks and Philadelphia Eagles and the 2023 Indianapolis Colts and Tampa Bay Buccaneers ).

 

 Beating a Ravens team that had just put up 41 points in Week 1 seemed different, even to veterans such as wide receiver Chris Olave , who is now in his fifth season.

 "I feel like since I've been here, we haven't really beat a good team. I feel like it's been tough for us to be able to battle against good teams or great teams that make the playoffs every year," Olave said. "Baltimore ... is a contender in the AFC. So just to be able to battle, be able to show our resilience, be able to come in here and get a W was huge for us, and we got to carry it over to next week."

 The Saints have found a quarterback who not only can close out games but appears to play his best in the fourth quarter and big moments. Shough's play hasn't been without flaws, and at times it has been perplexing.

 During the early and middle parts of the two games, he has played some of his worst football, only to turn up the dial when it counted the most. According to ESPN Research, Shough's Total QBR has been a dismal 14.3 rating through three quarters of the two games (ranked 29th of 30 qualified passers), but in the fourth quarter and overtime, his 97.7 rating is second in the league.

 

 He has only 56 passing yards in the first quarter compared with 350 and three touchdowns in fourth quarters and overtime.

 But when it has counted, Shough has stepped up.

 On key third downs, he has made big plays, such as a pass to Juwan Johnson on third-and-8 that gained 24 yards. With backup tackle Asim Richards handling two blockers on his left and rookie running back CJ Donaldson picking up a rusher on his right, Shough took a hit while getting the ball to Johnson, who ran to the Baltimore 2-yard line.

 "It was a special play. Got a lot of juice and energy," Moore said, "Obviously it very much changed the entire game management moving forward after that. ... That was a huge play. Just great effort by Juwan. Give us a chance to hopefully get that touchdown."

 Shough also has converted all four fourth-down attempts this season, via two runs and two passes.

 "I love those moments just because in my head it's just another down, it's just another play." Shough said. "We've prepared for a lot of those moments. So on the outside it feels like, man, this may be the game, but it generally feels like let's just go play."

 Now, with the Raiders up next, the Saints hope Shough and the team can keep that play going through all four quarters instead of just the final frame.

 "He's just going to keep going for it. And I think that's just the way he plays," Moore said. "There's highs and lows in games. There's things that go our way, the things that don't go our way. And he just keeps going. ... I was proud of him."

title: Why there's hope Pittsburgh Steelers O-line can improve
summary: Pittsburgh's young group has struggled to find consistency, but with adjustments, there's still time to improve.
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Moments before calling for the snap at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers surveyed the defense, paused and walked a couple of yards toward his line, quickly adjusting his protections as the play clock wound down.

 Left guard Mason McCormick craned his neck back to Rodgers, engaging with the quarterback before gesturing at center Zach Frazier . McCormick then pointed to running back Rico Dowdle , directing his attention to inside linebacker Robert Spillane on the other side of the line. As he walked back to the shotgun, Rodgers crossed his arms and made a shivering motion, one of his many cues to adjust the play.

 Then, confusion led to a collision.

 Dowdle ran to his right, preparing to throw a block in the gap between right guard Spencer Anderson and right tackle Dylan Cook .

 But the pressure was coming from Rodgers' left. Completely unblocked, linebacker Christian Elliss came off the edge and smoked Rodgers, sandwiching him in the backfield with Spillane. The pair knocked the ball loose, and it bounced backward for 36 yards as both teams struggled to secure it. Finally, left tackle Troy Fautanu jumped on the ball at the Steelers' 42-yard line to bring up fourth-and-43.

 

 That was a microcosm of the Steelers' 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots .

 "It's frustrating, just all around as an offense," Fautanu said after the game. "We couldn't really get anything going, and when we did, we just couldn't convert, we just couldn't score."

 Rodgers, who took a total of four sacks Sunday, was also strip-sacked one more time in the loss. That time, defensive tackle Christian Barmore muscled through Anderson to knock the ball loose, and Elijah Ponder scooped it up for the defensive touchdown.

 "They were giving us different looks, different pressures, different stunts," Fautanu said. "Obviously, the coaches go over it during the week. We've got to be able to go out there and execute and block our men regardless of if we're one-on-one. We've just got to do a better job."

 Things won't get any easier on Sunday, when the team hosts the Cincinnati Bengals ( 1 p.m. ET, CBS ), who are tied atop the league's leaderboard with eight sacks through two weeks.

 Steelers coach Mike McCarthy on Sunday shouldered the blame, pointing to a need to refine details, improve communication and reduce volume in the game plan until his young team can get the basics down.

 "Our protections weren't clean," McCarthy said. "We had opportunities, whether it was communication and breakdowns, clearly in the first half that took away some opportunities for big plays. ... The consistency of winning in the trenches, we need to be better there. But the reality of it is the detail is not there, and that's on coaching. It starts with me."

 Though every part of the offense has been flawed through two weeks of the McCarthy era, the problems on the offensive line run deeper than fine-tuning the little things. And with a 42-year-old quarterback, establishing a strong offensive line is the foundation for a successful offense. The unit is still salvageable, but McCarthy's preseason priority of creating an interchangeable line has created significant regular-season growing pains.

 

 "In hindsight you go back and you look how many days did we line up with the same offensive line? We worked a lot of different combinations," McCarthy said Monday. "No excuses, but they need continuity. They need reps, they need consistency. So the consistency will come through the common concepts. ... Our consistency starting up front, we need to give our guys more laps, more time on task and make sure we're asking them to do things that they got plenty of reps in."

 Through two weeks, the Steelers' offensive line has a pass block win rate of 52.5%, ranked 13th in the NFL, according to ESPN Analytics and NFL Next Gen Stats. Its run block win rate, however, is just 68.4%, the second lowest in the league. The Steelers are averaging 74.5 rushing yards per game (29th) and are averaging just 0.89 rushing yards before first contact (31st).

 "Something's got to change," Fautanu said. "I don't know if it's that we're not working hard enough as an offense or we're not working hard enough as an O-line. Just not connecting well with each other."

 Though McCarthy didn't overhaul the offensive line's personnel, he did significantly rearrange the group.

 During organized team activities, the Steelers coach elected to move Fautanu and McCormick from the right side of the line to the left. The pair already had chemistry from working together throughout the 2025 season, and the move solidified the left side of the line as 2023 first-round pick Broderick Jones worked back from injury.

 

 Anderson, the team's top in-house replacement option for Isaac Seumalo , moved to right guard, while Cook, who finished the 2025 season at left tackle after Jones' injury, moved to right tackle.

 Rather than emphasizing cohesion among the presumed starting five offensive linemen -- none of whom have more than four years of NFL experience -- McCarthy played a number of line combinations this preseason.

 Prior to being traded, Jones got reps at right and left tackle. Rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor , who missed a chunk of the preseason with an injury, rotated in at right tackle when healthy. Veteran interior offensive linemen Brock Hoffman and Ryan McCollum also got a lot of reps at a number of positions throughout training camp.

 The starting O-line played 19 snaps together in each of the first two preseason games, and none of them were with the entire starting offense, as Rodgers didn't play in the preseason. Cook was the only starter to play in the third game, and even then, he started out of position at left tackle.

 Through two weeks of the regular season, Anderson and McCormick have each allowed nine pressures, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, tied for 20th most in the NFL. Fautanu has allowed eight pressures, while Dylan Cook five and center Zach Frazier four.

 Cook has also allowed two sacks, tied for third most in the NFL through two weeks, and Anderson and Fautanu have allowed one apiece.

 "We need more consistency," Steelers offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio said Monday. "I don't know if there's one particular thing to point to, just seems like it moved around a little bit, but I think communication's got to be better and just consistency of what we're trying to get done."

 

 There are, however, a couple of things that could improve the unit. Not only will more time together help the group work through some of the communication kinks, but intentionally changing how they practice -- with more reps together and a lower volume of plays -- should also help.

 "Certainly the reps, the looks, the guys starting to settle in," Angelichio said. "As we go into the third week of the season, I think that stuff should start to play itself out certainly in the next couple of weeks, and that's what we're hoping for."

 McCarthy could also opt to replace Cook with Iheanachor. The first-round pick missed two preseason games, but he showed promise once he returned and made his debut in the third game. And when Fautanu missed one snap with an ankle injury against the Atlanta Falcons , the Steelers slid Cook to left tackle, and Iheanachor made a brief appearance at right tackle.

 "Max has taken a step each and every week," McCarthy said. "I thought he had a really good day Thursday in the padded work, the individual work. He's definitely making big steps. So it's getting better."

 Though he's a more raw prospect with just five years of organized football under his belt, Iheanachor earned rave reviews from coaches and teammates throughout the preseason. McCarthy could also consider replacing Anderson with Hoffman. The Steelers drafted guard Gennings Dunker in the third round earlier this year, but he has been inactive each of the first two weeks.
